### Sat 14 Nov 17:46:52 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

The level generator's first maps exist, the art thread's six prop lanes are logged, and I've started moving compile work off c4, which is at 0.7 GB free memory.

## Generator maps for you to look at

[maps.html](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/gen1/maps.html>) shows 72 generated rooms with no code door in them. I checked the file exists and holds 72 maps, but I have not judged the layouts myself. Its prop slots are still being added.

How it builds a room, from its [DESIGN.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/gen1/DESIGN.md>):

- **Modules in a row:** a room is a start, a row of modules and a gate. Each module is one idea, such as a blade tunnel, a timed door, a platform over a pit, a crate bridge, a fire strip, a climb or a fight floor.
- **Seed:** it picks the modules, their order and numbers, the room width and whether the room is mirrored.
- **Teaching:** each idea first appears alone in a lesson room, then under pressure, then combined with others.
- **Alternation:** odd depths are puzzle rooms and even depths are fights. Every tenth is a finale.
- **Fairness:** a checker refuses any room where a jump is too tight, a timing is frame-perfect, or running out of charges strands you.

Two things I'd like your reaction to on the page:

1. Rooms are straight strips from start to gate. If that reads as corridors, say so now, before the port.
2. Puzzle and fight rooms alternate strictly. Mixing them means allowing a refill pad next to enemies, which the game forbids today.

## Art thread

It started six lanes: three prop sets, the hall kit, a Megascans and CC0 list for you, and first-person animation research. The first batch (director's chairs) is due in about two hours.

One decision is yours. Green is the "way on" signal in the game, and you asked for green screens. My pick is blue screens inside rooms and green ones only out in the hall, beyond the play space.

[pc-b] passed every farm check: build, 112 tests, both packages, and the scripted run with the same result line as c4. A nine-file rebuild takes 56 s there against 137 s on c4. I told the farm lane to publish the [pc-b] instructions first, and told feel5 and vfx1 to build there once they exist.

13	- Phone on a tripod (or wedged on books). Nothing moves the camera. No zoom.
14	- Landscape, 1080p, **120 fps** if the phone has it at 1080p, else 60. The snap shuts in about 40 ms, which is 5 frames
15	  at 120 and only 2 at 60.
16	- Lock focus and exposure (tap and hold on the board). Bright room or a lamp on the board: high frame rates blur in
17	  dim light.
18	- Plain background in a colour the board is not (a dark wall if the board is light). No other moving things.
19	- Three bright tape dots on the board: the tip of the arm, the far top corner of the slate, the near bottom corner.
20	- Measure the slate's width and say it in the first take ("board 28 cm").
21	
22	Two angles, filmed one after the other
23	- **Eye angle:** tripod just behind your right shoulder at eye height, pointing where you look. This is the game's view.
24	- **Side angle:** 1.5 to 2 m to your left, at board height, looking along the hinge so the arm opens as a clear angle.
25	
26	Hold the board at arm's length as you would in the game, in your left hand. Each take: 2 s still, the move, 2 s still.
27	
28	| Take | Move |
29	| --- | --- |
30	| 1 | Snap shut (freeze) |
31	| 2 | Open it again (time resumes) |
32	| 3 | A weak half snap (no charges left) |
33	| 4 | Hold still 10 s, breathing normally |
34	| 5 | Bring the board up into view from your side |
35	| 6 | Lower it out of view |
36	
37	Three tries of each from each angle. About 2 minutes in all.
38	
39	Files
40	- Copy the originals by cable (not through a chat app, it shrinks them) to `D:\UE\ref\clap\`, named `eye_t1_a.mp4`,
41	  `side_t1_a.mp4` and so on, then tell the jam thread.
42	- They show you and your room, so they stay out of the repos and the dev log.
43	
44	Not needed: Rokoko. It needs your whole body in frame, does not track fingers or the board, and the arm above the
45	wrist is off screen in the game.
46
```

# Build farm for SUPERCUT

Lane farm1, 14 Nov 2026. Other PCs build, test, package and run SUPERCUT for lanes on c4. Git, agents and the
source of truth stay on c4. A farm PC holds a plain copy of a project folder (a "mirror"), never a git repo.
Nothing is ever pushed with git.

## Which PCs are ready

| PC | Root | Ready | Build | Tests | Package | Scripted run | Lanes at once |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[pc-b]` | `C:\UE` | **yes** (17:33) | yes | yes | Development and Shipping | yes, offscreen | 2 (builds queue, see below) |

The root table also sits at the top of `farm/farm.sh` (`root_of`). On every PC: engine in `<root>\UE_5.9`, mirrors in
`<root>\Farm\<name>`, packages in `<root>\Farm\_builds\<name>`, step logs in `<root>\Farm\_out\<name>\<step>`, farm
scripts in `<root>\Farm\_farm`.

## Five-minute start (from c4, Git Bash)

Pick a name for your lane (letters, digits, no spaces): use your lane name, for example `vfx1`. Never use another
lane's name and never `proof` (the farm's own check).

```bash
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
LOGS=/d/UE/wt/vfx1_farmlogs          # any folder on c4 outside the worktree; each step writes LOGS/<step>/

"$F" mirror [pc-b] vfx1 /d/UE/wt/vfx1                 # 2. copy your worktree (changed files only)
"$F" build  [pc-b] vfx1 "$LOGS" -Jobs 8               # 3. SupercutEditor, Development

grep "RUN wrapped" "$LOGS/run/run.log"                # 7. compare with the reference line

[SUPERCUT fabdl1](t3-thread://v2/12df28c1-1bab-4242-8860-5f9e21a1f8bf/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A05344926-1268-4f01-b43e-b984a609df3e%3Adelegate-task%3A4da6d2fc-449d-43ff-8a70-3929f8448a38) is Opus on the [account-B] account, driving your Firefox for the 30 Megascans items.

- **Where it works:** in a new Firefox window of its own, in the background. It does not touch your open tabs.
- **What it accepts:** the licence dialogs Fab shows on the way to a free download, as you said.
- **Where it stops:** on a sign-in page, a CAPTCHA, a payment step or any price above zero. It never types a password or code.
- **Where files go:** `D:\UE\megascans_dl\`, with a ledger of each file.

If it cannot do a step in the background, it will bring Firefox forward for that one step, and only when no Supercut game is running. So if you see Firefox pop up between play sessions, that is why.

## Prop import

setC delivered nine props: two road cases, a pallet stack, plastic crates, a steel drum, a pallet and three cable pieces. [SUPERCUT props1](t3-thread://v2/12df28c1-1bab-4242-8860-5f9e21a1f8bf/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A05344926-1268-4f01-b43e-b984a609df3e%3Adelegate-task%3Ae5ff599d-edca-4124-bf0a-4127b2a2c287) is importing them. Its job:

- a prop catalogue the level generator picks from by seed;
- cover-sized props that block the player, shots and enemies like today's boxes;
- the old props in the eight hand-made rooms swapped for the new ones;
- the revolver for the enemies;
- a show room you can walk through to see every prop.

Textures come in at 1024 unless you stand next to the prop. The package is about 232 MB now and the zip limit is 1 GB, so sixty props at full size would not fit.

## Usage is now the limit

The main account's weekly use went from 63% to 73% in 90 minutes, with three Fable sessions on it. The other two accounts are at 71% and 75% and moved one point each. At this rate the main account reaches 95% around 21:30 tonight, and this thread runs on it.

What I've changed: new lanes are Opus on the other two accounts, and the viewmodel animation lane and the generator port will be Opus instead of Fable. If you have another account, or want me to drop something to save usage, say so.

**What I hit along the way:**
- **Runs are offscreen.** A game started over ssh can't open a window. With `-RenderOffscreen` it runs with nothing on the person's screen, and the pictures are real frames. Offscreen frame rates are not what a player sees.
- **pc2's package needed a newer VC++ runtime.** The packaging step failed until I installed the engine's own `vc_redist.x64.exe` silently. I did the same on pc4, which had no runtime at all.
- **pc4 is blocked by Smart App Control.** The editor can't load our game DLL (error 4551), so tests, packaging and the game can't run there. I changed nothing.
- **One game per PC at a time.** Two games started together from one package folder on [pc-b]: one crashed at start, the other finished.
- **pc2 needs a longer timeout.** Its run takes about 8 minutes, so lanes add `-TimeoutSeconds 900`.
- **My mistake:** I ran that two-game test while [pc-b] was at 96 to 100% CPU from the two lanes' builds. The load check showed it and I went ahead anyway.

**Commands a lane uses** (FARM.md has the full list):
```bash

"$F" mirror [pc-b] vfx1 /d/UE/wt/vfx1
"$F" build [pc-b] vfx1 "$LOGS" -Jobs 8

```
`{P}` is the lane's copy of the project on that PC and `{B}` its package folder. Logs and pictures come back to `$LOGS/<step>/`, with the PC's user and computer names masked. Git stays on c4. Two lanes' builds on one PC wait for each other, because the engine allows one build at a time. There are no Shipping runs on farm PCs, because they write into the person's own user folder.

The game repo was not edited. The farm makes a temporary copy of each Tools script on the farm PC with its own paths filled in. The handoff has an optional small change to `run_demo.ps1` that would make the offscreen switch less fragile; nothing needs it now.

25 tools/leak_scan.py
"""Fail if a tracked file holds a private word, an email or an IP address. Run before every commit."""
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
words = list(json.loads((ROOT / "tools" / "redact.local.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["replace"])
files = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", "-co", "--exclude-standard"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.split("\n")
bad = 0
unread = 0
for name in filter(None, files):
    if Path(name).suffix.lower() in (".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif", ".mp4", ".webm"):
        unread += 1  # a picture or video: text rules cannot check it, a person or agent looks at each one
        continue
    text = (ROOT / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    hits = sum(len(re.findall(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])" + re.escape(w) + r"(?![A-Za-z0-9])", text)) for w in words)
    hits += len(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}", text))
    hits += len(re.findall(r"(?<![\d.])(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}(?![\d.])", text))
    if hits:
        print(f"{name}: {hits} private item(s)")
        bad += hits
print("leak scan:", "FAILED" if bad else "clean", f"({unread} picture or video file(s) not text-scanned)" if unread else "")
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

Props you can shoot through, and where the code lanes stand\n\n**Second prop batch.** The art thread's lane `setB` delivered seven props: three director's chairs, a cine camera\non a tripod, a grip cart and two wooden step ladders. Its note on the chairs and ladders: they are frames, so they\nshould stop a walking body but not a line of sight.\n\nThat needed a rule the prop catalogue did not have. A prop was either a full box (stops the player, enemies, shots\nand sight, so it is cover) or decoration (stops nothing). A full box round a ladder would stop bullets in thin\nair, and counting a chair as cover would lie to the player about where they are safe. So the catalogue line gets a\nthird state, `open=1`: the prop stops walking bodies only. Shots and enemy sight pass through, it never fills a\ncover slot, and nothing leaves a mark on its box. `[taste: owner review]`\n\nBoth lanes that read the catalogue were told in the same minute: the import lane (sets `open=1` from the prop's\nnotes and for chairs and ladders, with a test that a shot and an enemy's sight check pass through a prop that\nstops a walking body) and the generator lane (open props are obstacles when it checks that a room can be crossed,\nand are never placed where its rules ask for cover).\n\n**Code lanes, read from their commits at 18:43.**\n\n- `feel4` (main copy): two more commits. The footstep pace now follows a tuning line, and a chain of kills raises\n  the kill sound a semitone per kill. ### Sat 14 Nov 18:49:58 · Helper agent's report

Delegated task node:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A05344926-1268-4f01-b43e-b984a609df3e%3Adelegate-task%3Ab5fb6d24-a7ae-4b9d-a14c-f31b2dfed163 (SUPERCUT sfx1: real CC0 sounds to replace the code-made ones) [completed]:
38 of the 48 sounds now have a recorded pick, covering 55 of the 65 files. The other 10 keep their current code-made sound. Every pick is marked [taste: owner review], and nobody has listened to them yet, since this PC plays no sound. Everything is in the lane folder. I did not touch the game.

Open [listen.html](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/sfx1/listen.html>) in a browser from the lane folder. It has one row per sound: the current sound first, then 2 or 3 candidates. All 248 players point at files that exist.

**What I checked**
- **The project's own rules.** I put the picks into a copy of `Audio/wav` and ran the project's `measure.py` on it. All the hard rules pass: format, true peak, DC, starting and ending in silence, loop seams, family loudness, variants not too alike, and clap and revolver being the loudest two.
- **What fails.** 71 checks fail, all of them rules written for code-made sound: centroid, attack, decay time, flatness and the 15% above 6 kHz limit. Real recordings break these by nature.
- **The hearing tool.** Most current sounds came out closest to "filtered white noise" or "a synthesized beep" rather than their own description. I scored every candidate against its description and moved 8 picks where the score clearly favoured another clean take.

**The ten that matter most**

| # | sound | pick |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | rev_shot | Real .38 snub-nose shots with a low .357 layer. It is the only candidate that reaches the game's level, so GunShotVolume stays 1.0. |
| 2 | enemy_hit | Real wood knock with a punch under it |
| 3 | kill_knock | Heavy wood plus a low punch |
| 4 | clap_snap | Three real slate claps plus a little plank |
| 5 | rev_reload | Real gun mechanics placed on the game's timing; the cylinder closes at 0.86 s |
| 6 | step | Four real steps on a wooden floor. The Kenney set fails the "variants too alike" rule (0.98). |
| 7 | enemy_burst | A hit, then real boards clattering down |
| 8 | grunt_shot | Real paintball pop with the current glow under it |
| 9 | marksman_shot | Real rifle crack (Savage .300 Blackout) |
| 10 | door_unlock | A real bolt thrown in a lock |

**What needs you**
- **Import.** Copy the picked files over the same names in `Audio/wav`, then re-run `Tools/make_sounds.py`. Do not run `build_all.py` afterwards: it deletes every `sc_*.wav` and renders them all again from code. The change to `build_all.py` and `measure.py` that stops this is described in [IMPORT.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/sfx1/IMPORT.md>) section 3. No change to `SupercutAudio.cpp` is needed.
- **Credits.** The SUBMISSION.md lines are in IMPORT.md section 4: 34 source items, mostly BigSoundBank, plus Kenney, the Free Firearm Sound Library and rubberduck.
- **Freesound.** It needs an account, so I only listed 15 CC0 items for you to fetch (IMPORT.md section 5). The useful ones are revolver shots, clapperboards, projector reel runouts and glass shimmers.
- **To generate.** These still have no good recording: glyph_reveal, a film-burn layer for death, a sizzle layer for lava_loop, and enemy_shot_fly. Optional: marksman_aim and blade_loop, whose current sounds already fit. Each has a one-line description in IMPORT.md section 6.

**What I'm unsure about**
- **The hearing score is weak on hits under a second.** For example, rev_shot and kill_knock score near zero whichever take I pick. Your ears decide those.
- **Freeze sounds.** freeze_in, freeze_out and death use real projectors slowed down or sped up in code. That processing may sound artificial.
- **Clipped gun recordings.** The firearm library is hard-clipped in the crack. If you pick revolver take a or c instead of b, they are 3.4 to 3.8 dB too quiet; set GunShotVolume to about 1.5.
- **Phone recordings.** crate_thud and button_press are phone recordings from rubberduck; crate_thud has a noise floor of -60 dB. crate_thud also has two hits 90 ms apart.
- **Git.** The `.ogg` and `.flac` downloads in `src/` are not ignored by git, so they will show up in git status. I made no commit.

The audit table is in [AUDIT.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/sfx1/AUDIT.md>). How to re-run everything is in [HANDOFF.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/sfx1/HANDOFF.md>), and the timeline is in [LOG.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/sfx1/LOG.md>).

## What's in the video
The revolver is in view at 4:31 to 5:09, 5:16 to 5:43, 7:07 to 8:46, 8:51 to 9:49 and 14:30 to 15:30.

| Action | Clean examples |
| --- | --- |
| Single shot | 3, tracked |
| Shots in a row | 3 runs, 250 to 580 ms apart |
| Reload | 3 from empty, 6 from part full |
| Draw | 1 |
| Left hand leaves for a gadget | 3: a quick throw, a held ability, and its throw |
| Aim down sights | 1 |
| Inspect | 2 |
| Sprint, jump, swap | none clean |

## The ten numbers that differ most from the plan
1. **Reload length:** 2.22 s in the reference, 1.0 s in the plan. I scaled the beats into 1.0 s and left the length alone.
2. **Gun during the reload:** the reference never hides it, and the left hand loads it. The plan hides it from 0.28 to 0.62 s.
3. **Recoil size:** the gun top jumps 21.6% of screen height, and by eye the barrel tips 40 to 60 deg. The plan's kick is about 7.8%. I suggest about 13% (pitch 20, up 2.5 cm), since SUPERCUT fires three times as often.
4. **View kick:** the reference is 3.5 deg, which is 1.8 deg on SUPERCUT's screen. The plan has 0.8. I suggest 1.5 deg with a 60 ms rise.
5. **Recoil settle:** the reference reaches home at 217 to 300 ms and is done at 600 ms. The plan is home at 116 ms and done at 210 ms. I suggest spring w 18, z 0.43.
6. **Recoil dip below level:** 22% in the reference, 12% in the plan.
7. **Reload close:** the reference shows a cylinder spin with 4 clicks 50 ms apart. The plan spins it unseen.
8. **Recoil direction:** the reference goes right and clockwise on every shot. The plan picks a random side.
9. **Draw:** 0.75 s from below the centre in the reference. The plan's draw takes 0.35 s, and its start offset is +4 to the side where the reference implies -4. I'd keep 0.35 s and only move the start (one example).
10. **Recoil attack:** the reference peaks at 50 ms with 75% of the rise in the first frame. The plan's attack is 25 ms. I suggest 35 ms.

## The hand-off in five lines
1. At rest the left hand is out of view, and the revolver is held in one hand.
2. The hand comes up from below in 3 frames (50 ms), 75% of the way on the first frame.
3. The action happens 150 ms after the hand first shows. The hand then holds the pose for 170 to 400 ms.
4. It leaves down and to the left in 200 to 250 ms, speeding up as it goes.
5. The gun keeps aiming. For a quick action it doesn't move. For a held one it steps 3.6% right and 8.5% down over 250 ms, starting one frame before the hand shows.

## The two clapperboard versions
- **(a) Board stays in view, as today.** The arm snaps by frame 2 (33 ms), with 75% of the kick on frame 1. The board holds at the peak to 200 ms, then settles on the gun's spring and is close to home by 490 ms. A refused clap half-closes the arm, jams it, bounces it open and shakes the board with the HUD icons for 0.3 s. On resume the arm opens in 120 ms with a 5% overshoot and settles by 300 ms. This uses existing parts only and takes 1 to 2 h.
- **(b) Board comes up only for the clap.** The board rises from below in 2 frames, the arm snaps, and the board stays up through the freeze. On resume it drops out down and to the left. With the left hand resting out of view, as in the reference, this takes about 4 to 5 h. With it resting on the revolver, as you described, it takes about 8 to 10 h, because it also needs a posed left hand with fingers and a grip hand-off.
- In both forms of (b), the charge count moves to the HUD icons and the RIGHT MOUSE prompt moves to the HUD. The board waits attached to the camera, below the frame.

**With a day and a half left, I'd build (a).** The 45 ms freeze rule squeezes (b)'s rise into a 2-frame pop, so most of what makes the reference's hand-off read is lost before the snap anyway. Also, the reference never holds the revolver with two hands. If the board must go out of view, the hand-out-of-view form of (b) costs about half as much as the hand-on-gun form.

## What I'm unsure about
- **Converting to SUPERCUT's screen:** the screen-share numbers for SUPERCUT are estimated from the gun's position in code, give or take 20%. A frame dump of the game after a change is the real check.
- **Field of view:** I measured it from the compass at about 100 deg vertical, give or take 7%. Every conversion to degrees carries that error.
- **Look lag and draw:** one example each.
- **Hammer, trigger and cylinder during a shot:** I can't read them, because the gun is seen from behind.
- **Hand-off timings:** counted by eye frame by frame. The tracker loses the gun once the hand overlaps it.
- **Sound times:** these come from audio track 0 of the video, minus a 45 ms recorder delay. The 16 kHz wav that came with the brief has no gunshots.
- **(b) costs:** guesses. They depend on how quickly a usable left-hand pose comes out of Blender.

# animref1: the reference against anim1's plan

Each number in `lanes/anim1/plan.md` part 2 beside what the reference video shows (`REFERENCE.md`), and what I
would do. Fixed and untouched: one shot every 0.18 s, reload 1.0 s, a clap freezes the scene within 45 ms.

How screen sizes were compared: the reference camera has f = 610 px at 1440 high (vertical view about 100 deg);
SUPERCUT has f = 1172 px (horizontal 95, vertical 63). "% H" is a share of the screen height. Plan numbers in cm and
degrees were turned into % H at SUPERCUT's camera by placing the muzzle at GunHome + MuzzleOffset (about 60 cm
ahead, 13 cm below the eye) and moving it by the plan's offsets: **estimated**, the kick pivot and the mesh scale make
it +/- 20%. Spring numbers come from `scripts/spring.py` (1 kHz steps of the plan's own spring).

Sure-ness: **T** tracked frame by frame, **E** counted by eye, **S** estimated. **1x** = one example only.

# animref1: clapperboard choreography for SUPERCUT

Built on the reference's left-hand gadget moves (`REFERENCE.md` section 6). Times are from the input frame, in ms
and in 60 fps frames (F). The owner's real-clapperboard footage is fitted into these beats: his clip gives the
shape inside each beat (the board's path, the arm's angle curve), these numbers give where each beat starts and
ends. Picture in `plots/clap_beats.png`.

## What the reference gives us

1. The left hand is **not on the gun** at rest; it is out of view below the bottom edge.
2. It enters from below and reaches its working spot in **3 frames (50 ms)**, 75% of the way in the first frame.
3. The action point (release) comes **150 ms** after the hand first shows (quick throw); a held action keeps the
   hand up with a slow bob, about once a second.
4. A follow-through hold in the action pose: **170 ms** (quick) to **400 ms** (throw).
5. Exit: down and to the left, **200 to 250 ms**, speeding up as it goes.
6. The gun keeps aiming. For a quick action it does not move; for a held one it steps right 3.6% H and down 8.5% H
   in 250 ms (ease-out), starting about **1 frame before** the hand shows.

SUPERCUT's rule changes one thing: a clap must freeze the scene within 45 ms (2.7 frames). The reference's 150 ms
from hand-in to release cannot be kept; everything before the snap is squeezed into 2 frames, and the reference's
timing is used for what comes after.

cd "D:/UE/ref/ui/work" && python -I - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, wave
def rd(p):
    w=wave.open(p); a=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float32)/32768; return a
a=rd("track0_16k.wav"); b=rd("track2_16k.wav"); n=min(len(a),len(b)); a=a[:n]; b=b[:n]
# lag by cross-correlation on a loud 20 s window
e=np.convolve(b**2,np.ones(16000),'same'); c=int(np.argmax(e)); s=max(0,c-160000); x=a[s:s+320000]; y=b[s:s+320000]
best=max(range(-400,401), key=lambda L: float(np.dot(x[400:-400], np.roll(y,L)[400:-400])))
print("lag samples", best, "corr", float(np.corrcoef(x[400:-400], np.roll(y,best)[400:-400])[0,1]))
db=lambda v: 10*np.log10(np.mean(v**2)+1e-12)
# per-10s: level of mix, game, and least-squares residual after best gain
res=[]
for i in range(0,n-160000,160000):
    xa=a[i:i+160000]; yb=np.roll(b,best)[i:i+160000]
    g=float(np.dot(xa,yb)/(np.dot(yb,yb)+1e-12)); r=xa-g*yb
    res.append((i/16000, db(xa), db(yb), g, db(r)))
import statistics
print("windows",len(res))
print("median gain", statistics.median(r[3] for r in res), "median residual dB", statistics.median(r[4] for r in res), "median mix dB", statistics.median(r[1] for r in res))
loud=[r for r in res if r[4] > r[1]-6]
print("windows where residual within 6 dB of mix:", len(loud))
for r in res[::9]: print("t=%4.0fs mix %.1f game %.1f gain %.2f residual %.1f"%r)
EOF

import numpy as np, wave
def rd(p):
    w=wave.open(p); return np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float32)/32768
a=rd("track0_16k.wav"); b=rd("track2_16k.wav"); n=min(len(a),len(b)); a=a[:n]; b=b[:n]
db=lambda v: 10*np.log10(np.mean(v**2)+1e-12)
W=160000; k=n//W
lev=[db(b[i*W:(i+1)*W]) for i in range(k)]; c=int(np.argmax(lev)); x=a[c*W:(c+1)*W]; y=b[c*W:(c+1)*W]
f=np.fft.rfft(x)*np.conj(np.fft.rfft(y)); cc=np.fft.irfft(f); L=int(np.argmax(cc)); L = L-W if L>W//2 else L
print("lag samples",L,"corr at lag %.3f"%(cc.max()/np.sqrt(np.dot(x,x)*np.dot(y,y))))
bs=np.roll(b,L); rows=[]
for i in range(k):
    xa=a[i*W:(i+1)*W]; yb=bs[i*W:(i+1)*W]; g=float(np.dot(xa,yb)/(np.dot(yb,yb)+1e-12)); r=xa-g*yb
    rows.append((i*10,db(xa),db(yb),g,db(r)))
m=np.median
print("windows",k,"median gain %.2f median mix %.1f game %.1f residual %.1f"%(m([r[3] for r in rows]),m([r[1] for r in rows]),m([r[2] for r in rows]),m([r[4] for r in rows])))
print("windows where the residual is within 6 dB of the mix:",sum(1 for r in rows if r[4]>r[1]-6))
for r in rows[::8]: print("t=%4ds mix %.1f game %.1f gain %.2f residual %.1f"%r)
EOF

import numpy as np, wave
def rd(p):
    w=wave.open(p); return np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float32)/32768
a=rd("track0_16k.wav"); b=rd("track2_16k.wav"); n=min(len(a),len(b)); r=a[:n]-b[:n]
db=lambda v: 10*np.log10(np.mean(v**2)+1e-12)
W=16000*5; out=[]
for i in range(n//W):
    out.append("%d:%02d=%d"%(i*5//60,i*5%60,round(db(r[i*W:(i+1)*W]))))
print(" ".join(out))
# spectrum of the residual in its loud parts: speech sits 100-4000 Hz with syllable-rate modulation 3-8 Hz
loud=np.concatenate([r[i*W:(i+1)*W] for i in range(n//W) if db(r[i*W:(i+1)*W])>-45])
env=np.abs(loud); e=env[:len(env)//160*160].reshape(-1,160).mean(1)  # 100 Hz envelope
E=np.abs(np.fft.rfft(e-e.mean()))**2; fr=np.fft.rfftfreq(len(e),0.01)
band=lambda lo,hi: E[(fr>=lo)&(fr<hi)].sum()
print("loud seconds",len(loud)/16000,"envelope energy share 2-8 Hz: %.2f"%(band(2,8)/band(0.2,50)))
S=np.abs(np.fft.rfft(loud[:16000*60]))**2; f=np.fft.rfftfreq(16000*60,1/16000)
sb=lambda lo,hi: S[(f>=lo)&(f<hi)].sum()/S.sum()
print("spectrum share <100 Hz %.2f, 100-1000 %.2f, 1000-4000 %.2f, >4000 %.2f"%(sb(0,100),sb(100,1000),sb(1000,4000),sb(4000,8000)))
EOF

### Sat 14 Nov 19:20:34 · Helper agent's report

Delegated task node:delegated-task:provider-continuation%3Amessage%3Athread%3Athread%253Adelegated-task%253Acommand%25253Amcp%25253A05344926-1268-4f01-b43e-b984a609df3e%25253Adelegate-task%25253A4baf7b3a-6059-4ebe-b85b-4e7dbc1ac416%3Aordinal%3A1%3Af4d7b985-2f25-4297-89ac-3289e6413612 (SUPERCUT gen1: procedural level generator prototype) [completed]:
The room generator works in Python and its rooms load and play in the build copy; nothing is ported into the game yet. Rooms with props have not been loaded in any game, because the build has no prop catalogue.

## What it makes
- **Rooms:** a room comes from `(seed, depth)` alone, byte for byte the same on every run. It is a row of modules between a start and a gate, inside 400 cm outer walls, open at the top.
- **Run shape:** odd depths are puzzle rooms and even depths are fights. Depths 1 to 7 teach one thing each, stacking starts at 8 and 9, finales come every 10th depth, and all nine lessons are done by depth 15.
- **Modules:** 16, all from today's pieces (blade tunnel, timed door, dolly pit, ferry, crate bridge, bar bridge, four fire modules, climb, three enemy lessons, arena, pad bay). The code door is gone.
- **Props:** picked by category, class and size from a 31-prop stand-in catalogue made from the art lanes' files.

## Proof numbers
- **Fairness:** 15,000 rooms (seeds 1 to 1,000 at 15 depths) with props and the same 15,000 without. In both, 14,999 are fair at the first attempt, one is re-rolled once, and none gave up.
- **The one refusal:** seed 517, depth 14, "the Marksman sees the player at the start". The generator was wrong and the checker was right. No refusal came from a checker mistake.
- **Checker self-test:** 49 rooms, 0 wrong. 47 are broken on purpose and get the refusal named for them; 2 are fair on purpose and pass.
- **Variety:** from depth 8, 2,000 seeds give 1,998 to 2,000 different layouts. Lesson rooms give 323 to 1,080, by design.
- **In the game** (build copy packaged between `584e9b1` and `683bff6`, rooms without props):
  - 70 of 70 rooms load with no loader error or warning.
  - 9 rooms were played to the gate by script, each with the `END reached` line.
  - The three play runs built 12 of 12 rooms each.
- **Test vectors:** 51 `(seed, depth)` pairs with and without props, identical on a second write.

## Answers the jam thread asked for
- **400 cm walls:** nothing changed in any check or route. The same nine play scripts pass. The height is one value, `wall_height` in `gen/data/plan.json`.
- **The 101 cm case:** not a step. The checker's jump up stays 100 cm, a blocking prop 101 to 110 cm high is never placed, and the checker refuses a room that has one. Today that rules out `road_case_open`.
- **Cover by height:** an apple box gives way only to a full prop 75 to 125 cm high, which is low cover. A flat gives way only to a full prop at least 150 cm high and 60 percent as long. None of the 31 props is that, so every flat stays a flat.
- **Climbing out:** the checker refuses any room where a player can stand within 200 cm of a wall top.
- **`open`:** required on every catalogue line. Open props stop walking only and are never cover.

## The port
The estimates are mine and nobody has started it.

| Plan | What it is | Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Bake | Python-made room and run files as loose files; the game picks a run by seed | 3 to 4 hours |
| B1. Port the generator | Rooms built in the game; the checker's verdicts ship as a table | 10 to 14 hours |
| B2. Port the checker too | Any seed is fair with no table | 12 to 16 hours more |

With four hours, do plan A and stop. It cuts endless depth and nothing else a jam player would notice. The two movement pieces I would add for the least code are a bridge solid only in a freeze, and a launch ram.

## The owner's open choices `[taste: owner review]`
1. Puzzle on odd depths and fight on even, always.
2. One Marksman a room at every depth.
3. The clap lesson is always the blade tunnel; the bar lesson can ask for a wait of up to 8.3 s.
4. Pad bays are skipped half the time from depth 9.
5. Outer walls at 400 cm.
6. One prop stands in for a whole 160 or 240 cm apple box, so that cover gets smaller.
7. Flats are never swapped with today's catalogue.
8. Blocking props in wall slots are unplanned extra cover in a fight.
9. Lava landings are 4 m.
10. A 101 to 110 cm prop is never placed.
11. The bar on end reads as a wall, and a frozen platform level with the bank reads as floor.
12. Gear on the blade tunnel's block stands up to 652 cm and shows above the walls.
13. In the port: whether a generated run ends or goes on for ever, and what a Shipping build does with a catalogue that does not match its rooms.

## What I am unsure about
- **Fast platform:** the dolly pit's lesson rests on a 1,500 cm/s platform being too fast to board. That is the checker's model and was not tried in the game.
- **Jumps not scripted:** the jump onto a 100 cm box, the 200 cm climb with a box, and the pit stairs. The numbers are the game's own.
- **Jumps from props:** a jump from 100 cm up carries about 4.8 m by my working, not measured. The checker does not model it, so a prop near lava or a pit could give a shortcut.
- **Build age:** the game repo was at `6359fc6` when I last looked, newer than the build copy.
- **Depth:** nothing was run past depth 30 except one test vector at 40.

Two `Supercut` processes are running now. I did not start them and left them alone.

## The short answer

There are three ways in, each a strict part of the next. Pick by the hours you have.

| Plan | What goes in the game | New C++ | My estimate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. Bake | Room and run files made by the Python, as loose files. The game picks a run file by seed. | About 150 lines, plus the prop catalogue | 3 to 4 hours |
| B1. Port the generator | Rooms built in the game from `(seed, depth)`. The checker stays in Python and its verdicts ship as a small table. | About 1,400 lines | 10 to 14 hours |
| B2. Port the checker too | Any seed is fair with no table. | About 1,800 lines more | 12 to 16 hours more |

The estimates are mine and nobody has started the port. With four hours, do plan A and stop.

Plan A costs nothing in variety for a jam: 2,000 seeds give 2,000 different runs, about 30 KB a room.

## What the generator promises

- `build_room(seed, depth, attempt, known, props)` returns the room as text in the game's room file format.
  The same arguments and the same data files give the same bytes on any machine.
- `seed` is 0 to 4294967295. `depth` is 1 for the first room of a run and has no upper limit.
  `attempt` is 0 unless the checker refused the room. `known` is a bit mask of lessons the player has already
  had (bit 0 = clap, then grunt, timed, platform, crates, fire, bar, rusher, marksman: the order of `tags` in `plan.json`).
- A room depends on nothing but those arguments. Room 9 can be built without rooms 1 to 8.
- `props=1` places props from the catalogue with `dress` lines. `props=0` writes plain boxes and no `dress` line.
  They are two different rooms with two different hashes. Today's game loads only `props=0` rooms.

Everything is whole numbers of cm. No float decides anything. No dict or set order decides anything.

## Plan A: bake

1. On the build machine: `python gen.py run SEED --out <folder> --depths 12` for each seed you ship (add `--noprops`
   until the game has the catalogue). It writes `Rooms/gen/s<seed>/dNN.txt` and `Runs/gen_s<seed>.txt` and refuses
   to write a room the checker did not pass.
2. Copy both folders into the game's `Content`. `Config/DefaultGame.ini` already stages `Rooms` and `Runs` as loose
   files, and `SupercutRoomFile::PathOf` already takes a name with folders in it (`gen/s7/d03`). I loaded 70 such
   rooms in the packaged build this way.
3. `SupercutGameMode.cpp`, `InitGame`: when the command line names no run and no room, set
   `RunName = "gen_s" + (1 + Seed % ShippedSeeds
[... 2288 more characters not shown]

With that in, the default game is a generated run, and the hand-made rooms stay only for tests. Rebuilding the generator inside the game for endless depth would take 10 hours or more, so it is out unless you want it.

Delegated task node:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A05344926-1268-4f01-b43e-b984a609df3e%3Adelegate-task%3Af71eb297-5ad1-4888-af4d-2b104683b2ad (SUPERCUT dlss1: DLSS for the NVIDIA award, feasibility and plan) [completed]:
The plan and the build brief are written. I changed nothing in the game, the engine or any farm PC.

**Can we qualify?** Yes, with DLSS Super Resolution or DLAA alone. The jam's award terms on itch.io say the entry must use "at least one of the following NVIDIA features: ... NVIDIA DLSS". Frame Generation is not needed. Two catches:
- The GPU goes to the best-ranked Render Royalty entry that also uses an NVIDIA feature. DLSS gets us in, but the visuals score decides who wins.
- Singapore is not on the award's list of excluded countries.

**Is there a plugin for 5.9?** No.
- Our engine folder has no DLSS, NGX or Streamline plugin. I checked on disk.
- It does ship Epic's own NVIDIA Reflex plugin, but Reflex is not on the award's list.
- The newest DLSS plugin is v8.9.0, built for UE 5.8.
- Good sign: I compared our 5.8.4 and 5.9 engine folders. The file that defines how an outside upscaler plugs into the engine is identical in both, and the DirectX 12 interface the plugin uses is unchanged. So the 5.8 plugin has a fair chance to build on 5.9 with small fixes. That stays unproven until a build runs.

**What the owner must do by hand:**
1. Open https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss and click "Download UE 5.8 DLSS Plugin". Expect to accept the NVIDIA RTX SDK licence (https://developer.download.nvidia.com/licenses/nvidia-rtx-sdk-license-2024.02.23.pdf). Expect a free NVIDIA developer sign-in too, since the link sits under a `/secure/` path. I did not open the link.
2. Save `2026.10.16_ue5.8_dlss4.5plugin_v8.9.0.zip` to `D:\UE\dl\dlss\`. Don't unzip it.
3. Have a person on [pc-b] read the NVIDIA driver version. Don't update the driver without deciding first.
4. Decide on the credit. The licence requires naming DLSS on splash screens and in credits. But using NVIDIA's logos needs their written approval two weeks ahead. My pick: a plain-text "NVIDIA DLSS" line, no logo.

**Hours:** about 6 to 9 agent hours for the smallest version (OFF, DLAA, QUALITY, BALANCED, PERFORMANCE). Frame Generation would add 4 to 8 hours. It can't be proven on the farm, because farm runs have no game window. And when someone ported the plugin to 5.8 before NVIDIA did, Frame Generation crashed. Reflex adds nothing to eligibility.

**Three biggest risks:**
1. The plugin won't compile on 5.9, or compiles and crashes at start.
2. It changes the game on PCs without an NVIDIA card. The c4 AMD run must print the same `RUN wrapped` line and match the old screenshots.
3. The zip goes over 1 GB. The Development package folder was already 1.08 GB uncompressed today, so the "about 250 MB" figure is out of date.

One more trap I confirmed: the game's `.gitignore` line `Binaries/` drops the plugin's NVIDIA DLLs from git without any warning. A judge build from a clean checkout would then have no DLSS. The brief has the fix.

**The sketch look:** DLSS takes TSR's place, and the sketch still runs after it at full output resolution. The existing jitter fix during the freeze should carry over. Outlines get coarser below 100% because depth and normals stay at the lower render resolution, so DLAA is the cleanest choice. The brief includes a still-frame pixel check and a 4-up screenshot for you to judge.

**Recommendation:** do the smallest version only. Start as soon as the zip is on disk. Stop and revert if it doesn't build and pass the AMD check by Sunday 11:00 SGT. Skip Frame Generation and Reflex.

**Not verified (all need the zip):**
- the plugin's folder names, dependencies, version field, function names and console variables for v8.9.0
- whether an NVIDIA sign-in or application ID is needed
- the minimum driver
- the DLL sizes
- whether the DLLs show a watermark
- how Streamline behaves on AMD
- the checkbox list on the NVIDIA form question

- **Eligibility:** DLSS Super Resolution or DLAA alone meets the award's terms. Frame Generation is not needed.

- **Cost:** 6 to 9 agent hours for OFF, DLAA, QUALITY, BALANCED and PERFORMANCE.
- **Stop rule:** if it does not build and leave the game unchanged on this AMD PC by Sunday 11:00, it gets reverted.

**Your hand steps**

1. Open https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss and click "Download UE 5.8 DLSS Plugin". Expect to accept the NVIDIA RTX SDK licence and probably sign in to a free NVIDIA developer account.
2. Save `2026.10.16_ue5.8_dlss4.5plugin_v8.9.0.zip` into `D:\UE\dl\dlss\` without unzipping it. The folder does not exist yet.

void ASupercutCharacter::StartReload()
{
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	if (bDead || ReloadLeft > 0.f || Rounds >= Tuning.RevolverRounds)
	{
		return;
	}
	ReloadLeft = Tuning.ReloadSeconds;
	AutoReloadLeft = 0.f;   // the reload key during the wait starts it now
	USupercutAudio::Get(this).PlayFlat(TEXT("rev_reload"));
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("RELOAD start"));
	DropShells();
}

void ASupercutCharacter::DropShells()
{
	// Six shells, one from each chamber of the cylinder, where the rounds sit now.
	TArray<FTransform> Shells;
	for (const UStaticMeshComponent* Round : GunRounds)
	{
		Shells.Add(Round->GetComponentTransform());
	}
	ASupercutChips::DropShells(GetWorld(), Shells, GetVelocity(), GunRounds[0]->GetStaticMesh());
}

void ASupercutCharacter::RefillRounds()
{
	Rounds = FSupercutTuning::Get().RevolverRounds;
	ReloadLeft = 0.f;
	AutoReloadLeft = 0.f;
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("RELOAD at once: %d rounds"), Rounds);
}

void ASupercutCharacter::PlaceAt(const FVector& Location, float Yaw)
{
	const FRotator Facing(0.f, Yaw, 0.f);

	if (AController* Driver = GetController())

	}
	JumpBuffer = 0.f;
	bTrackingJump = false;
}

## How the first pass missed the two-handed hold
- I looked at the inspects only at one frame every 0.33 s, at low resolution. Those are the clearest views of the hands.
- I looked at the hand-offs at every 2nd frame, and only in crops around the gun, so I missed where the left hand starts.
- I never studied the rest pose at full resolution. Both gloves are dark plates over purple and overlap from behind, so I read two hands as one right hand.
- At 15:17 the left hand leaves from under the gun. I described that as "entering from below the bottom edge".
- I never transcribed the commentary. I wrongly assumed the audio had no voice, and he says at 6:43 that the right hand rests above the left.

The same mistake caused two more errors: round 1 said the left hand loads during the reload, and that there were no jump or walk examples. Both are fixed. Recoil, view kick, idle and look lag are unaffected. The draw needs a re-check, and the reload has been redone.

## His best take, measured
| Beat | Clip time | Length | What happens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Board first seen | 22.26 | | enters at the bottom edge |
| Rise | 22.31 to 22.56 | 300 ms | climbs to 31% from the top; tilts to +59 deg, free end up |
| Open hold | 22.56 to 22.81 | 250 ms | arm folded right back (175 deg) |
| Strike | 22.81 to 22.96 | 150 ms (9 frames) | arm closes slowly for 2 frames, then fast; the board chops down and rolls level |
| Snap | 22.960 | | the arm bounces open 5 deg for one frame; the board rebounds up 6% within 50 ms |
| Pause | to 24.21 | 1.25 s | the board sinks slowly |
| Exit | to 24.63 | 400 ms | down out of frame |

From first seen to the snap took 700 ms in this take and 1250 ms in take 2. Mirrored, his left hand holds the board by its hinge end, which is the end nearer the gun.

## SUPERCUT sequence (clap with charges)
| ms from press | Beat |
|---|---|
| 0 | The scene stops, as today. The left hand lets go of the gun; the board appears below the frame. The gun starts stepping aside. |
| 0 to 50 | Rise to the open spot (EaseOutCubic): 29.8% across, 39% down the screen, roll +59 |
| 50 to 150 | Strike: the arm closes with EaseInQuad while the board chops down |
| 150 | Snap: the clap sound, view nod and FOV punch move here, and the sweep starts |
| 150 to 650 | Bounce, then a slow sink while the sweep runs |
| 650 | Explosion; the board is gone |
| 650 to 900 | The hand drops down-left out of view, then comes back up to its spot under the gun |
| 900 to 1000 | The gun dips 1% as the hand lands, then is back at home |

[CLAP2.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/animref1/CLAP2.md>) also has:
- the refused clap and the resume;
- the cm offsets for every beat;
- the support hold described for the art lane, plus the path between the two hand poses.

## The timing conflict
I recommend (i): the scene stops on the press, and the snap comes at 150 ms. His footage doesn't argue against it.
- His rise and open hold are a person's pace with a real board. The reference game's hand is up in 50 ms and acts at 150 ms, and that reads fine.
- What matters from his footage is the strike's shape, and it survives at 6 frames.
- Option (ii) can't show the arm closing in 45 ms.
- Option (iii) breaks the 45 ms rule.

## The sweep, in three lines
1. It runs for a fixed 0.5 s from the snap: 0.45 s for the room, then 0.05 s in which the gun, hands and board turn last.
2. The front moves evenly in 1/depth from infinity to 150 cm. It crosses the floor at an even pace on screen, and the code never needs the room's size.
3. The front is a soft band of pencil lines leading about 10% ahead, with paper and hatching filling in behind.

The shader already reads depth per pixel. The change is two new parameters in the shader and in the shared parameter set, plus driving them from the character code. CLAP2 section 6 has the details.

| Move the gun home | 0.5 |
| Board hidden at rest, and the clap's steps in code | 3 |
| Snap timing, with sound, nod and FOV punch moved to the snap | 1 |

Build order, each step playable:
1. Move the gun home.
2. The board pops up with the new timing and a plain sketch fade.
3. The sweep.
4. The explosion.
5. Skeletal hands.
6. The support pose and the blend.
7. The refused clap.

## Other new results
- **Placement:** rear sight at 65.0% across and 57.7% down, barrel parallel to the view. In SUPERCUT terms, the gun home moves to about (49, 17, -8) with no rotation. Keep the scale at 1.36.
- **Reload:** the left hand holds the gun and works the cylinder; the right hand loads with a speedloader. Four takes, 2.17 to 2.32 s. At 1.0 s it still reads but feels rushed, and below about 0.8 s the loading stops reading. I'd pick 1.4 s; the length is the owner's call.
- **Jump:** the gun drops 21% of screen height on take-off (133 ms) and 18 to 20% on landing (83 ms), and recovers in 350 ms.
- **Moving:** the gun sits 3 to 7% lower and slides toward a strafe. The bob is ±1% at about 3 Hz.

All of these add to the recoil and the reload; nothing waits for anything else. The reload, placement and bob rows are in [PLAN_DIFF.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/animref1/PLAN_DIFF.md>).

## Two changes from his footage
- **Board moved left:** I shifted the whole board path 16% of the screen width to the left, so the board and the left hand stay clear of the crosshair. His board sits in front of his face.
- **Shorter pause:** his pause is 1.25 s. I cut it to the 0.5 s sweep, so the player has both hands back by 1.0 s.

If he wants either one his way, set the shift to 0 or lengthen the sweep.

## What I'm unsure about
- **Phone field of view:** I assumed 66 deg for his phone. That sets the board's size (30% of screen width, ±2) and the key positions (±6%).
- **Roll sign:** whether positive roll in Unreal lifts the board's free end. One picture settles it.
- **Arm angle:** his arm opens to 175 deg, the game's to 30. At 30, the close may read weakly.
- **Support spot:** the left hand's spot in cm comes from my description, not fitted to the arms3 mesh.
- **Hand scale:** the right hand is 1.36 times life size and the left is life size, so the support pose will look off unless both share one scale.
- **Reload sounds:** he talks over every reload, so only the loud sounds are named.
- **Transcript:** two lines are garbled. One is at 15:00.9 to 15:06.6. The other is the closing "that football animation", probably the clapperboard.

### Sat 14 Nov 19:46:58 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

The second pass of the motion study confirms your correction, and the work it describes is now split into three lanes. Two briefs are written and launch as soon as pc2's scripted run confirms the merged build.

**How the first pass got the hold wrong** (the lane's own account): it sampled the inspect animation at one frame every 0.33 s at low resolution, looked at the hand-off only in crops around the gun, and never studied the rest pose at full size. The two dark gloves overlap from behind and it read them as one hand. It also had no transcript, which was my error. This time it went frame by frame, and I checked its strip of the ability hand-off myself: the left hand comes out from under the gun.

**What it measured from your clapperboard take**

| Beat | Your take | In the game |
|---|---|---|
| Rise | 300 ms | 0 to 50 ms |
| Open hold | 250 ms | none |
| Strike | 150 ms, slow start then fast | 50 to 150 ms, same shape |
| Snap | bounce, board rebounds | 150 ms: clap sound, sweep starts |
| Pause | 1.25 s | 0.5 s, the length of the sweep |
| After | board exits | board breaks apart at 650 ms, both hands on the gun by 1.0 s |

**The three lanes**

1. **Gun motion (view1):** placement matched to your reference (gun about 11 cm further forward and 7 cm higher, barrel straight), bigger recoil that always kicks right, bob, the gun dropping on jumps and landings, and the reload kept in view.
2. **Clapperboard (clap1):** board hidden at rest, the move above, charge count on the HUD, the far-to-near sketch sweep, and the board breaking apart.
3. **Hands (not started):** rigged hands, the left-hand support pose, and the hands' part of the reload. It needs the third pose from the art thread and both lanes above merged first.

**Calls I made that are yours to overrule** `[taste: owner review]`; each is one tuning number:

- **Pause:** cut from your 1.25 s to 0.5 s so the player gets both hands back within a second.
- **Board position:** shifted 16% of the screen to the left so it never covers the crosshair. Yours sits centred.
- **Freeze timing:** the scene stops on the press, and the snap lands 150 ms later.
- **Reload length:** stays 1.0 s for now. Your reference is 2.2 s and the study's pick is 1.4 s. At 1.0 s the eject and the cylinder shutting flash past in 2 to 3 frames. Tell me a number and I'll change it.

**What may not make it:** the "exact reload" with the left hand working the cylinder and the right hand using a speedloader is 6 to 8 hours of work after the rigged hands are in. It might not fit before Sunday's feature stop. The gun's own part of that reload will be in either way.

Details are in [CLAP2.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/animref1/CLAP2.md>) and [PLAN_DIFF.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/animref1/PLAN_DIFF.md>).

In a recording, one hanging shot adds nothing measurable and five add +1.6 dB, so the camera kick does most of the "five feels bigger than one". Fixing it means raising `shot_release` in mix1's level table, which I left to you and the sound lane.
- **B8 has a fifth tuning line,** `ReleaseSoundFullCount` 4 (1 to 24), so the sound has its own number for how it grows with the count. One shot keeps today's volume and four or more play at twice that.
- **B9 changes most gunshots in main8,** because 45 of its 46 shots are fired during a freeze. Nobody has listened to it; no sound plays aloud here, and the hearing tool couldn't tell the two pitches apart.
- **W1 has a narrow tuning window.** Measured by bounding boxes, the depth scale only works between about 0.38 and 0.40, and 0.4 is the default. The film-gear before/after pictures show no clipping on either side, because the gear's collision box keeps the eye far enough away.
- **B12 pictures:** the lines read fine. The clutter is the hanging shots themselves: big yellow discs 100 cm from the muzzle that wall off the middle of the screen with 12 hanging.
- **Not run:** a full unity build. Farm builds are adaptive and left my test file out of the unity file, and builds stay off c4. Instead I checked that none of my test helper or test class names appear in any other source file.
- **Farm slips:** I built once at 71% CPU on [pc-b] and started one picture run while another lane's editor was busy there. After that, every heavy step went through a gate script that refuses unless [pc-b] is free.
- **No c4 vs [pc-b] difference to report:** every run on either PC gave the reference line, though no single head was run on both.

- **Sounds.** Every hover plays a short tick, and every click plays a louder clack, 12 to 15 dB over the tick (0:18 to 0:44). The pattern comes from the reference's game sound on track 0, with his voice taken out. It plays a 30 to 40 ms tick then a soft tone on hover, and a burst 15 to 20 dB louder on click. The sounds themselves are our own. The mock has stand-in sounds behind a "Sound off" button, off by default.

## Sounds

You don't have to know where to begin: lane [SUPERCUT sfx3: ranked sound candidates and a picking page for the owner](t3-thread://v2/12df28c1-1bab-4242-8860-5f9e21a1f8bf/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A05344926-1268-4f01-b43e-b984a609df3e%3Adelegate-task%3Aee48656f-77ef-479d-b7d0-a9a9cfdc7a83) is building that starting point. It will:

- **Rank** the 48 sounds by how often each plays in a run and how loud it is, so the top of the list is where you begin.
- **Cut candidates:** 4 to 6 for each of the top 12 to 15 sounds, levelled to equal loudness, with your gun pack first for anything gun-like. The current sound is always one of the choices.
- **Build a page** where you pick one per sound, or "none of these", and add a one-line note. A button exports your picks as a file for me.
- **Render fight clips:** a 20 to 30 second stretch of a real fight with one sound swapped, if the game's log carries enough to do it honestly.

Nothing goes into the game until you've picked. No lane and no tool here can hear; they can only measure. Your ears are the only judge, so the page is built to make each call take seconds.

The two-handed hold is posed and delivered by the art lane, and a lane is now bringing the hands into the game: [SUPERCUT hands1: rigged hands imported, posed from data, blend, behin...](t3-thread://v2/12df28c1-1bab-4242-8860-5f9e21a1f8bf/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A05344926-1268-4f01-b43e-b984a609df3e%3Adelegate-task%3A8eb3134e-4239-42c4-9b93-7f00d103be94).

This is the hold as posed, from six sides. The view from behind (right column, middle) is closest to what the player sees:

![two-handed hold](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/arms3/renders/hold_support/_views.jpg>)

**What the art lane measured**
- **Overlap:** none between either hand and the gun, or between the two hands. Trigger, hammer and cylinder all move freely, and the sights are not hidden.
- **Hand-off path:** moving the left hand straight from the gun to the board would pass through the gun and the right hand. It made an in-between pose (hand 6 cm left, fingers open) that clears both.
- **Its own doubts:** the left hand cups under the right more than it wraps around it, and its wrist is bent 30 degrees, the limit of a real wrist.

**What hands1 does now**
- Imports the rigged mesh.
- Poses it by code from the art lane's pose data.
- Builds the blend through the in-between pose.
- Puts the hands in the game behind a switch that is off by default.

I started it now, without waiting for the gun and clapperboard lanes, because the game has no hands at all today, so the import collides with nothing. Tying the hands to the clap and the reload is a second pass after those two lanes are merged.

**Two things need you**
1. **Licence.** The art lane says the Fab listing for these hands shows no licence. You downloaded them, so please check what the listing or your Fab library says. The hands stay behind the off switch and out of the build that ships until you confirm, and the lane is recording every file it imports so they can be removed in one commit.
2. **Visibility.** At today's gun position only 29% of the right hand and 10% of the left are on screen. The gun lane is moving the gun up and forward to match your reference, and hands1 will report the share at the new position. If the left hand is still mostly out of frame, the support pose needs changing.

Delegated task node:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A05344926-1268-4f01-b43e-b984a609df3e%3Adelegate-task%3Ac2d5e25d-acad-4adb-baa9-99545eb7f260 (SUPERCUT vfx1: particle effects for the flash and impacts) [completed]:
Lane vfx1 is finished: the muzzle flash, shot impacts and enemy hit and kill bursts are particle effects on branch `vfx1`, five commits on `683bff6`, tree clean, nothing pushed, merged or packaged. Effect (d), the clap ring and refill pad, is not built.

**Route.** An editor commandlet runs `Tools/make_vfx.py`, which drives the engine's own experimental Niagara toolset plugin (enabled on the command line only). It rebuilds every asset under `Content/VFX` in about two minutes with no person at the editor. It starts from the engine's DefaultSystem and DirectionalBurst template emitter, which are engine content. The textures are drawn by `Art/vfx/make_vfx_textures.py`.

**Checks**, all on [pc-b] through the farm wrapper, on the committed tree:
- **Tests:** 118 passed, 0 failed (the 112 from before plus 6 new). The new ones cover the seven tuning lines, flash spawn and expiry, freeze and resume, sparks on metal against dust on foam, and same seed with and without effects.
- **Scripted run `main8`, seed 1, twice:** both give `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17`, equal to the reference. It needs `-TimeoutSeconds 540` on the farm, because the default 240 s limit stops it mid-run.
- **Frame time:** in a fight room the effects-on runs were not slower than effects-off (average 158 and 136 against 123 and 118). The spread between runs on a shared PC is larger than any cost. These are offscreen numbers; no desktop measurement was made.

**What is weak in the pictures:**
- The enemy hit burst is hard to find behind the game's own white flash, hit marker and chip cubes. The kill reads better, a yellow pop then brown dust.
- Wall dust and scraps are clear from two steps away but faint from mid-room, and the scraps look like cut paper up close.
- The smoke wisp is small and easy to miss.

**Things you should know:**
- Every system ends with an empty emitter named `End`. In the last emitter of a system built this way, sprites sized by an expression on a user number do not draw. I found the pattern by bisecting, not the engine cause.
- Not checked: the cook and a packaged build, fire at one shot every 0.10 s, and how the effects sit with feel4's wall marks.
- The asset commandlet ran on c4 because the farm wrapper has no commandlet step, so no asset came back from [pc-b].
- A stale `shots/tex_preview/T_Vfx_Ring_preview.jpg` is left in the lane folder. A safety check refused the delete.
- [pc-b] shows two `Supercut` processes running now. They are not mine and I left them alone.
- The gotchas in the handoff are not yet copied into `unreal/GOTCHAS.md`.

The handoff also has the ten-minute recipe for a new effect, the tuning table, cook requirements, merge notes and the `[taste: owner review]` list.

16	## 1. The authoring route
17	
18	Chosen: an editor commandlet runs a Python script, and the script drives the engine's own Niagara toolset.
19	
20	```
21	UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe <copy>\Supercut.uproject -run=pythonscript -Script=<copy>\Tools\make_vfx.py
22	    -EnablePlugins=NiagaraToolsets -AllowCommandletRendering -unattended -nopause -nosplash -abslog=<log file>
23	```
24	
25	Inside, every edit is one call: `unreal.ToolsetRegistry.execute_tool("NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System", tool, json)`.
26	The toolset is the experimental plugin `Engine\Plugins\Experimental\Toolsets\NiagaraToolsets` of 5.9. It is switched
27	on by the command line only, so the game and the `.uproject` do not depend on it.
28	
29	Why this one: it needs no person and no open editor, it takes about two minutes, and the whole recipe is one text
30	file in git. Each run deletes and rebuilds every asset, so the assets always match the script.
31	
32	What the script starts from, all engine content, nothing downloaded:
33	
34	- `/Niagara/DefaultAssets/DefaultSystem` as the template system. Its own Fountain emitter is removed.
35	- `/Niagara/DefaultAssets/Templates/Emitters/DirectionalBurst` as the template for every emitter.
36	- `/Niagara/DynamicInputs/UniformRange/V2/RandomRangeFloat` for random numbers per particle.
37	- `/Niagara/Modules/Update/Size/ScaleSpriteSize` for growth over life.
38	
39	The textures and the materials are ours: the script imports the PNGs and builds six unlit materials node by node.
40	
41	What was tried and dropped:
42	
43	- Calling the toolset's functions straight from Python. They are `AICallable`, not `BlueprintCallable`, so Python has

cd "[notes]/unreal" && cat >> GOTCHAS.md <<'EOF'

## SUPERCUT vfx1 lane: Niagara effects built by script (14 Nov 2026, verified by the lane)

Full list and the ten-minute recipe for a new effect: `megajam-2026/lanes/vfx1/HANDOFF.md`, sections 1 and 10.

- Niagara systems can be authored with no open editor: `UnrealEditor-Cmd ... -run=pythonscript -Script=Tools\make_vfx.py
  -EnablePlugins=NiagaraToolsets -AllowCommandletRendering`. The only door from Python is
  `unreal.ToolsetRegistry.execute_tool("NiagaraToolsets.NiagaraToolset_System", tool, json)`. The toolset's own
  functions are `AICallable`, not `BlueprintCallable`, so Python has no binding for them.
- In a system built this way, the LAST emitter does not draw sprites whose size or life is an expression on a user
  number (`User.Size * 4.0`). Found by bisecting, cause in the engine not found. Cure: end every system with an
  empty emitter (`End`). `System.save()` in the script adds it.
- The toolset's `GetSystemCompileState` and `GetStackIssues` never return in a commandlet. Read the log for
  `LogNiagaraCompiler: Error` and `LogMaterial: Error` instead.
- Particle colours are linear light: 0.21 shows as middle grey. The particle script machine has no `smoothstep`.
- Inputs behind a mode switch ("Lifetime Mode", "Sprite Size Mode") do not exist until the mode is set.
- A Niagara component does not run without a renderer (`-nullrhi`, the tests), and `UNiagaraSystem::IsReadyToRun()`
  is always false there. Tests can prove an effect actor spawned and expired, not that anything drew.
- Systems loaded only by path from C++ need `+DirectoriesToAlwaysCook=(Path="/Game/VFX")` in `DefaultGame.ini`, or
  the cook leaves them out. Sprite materials need the "used with Niagara sprites" flag or a packaged game draws the
  default material.
- Additive particles show nothing against white rooms. The hot materials are alpha composite.
- An uncooked run draws nothing for about 8 frames on the first use of each effect material ("Preparing Shaders").
  Picture scripts fire one warm-up shot first.
- Every copy of the game on a PC reads the same `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Supercut\Tuning.txt`. Do not put one there to try
  numbers while other lanes run on that PC.
EOF

### Sat 14 Nov 21:12:30 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

The first check of the particle effects merge found a real problem, and I've fixed it in the main copy. The re-check is running on pc2 now.

- **What failed:** 134 of 135 tests passed. The one failure was the test that says a kill opens the room's gate on the same frame.
- **Cause:** the room and the shot update in no fixed order. When the room happened to go first, the gate and the room-clear music came one tick late. The new effects did not cause this; they changed how many objects exist, which moved the order.
- **Fix:** the kill itself now asks the room to open the gate, so the order no longer matters.

Your play folder and the testers' copies stay on the previous build until the re-check prints 135 passing tests and the reference run line. The gate can now open one tick earlier than before, so I'll compare the run line carefully.

### Sat 14 Nov 21:28:20 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

Yes, you can pose them yourself, and your eye for the proportions looks right to me. I've asked the art thread ([Epic Jam Free Stuff](t3-thread://v2/12df28c1-1bab-4242-8860-5f9e21a1f8bf/3ca8fc11-12b5-42c9-8b85-275c3872e49f)) for a Blender file built for that, and it is queued there now.

**What you'll get:**
- One Blender file with the revolver, the clapperboard and both rigged hands in today's poses.
- A camera at the game's eye, so the camera view is what the player sees. There is one for where the gun sits today and one for where the gun-motion lane is moving it.
- One scale control for the hands and one for the gun, plus a plain box with the measurements of an ordinary revolver beside the gun to judge size against.
- A short how-to with the exact keys.
- A script that turns your saved file back into the pose data the game reads, and re-runs the checks that the fingers don't pass through the gun.

**On the size:** reading the art lane's grid picture, the gun is about 20 cm long and 15 cm tall, which is ordinary for a short revolver. Its cylinder is about 5.5 cm across where a real one is about 4, so the body is fat. The hands are a slim pair, with a wrist about 5 cm wide. So I think it is both: a chunky gun in thin arms. Those numbers are read off a picture, and I've asked for real measurements.

![current two-handed hold, six views on a 2 cm grid](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/arms3/renders/hold_support/_views.jpg>)

Nothing changes in the game meanwhile. The lane importing the hands keeps working with the current poses behind its off switch, and your poses will replace them through the same data files.

"""Masks file names that a lane listed from the owner's own folders. Reads the names from the exported transcript's
PowerShell tables (name, size, date, time), so no name is written here or printed. Skips the lane's own NN_ files.
Usage: python -I add_words10.py <transcript.md> [more.md ...]"""
import io, json, re, sys
p = r"D:\UE\megajam-2026-devlog\tools\redact.local.json"
d = json.load(io.open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
r = d["replace"]
row = re.compile(r"^(.+?)\s+(\d+)\s+\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{4}\s+\d{1,2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\s+[AP]M\s*$")
added = 0
seen = 0
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    for line in io.open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        m = row.match(line.rstrip("\n"))
        if not m:
            continue
        name = m.group(1).strip()
        seen += 1
        if re.match(r"^\d\d_", name) or len(name) < 6 or name.startswith("["):
            continue
        for k in (name, name.rsplit(".", 1)[0]):
            if len(k) >= 6 and k not in r and not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z]+", k):
                r[k] = "[file]"
                added += 1
json.dump(d, io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
print("rows seen", seen, "keys added", added, "total", len(r))
```

Yes, we're regenerating it. The art thread has the job (sent 22:19), and the old revolver stays in the game until you approve pictures of the new one.

**What I asked for**
- **The gun:** an original model of the real-world type you named: large stainless frame, long barrel with a full underlug, vented rib on top, gas ports by the front sight, fluted six-shot cylinder, all-black rubber grip.
- **Where the look comes from:** real photos of the real gun, used for looking at only. I did not point the art thread at the game's model or screenshots: I can't have it copy a specific game's art, and the real gun gets you the same look. No maker's marks or text on it.
- **Mechanics:** the same moving parts as the first one (cylinder, hammer, trigger, six rounds), plus a swing-out crane, which the first gun never had. That lets the reload show the rounds leaving.
- **Credits:** capped at 20 for this job, with a ledger. Higher quality tiers are allowed this time.
- **Size:** built to the real gun's published dimensions, with a table against the hands, so "oversized" gets answered with numbers.
- **Timing:** candidate pictures at the game's camera, beside the old gun, by about 23:45. Cut and checked parts by about 02:00.

**Your question on part splitting**
- We did it another way. The first revolver was generated whole, then cut in Blender with hand-placed cut shapes and pivots. An earlier attempt to generate it from an exploded picture failed because the image tool refused that prompt twice.
- The splitter in your screenshot does not appear in the generator's API docs, which list only submit, check status, download and check balance ([docs.hyper3d.ai](https://docs.hyper3d.ai/)). It looks like a website-only feature; the art thread will check the full parameter list once to confirm.
- The plan is the same cut route, since it is proven. A splitter would not give us pivots or clearances anyway.

import tempfile
import time

SKIP = {"Intermediate", "Binaries", "Saved", "DerivedDataCache", ".git"}
PRUNE = ("Source/", "Content/", "Config/", "Tools/", "Script/")
TAR = r"C:\Windows\System32\tar.exe"


def ssh(host, cmd, data=None):
    r = subprocess.run(["ssh", host, cmd], input=data, capture_output=True)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit(f"FARM ssh {host} failed ({r.returncode}): {cmd}\n{r.stderr.decode(errors='replace')}")
    return r.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def main():
    host, root, name, proj = sys.argv[1:5]
    proj = os.path.abspath(proj)
    if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(proj, "Supercut.uproject")):
        sys.exit(f"FARM no Supercut.uproject in {proj}")
    dest = f"{root}\\Farm\\{name}"
    t0 = time.time()
    remote = {}
    for line in ssh(host, f"powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File {root}\\Farm\\_farm\\list.ps1 -Dir {dest}").splitlines():
        rel, size, mtime = line.rsplit("|", 2)
        remote[rel] = (int(size), int(mtime))
    local = {}
    for top in os.listdir(proj):
        if top in SKIP:
            continue
        p = os.path.join(proj, top)
        if os.path.isfile(p):
            st = os.stat(p)
            local[top] = (st.st_size, int(st.st_mtime))
            continue
        for d, dirs, files in os.walk(p):
            for f in files:
                full = os.path.join(d, f)
                st = os.stat(full)
                local[os.path.relpath(full, proj).replace("\\", "/")] = (st.st_size, int(st.st_mtime))
    send = sorted(r for r, v in local.items() if remote.get(r) != v)
    gone = sorted(r for r in remote if r not in local and r.startswith(PRUNE))
    nbytes = sum(local[r][0] for r in send)

The art thread confirms the new revolver is under way as lane rodin6, with the 20-credit cap and the same two report points: whole-gun pictures about 23:45, cut and checked parts about 02:00.

On the main build, the check of the generated-runs merge passed its build and all 143 tests, then failed at packaging. That one was my doing:

- **What failed:** the game target would not link, because one compiled file on pc2 was older than the code it was supposed to match.
- **Cause:** I merged gen2 into the main copy at 21:22 while the previous check was still packaging on pc2. Thirty-five seconds later pc2 compiled that file from the old source. Because the mirror keeps file times, the build tool then saw a "newer" object and skipped recompiling it.
- **Fix:** I deleted the stale compiled files on pc2, so the game target rebuilds in full.
- **Rule from now on:** I do not merge into the main copy until a running check has finished packaging. It is written into `unreal/GOTCHAS.md`.

**Calls for you, each marked `[taste: owner review]`**
- A scratch on the flatbed trolley could read as a "4".
- The crew stool blocks shots and sight like a solid box, where the chairs let them through. It could be made see-through like the chairs.
- The Marksman's shot starts 61 cm past its revolver's muzzle. I kept the shot point where it was, because moving it changes play.
- The lamp's barn doors cut dark bars across its lit face when seen from below.
- Cover props cook their textures at 2048. Dropping them to 1024 would save about 80 MB.

# Re-bake the generated runs with props

Lane gen2, 14 Nov 2026. For after lane props1's branch is merged: it adds the prop catalogue

Fixed and proven in a packaged build. The fault was real and shows clearly in pictures. The fix is commit `c3cf0bc` on branch `litter1` (tree clean, not merged).

**Before** (packaged Development build of `9c6f131`, room `fight/01_wind_machine`, 1920x1080): the log had both warning lines, once each. All three kinds of litter drew the engine's default material:
- Landed chips were grey cubes with the engine's fine checker pattern.
- Shot marks on the floor were light grey discs. The game sets a near-black scorch.
- Shells were flat grey, with no brass.

**After:** the chips are tan wood, the marks are near black, and the shells are brass with grey tips.

![before and after](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/litter1/shots/sheet_before_after.jpg>)

**Fix:**
- **`M_Solid`:** `Tools/make_assets.py` now sets `MATUSAGE_INSTANCED_STATIC_MESHES` on it. I checked the enum name in the engine's `MaterialInterface.h`.
- **`MI_Revolver_Round`:** its parent is `M_HeldProp`. That is made by `make_props.make_material`, which `Tools/make_held.py` calls. Both functions now take a list of usage flags, empty by default, and only `make_held.py` passes the instanced-mesh flag, so `M_SetProp` is built as before.
- **Why the parent is enough:** a material instance takes its parent's usage flags unless it overrides them. I checked this in the engine's `MaterialInstance.cpp`.
- **Assets:** I ran both scripts on [pc-b]. Of the 46 assets they remade, only `M_Solid.uasset` and `M_HeldProp.uasset` changed: each grew 64 bytes, and the one new field in each is `bUsedWithInstancedStaticMeshes`. The other 44 differ only in GUIDs and hashes, so I left them out.
- **Picture script:** `Script/litter1_pics.txt` is new and committed with the fix.
- **Same fault elsewhere:** `SupercutLitter` is the only instanced mesh component in `Source\Supercut`, and its pieces can only get these two materials.

**Checks** (all on [pc-b]):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Tests | 135 pass, 0 fail |
| Fixed package, picture run | 0 `missing usage flag` lines, no material warnings |
| main8 reference run, twice | `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17` both times; 0 `missing usage flag` lines (the run has 14 reloads) |

**Not checked:**
- I did not run main8 on the unfixed package. The "before" line is your pc2 reference.
- No Shipping build.
- [pc-b] compiles with a newer MSVC than c4. Only content and Python changed, but the judges' build should still come from c4.
- I did not re-run `make_props.py` (the set props).
- I did not add a dev-log entry; I left that for when you merge.

**Things to know:**
- `set_material_usage` is deprecated in 5.9 and prints a Python warning each run. `make_vfx.py` uses it too. I kept it, as the brief asked.
- `lanes\props1\HANDOFF.md` does not exist. I followed hands1's way of running editor Python on a farm PC instead.
- The first `package` of a new farm name fails in 0 s, because a fresh mirror has no `Saved\Logs` folder. Run `build` once first. This and three other traps are in `unreal/GOTCHAS.md` under a new litter1 section.

**Frame time:** the hall costs under 15% everywhere I could measure cleanly, so nothing was cut. Two methods agree:
- Same package, hall off then on, back to back: room 03 +0.43 ms (about 9.5%), room 01 +0.25 to +0.38 ms (5 to 7.5%).

Editor runs hide this. I re-saved both with the flag, and a new test goes red if they lose it. props1's importer (`make_props_real.py`) and `make_assets.py` should set the flag too, or a regenerate breaks it. This is the main merge risk, because binary files can't be merged by hand.

It writes `arms3/owner_pose/out_rodin6/` and never touches `owner_pose/out/` or `arms3/out/`. Run on the untouched file it exits 0, and its pose files equal `arms3/out/poses` to 0.00004, so the starting poses are the first file's.

Why a second bring-back script, which you did not ask for: plain `bring_back.py` does run to the end on the new file, but it is wrong for it in three ways.

- Its touch counts compare with the old gun's baseline, so the untouched new file reads "NOT clean".

[bring_back_rodin6.py](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/arms3/owner_pose/bring_back_rodin6.py>) is the same route: it calls `bring_back.py`'s own worker step and arms3's three scripts unchanged, after pointing the item loader at the new gun at the factor stored in the file. Its clearance line for the right hand reads 133 pairs, the same 133 the file's own touch count gives, so the worker's gun sits where the file's gun sits. It has its own baseline, `baseline_touch_rodin6.json`.

#!/bin/bash
# Merge check of the main copy on pc2 (farm name sfx2). Waits until pc2 passes the load check, then
# mirror, build, test, package, scripted run, picture run, fetch. Usage: merge_check.sh [picture script name]
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
LOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs
PICLOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs_pics
PC=pc2
NAME=sfx2

# Priority flag: while it is fresh, status reports the PC as busy to every lane (farm/remote/status.ps1).
flag_on()  { ssh $PC "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"Set-Content -Path C:\\\\UE\\\\Farm\\\\_main_waiting -Value main\"" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
flag_off() { ssh $PC "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"Remove-Item C:\\\\UE\\\\Farm\\\\_main_waiting -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\"" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
trap flag_off EXIT

idle() {
  local s; s=$("$F" status $PC 2>&1)
  local ram cpu busy
  ram=$(echo "$s" | sed -n 's/^free_ram_gb=\([0-9.]*\).*/\1/p')
  cpu=$(echo "$s" | sed -n 's/^cpu_load_pct=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p')
  busy=$(echo "$s" | sed -n 's/^busy_procs=//p' | sed 's/ *SupercutMainCheckx1//')
  [ -z "$busy" ] && busy=none
  flag_on
  echo "$(date +%H:%M) ram=$ram cpu=$cpu busy=$busy"
  [ -z "$ram" ] && return 1
  case "$busy" in *Supercut*|*UnrealEditor*|*cl*|*link*|*dotnet*) return 1;; esac
  awk -v r="$ram" -v c="$cpu" 'BEGIN{exit !(r>=6 && c<60)}'
}
wait_idle() {
  for i in $(seq 1 90); do idle && return 0; sleep 60; done
  echo "WAIT_TIMEOUT"; return 1
}
step() { flag_on; echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) $*"; "$@"; local rc=$?; echo "=== exit $rc"; return $rc; }

wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" mirror $PC $NAME /d/UE/Projects/Supercut59 || exit 1
step "$F" build $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Jobs 8 || exit 2
wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" test $PC $NAME "$LOGS" || exit 3
grep -a "passed\|failed" "$LOGS/test/console.txt" | tail -3
wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" package $PC $NA
[... 589 more characters not shown]
