All eight steps are committed on `ui1` in `D:\UE\wt\ui1`, and the worktree is clean. The handoff is [HANDOFF.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/ui1/HANDOFF.md>), and times and causes are in [LOG.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/ui1/LOG.md>).

**What is in, per step**
- **Step 0 (`219769f`):** the shared style, a painter that draws everything by code, and one hover and click sound hook. The HUD lane starts from this commit.
- **A1 (`9264563`):** the settings frame: six tabs, section headers, scroll, X to reset a tab, Esc to go back.
- **A2 (`e995cef`):** slider rows (number centred on the track, drag, a refusal at each end). DISPLAY MODE now reads the actual window.
- **A6 (`333032e`):** the title screen, with the reveal and the START press.
- **A7 (`c030c1b`):** the pause panel slides in from the left and out again, and QUIT GAME asks for confirmation on a band.
- **A4 (`e530302`):** the CROSSHAIR tab with a 3x preview. The HUD draws the crosshair from the settings, and the default is the old crosshair pixel for pixel.
- **A3 (`c931a61`):** AUDIO, VIDEO, GAMEPLAY and ACCESSIBILITY rows wired to the engine, plus the performance overlay.
- **A5 (`ced7787`):** CONTROLS gets INVERT LOOK and two key boxes per action. Taking a key another action holds swaps the two keys, and Esc cancels. The player controller now reads every game key from these bindings.

**Checks**
- **Build and tests:** every step built and passed all its tests: 131, 134, 137, 140, 143, 146, 150, then 153 for A5, with no failures. A5's tests passed on both [pc-c] and [pc-b].
- **main8:** twice after every step, both runs gave `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17`.
- **Pictures:** taken at 1920x1080 and 1280x720 for every step and compared with the mock; they match. The key boxes use the mock's exact sizes, colours and 530 ms blink.
- **The brief's proofs each have a test:**
  - every setting is saved, clamped and read back;
  - a rebind swaps FORWARD and BACK and survives `LoadSettings(true)`;
  - FORWARD rebound to I walks the hero 267 cm in 0.5 s, while W now walks it 0 cm;
  - the pause panel slides in and out;
  - every clickable element plays one hover and one click sound, and none has a rounded corner (216 elements checked);
  - the default crosshair matches the old one.
- **Colour-blind mode:** it shows in the pictures. With PROTANOPIA the red marks shift from (91,22,15) to (113,47,40), while greys move by 1 at most.

**Run line:** A5 was built, tested and packaged on [pc-c]. [pc-c]'s own user load then held the load check for 12 minutes, so as you said, A5 was rebuilt, tested, packaged, run and pictured on [pc-b] (farm name `ui1`, `-TimeoutSeconds 540`).

**Rows left out, and why**
- **Not in 5.9 or would change nothing:** OUTPUT (no such setting in 5.9), RESOLUTION (the desktop size or WindowSize is used, as today), RAY TRACING (the game uses none), LANDSCAPE quality (the game has no landscape).
- **Your decision:** FIELD OF VIEW stays with the tuning file.
- **Other lanes:** the HUD lane's five rows, B4's teaching prompts, B5's INTERFACE volume, and B6's upscaler and DLSS.
- **DLSS MODE:** not added. A comment above RENDER RESOLUTION on the VIDEO tab marks where main's row goes (lane dlss2), and HANDOFF says how to wire it. That comment went in after the last build.

**Things that differ from the spec**
- **Key bindings don't use Enhanced Input.** 5.9's rebinding works only on input actions and mapping contexts, and the game has none: it reads raw keys. So the bindings are saved in `USupercutUserSettings`, as the brief says settings should be.
- **Volume defaults stay 100,** as the game is today. The spec asks for MASTER and MUSIC at 80. This is flagged for your review.

**What I did not check**
- No real keyboard or mouse input; everything came from tests and scripts.
- Only PROTANOPIA was pictured, not the other two modes, and the spec's check that the four signal colours stay apart in each mode is not done.
- Frame rate on a desktop session (farm runs are offscreen).
- Picture sizes other than the two above.
- Sounds aloud: every run was `-Silent`.

**Merge risk:** `USupercutUserSettings` will conflict with main's DLSS fields; keep both sides.

The interface lane has finished, and I merged it and the hands into the main copy myself. The check of the result is running on pc2.

![title screen](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/ui1/shots/a6_ui_title_hover_settings_1080.jpg>)

**What the interface lane built**
- A title screen, and a pause panel that slides in from the left.
- Settings with six tabs: gameplay, crosshair, controls, accessibility, audio and video.
- Full crosshair customisation with a live preview. The default matches the old crosshair pixel for pixel.
- Key rebinding with two keys per action. Taking a key another action holds swaps the two.
- Colour-blind modes and a performance overlay.

**What it left out**
- The DLSS row. The place for it is marked on the video tab, and it gets wired in the next pass.
- The in-game HUD restyle, which is a separate lane.
- Field of view, which stays in the tuning file.

**Two things for you** `[taste: owner review]`
- Volume defaults stay at 100, as the game is today. The spec asked for master and music at 80.
- Only one of the three colour-blind modes was pictured.

Both merges had small conflicts and I kept both sides in each. The main copy is now `dba8950`. If the pc2 check passes, this build goes to your play folder.

Delegated task node:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A05344926-1268-4f01-b43e-b984a609df3e%3Adelegate-task%3A829fe43f-9e40-4c8a-b48e-cd5cb99be097 (SUPERCUT view1: revolver view model motion from the owner's reference) [completed]:
All seven steps are committed on `view1`, one commit each. The tree is clean, and [HANDOFF.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/view1/HANDOFF.md>) is written. Nothing was merged, rebased or pushed.

**What is in, per step**
1. **Placement** (094fc62): the gun sits at (49, 17, -11.5), placed by its sights. Shots now start from a muzzle fixed to the camera, so no view motion can move where a shot goes.
2. **Recoil and single action** (6abe6c8): the gun kick has a 35 ms rise and a spring settle. The hammer, trigger and cylinder work as a single-action revolver.
3. **Bob, move offset, jump, landing** (d2cb86f).
4. **Idle breathing, look lag, drop on turn, strafe tilt** (ede1743).
5. **Reload in view** (051c78b), gun only:
   - The gun follows keyed poses through the beats, with the eject merged into the cylinder swing.
   - The cylinder swings out on a new hinge.
   - The shells now drop at the eject beat.
   - All six rounds show at 0.658 of the reload; `GetRoundsShown()` is there for the HUD.
   - Each beat calls `OnReloadBeat(name)` for the hands lane.
6. **Draw and holster** (26eaae8): the gun comes up at spawn and in each new room. A shot ends the draw at once. A death holsters it.
7. **View kick** (ef920c1): 1.5°, a 60 ms rise, back by 0.25 s. There is a new tuning line, `FireKickRiseSeconds`.

**Checks**
- **Build and tests:** passed on pc2 at every step. The suite went from 129 tests to 144, all passing at the end.
- **Run line:** after every step, both main8 runs printed `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17`. Steps 1 and 7 were allowed to change it; neither did.
- **30 and 240 fps:** the same three-shot log peaks at 1.009 at 33 ms at both. It settles 0.317 s and 0.315 s after the third shot.
- **Step 4:**
  - Ten seconds standing still stays inside the breathing amplitudes.
  - A 360°/s turn reaches the clamps (2.5 cm, 4°) and never passes them.
  - At full lag against a wall the gun is whole and in frame.
- **Step 5:**
  - In the strip (a picture every 50 ms), the gun never leaves the frame.
  - A reload during a jump stays in frame too.
  - Rounds become usable 1.008 s after the start, from both the reload key and the auto start. That is the same as before; the extra 8 ms is one frame of the timer's own rounding.
- **Step 6:** a shot one frame into the draw puts the gun home on the next frame.
- **Step 7:** one shot peaks at 1.53° at 62.5 ms and is back at 254 ms.
- **Clip:** there is a 2 s silent clip of three shots and a reload, `shots/v7_clip_shots_reload.mp4`.

**Changes from the spec, and why**
- **Home height** -8 → -11.5: at -8 both sights sat 4 to 5% of the screen height too high.
- **Gun kick pitch** 20 → 23: the spec wanted about 13% of the screen height. 20 measured 11.5%; 23 gives 12.8%.
- **Move onset:** a spring instead of a cubic ease, because a spring restarts cleanly from any state.
- **Landing:**
  - The drop scales with how fast the player was falling.
  - It starts from wherever the jump's drop is; without that, a cut-short jump landed with the gun low and snapped.
- **Reload:**
  - Only the 1.0 s layout is built, since ReloadSeconds stays 1.0.
  - The keys use a smoothstep ease. The cubic ease turned the gun 12.6° in a single frame; smoothstep keeps it under 7°.
- **Draw:**
  - It starts from (-6, -4, -22), as PLAN_DIFF recommends.
  - There is no click on the hammer cock, since this job adds no new sounds.
- **View kick:** I read "back by 0.25 s" as 0.25 s after the shot, with the 60 ms rise included.

**Not checked**
- **Packaged build:** every run was the editor build in game mode.
- **HUD:** it still reads `GetRounds()`, so its count fills at the end of the reload. Wiring it to `GetRoundsShown()` is clap1's job.
- **Real mouse turns:** the look lag was only checked with scripted turns and tests.
- **Not in pictures:** the holster, and a reload during a freeze. Both have tests only.
- **1.4 s reload:** the layout with a separate eject beat is not built.

The merge risks and gotchas are written up in HANDOFF.md.

**Changes REBAKE.md did not foresee:**
1. **Flat hall floors.** Three hall floor pieces have `size=400,400,0`, and the generator's reader refused any 0. It now follows the game's own rule (`SupercutProps.cpp` lines 135 to 141): 0 is allowed only on a prop that does not block.

The reader now leaves `where=hall` lines out, and the checker refuses such a prop too. That is why the prop count reads 117, not 125; the hash is unchanged.
3. **One test updated.** `ARoomsCatalogueLineMustMatchTheLoadedCatalogue` expected the old stand-in catalogue's hash, which step 2 replaces by design. It now expects `cb703ef0` and also checks that the game loaded that same hash. It is stricter than before, not looser.

- Generator: self-test 49 cases, 0 wrong. In the test vectors only the catalogue and the `props1` entries changed; no `props0` entry moved. `check_baked.py` prints `600 rooms (600 with props, catalogue cb703ef0), 50 runs, 0 problems`.

- Catalogue in the package: I listed it on both PCs. It is a loose file at `Supercut/Content/Props/catalogue.txt`, byte-identical to the source. It gets there through a line in `Supercut.Build.cs` (`RuntimeDependencies`), not through `DefaultGame.ini`.
- Load pass: all 50 runs read the right run file and built 600 rooms, with 0 `ROOM FILE` lines and 0 warnings. Runs 1 to 44 ran on [pc-c], 45 to 50 on [pc-b].

**The six pictures** (props show the default material because of the base fault, so I judged placement and size only):
- `gen_s7` room 8, fight practice: the plain dark flat ahead fills the view and no prop is visible. Reads bare.

In none of them does a prop block the way, float, sink or sit inside another that I can see.

**Problems found by counting, not fixed:**
- **Flats are why rooms look bare.** 914 of 1,112 crate boxes became props, but only 6 of 1,315 flats did. The catalogue has no room prop that is thin, about 2.6 m long and 1.9 m tall, so every arena room opens on a dark flat and the props sit behind it or along the walls. A flat-shaped set prop in the catalogue would fix most of this.
- **Some props poke into walls.** The generator ignores `from=` (a prop whose box is off its origin). Three props that do not block are affected, and 47 of their 92 placements reach up to 12 cm into a wall. It only affects looks.
- **Hall-only marking has gaps.** 28 hall pieces have no `where=hall` mark. None gets placed today, but a later catalogue change could let one in. Marking them all in `make_props_real.py` would close it.

#!/bin/bash
# Merge check of the main copy on pc2 (farm name sfx2). Waits until pc2 passes the load check, then
# mirror, build, test, package, scripted run, picture run, fetch. Usage: merge_check.sh [picture script name]
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
LOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs
PICLOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs_pics
PC=pc2
NAME=sfx2

# Priority flag: while it is fresh, status reports the PC as busy to every lane (farm/remote/status.ps1).
flag_on()  { ssh $PC "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"Set-Content -Path C:\\\\UE\\\\Farm\\\\_main_waiting -Value main\"" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
flag_off() { ssh $PC "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"Remove-Item C:\\\\UE\\\\Farm\\\\_main_waiting -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\"" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
trap flag_off EXIT

idle() {
  local s; s=$("$F" status $PC 2>&1)
  local ram cpu busy
  ram=$(echo "$s" | sed -n 's/^free_ram_gb=\([0-9.]*\).*/\1/p')
  cpu=$(echo "$s" | sed -n 's/^cpu_load_pct=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p')
  busy=$(echo "$s" | sed -n 's/^busy_procs=//p' | sed 's/ *SupercutMainCheckx1//')
  [ -z "$busy" ] && busy=none
  flag_on
  echo "$(date +%H:%M) ram=$ram cpu=$cpu busy=$busy"
  [ -z "$ram" ] && return 1
  case "$busy" in *Supercut*|*UnrealEditor*|*cl*|*link*|*dotnet*) return 1;; esac
  awk -v r="$ram" -v c="$cpu" 'BEGIN{exit !(r>=6 && c<60)}'
}
wait_idle() {
  for i in $(seq 1 90); do idle && return 0; sleep 60; done
  echo "WAIT_TIMEOUT"; return 1
}
step() { flag_on; echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) $*"; "$@"; local rc=$?; echo "=== exit $rc"; return $rc; }

wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" mirror $PC $NAME /d/UE/Projects/Supercut59 || exit 1
step "$F" build $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Jobs 8 || exit 2
wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" test $PC $NAME "$LOGS" || exit 3
grep -a "passed\|failed" "$LOGS/test/console.txt" | tail -3
wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" package $PC $NAME "$LOGS" || exit 4
wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" run $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Packaged

"""Deflate size of a folder as a zip would store it (level 6), without writing the zip. Usage: zipsize.py <folder>"""
import os, sys, zlib
root = sys.argv[1]; raw = 0; packed = 0; big = []
for d, _, fs in os.walk(root):
    for f in fs:
        p = os.path.join(d, f); c = zlib.compressobj(6, zlib.DEFLATED, -15); n = 0; z = 0
        with open(p, "rb") as h:
            while True:
                b = h.read(1 << 22)
                if not b: break
                n += len(b); z += len(c.compress(b))
        z += len(c.flush()); raw += n; packed += z + 120 + 2 * len(os.path.relpath(p, root)); big.append((z, n, f))
print("raw MB %.1f  zip MB %.1f  files %d" % (raw / 1048576, packed / 1048576, len(big)))
for z, n, f in sorted(big, reverse=True)[:6]:
    print("  %7.1f MB zipped  %7.1f MB raw  %s" % (z / 1048576, n / 1048576, f))
EOF
cat > "$S/scripts/ship_check.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash

grep -a "RUN wrapped" "$LOGS/run/run.log"
rm -rf "D:/UE/Builds/_from_farm/main_ship"
echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) fetch"; "$F" fetch pc2 sfx2 builds/Supercut59_ship/Windows "D:/UE/Builds/_from_farm/main_ship" | tail -1

#!/bin/bash
# Swaps the testers' copies (C:\SupercutPlaytest on [pc-c] and [pc-b]) to the fetched Shipping package. Keeps Play.bat and logs.
# Skips a PC where a Supercut process is running.
SRC="D:/UE/Builds/_from_farm/main_ship/Windows"
TAR="D:/UE/Builds/_from_farm/main_ship/ship.tar"
[ -f "$SRC/Supercut.exe" ] || { echo "no package at $SRC"; exit 1; }
rm -f "$TAR"; tar -cf "$TAR" -C "$SRC" . || exit 1
SUM=$(cksum < "$SRC/Supercut/Content/Paks/Supercut-Windows.ucas" | cut -d' ' -f2)
echo "local ucas bytes $SUM"
for pc in [pc-c] [pc-b]; do
  echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) $pc"
  n=$(ssh -o ConnectTimeout=20 $pc 'tasklist | find /i /c "supercut"' | tr -d '\r')
  [ "$n" = 0 ] || { echo "SKIP $pc: game running ($n)"; continue; }
  ssh $pc 'cmd /c "if exist C:\SupercutPlaytest_new rmdir /s /q C:\SupercutPlaytest_new & mkdir C:\SupercutPlaytest_new"' || continue
  scp -q "$TAR" "$pc:C:/SupercutPlaytest_new/ship.tar" || { echo "scp failed"; continue; }
  ssh $pc 'cmd /c "cd /d C:\SupercutPlaytest_new && tar -xf ship.tar && del ship.tar"' || { echo "untar failed"; continue; }
  n=$(ssh $pc 'tasklist | find /i /c "supercut"' | tr -d '\r')
  [ "$n" = 0 ] || { echo "SKIP $pc: game started meanwhile"; continue; }
  ssh $pc 'robocopy C:\SupercutPlaytest_new C:\SupercutPlaytest /MIR /XF Play.bat /XD logs /NFL /NDL /NP /NJH' | grep 'Files :\|Bytes :'
  ssh $pc 'cmd /c "rmdir /s /q C:\SupercutPlaytest_new & dir /b C:\SupercutPlaytest & for %I in (C:\SupercutPlaytest\Supercut\Content\Paks\Supercut-Windows.ucas) do @echo ucas bytes %~zI"'
done
rm -f "$TAR"; echo "DONE $(date +%H:%M)"
EOF
bash "$S/scripts/testers_swap.sh" > "$S/testers_swap.log" 2>&1; cut -c1-160 "$S/testers_swap.log"
```

**2. The black sides**

- **Cause:** generated and hand-made rooms get the same light from `BuildLight` (`SupercutRoom.cpp:94`; the `keylight` line builds nothing).

  - There is no sky light or ambient. The studio and hall walls are kept out of Lumen, so Lumen only bounces light off the floor. Exposure is fixed.
  - A face turned from both lights gets almost nothing. A white wall in shade still reads because it faces the fill and its paint reflects about three times more light than dark timber or charcoal cloth.
  - Nothing sits in the character, HUD or settings.
- **Fix:** an even grey sky light in `BuildLight`, built from a small cube texture made at run time (no asset to cook), with a new tuning value `AmbientLux` set to 0.3 `[taste: owner review]`.

  - Blanket's shadow side: 3.5 → 19.8 (this also includes the new grey cloth).
  - White wall's shade side: 87 → 105 (+21%), the limit issue above.
- **Other settings tried:** 0.6 lifts the flat to 27 but the white wall's shade side to 121. Swapping the fill for ambient made things worse.

  - At 1080p the game is limited by the CPU there, so those runs say little.
  - Not measured: the GTX 1070 (pc2 is your check PC), and the low preset with Lumen off.

#!/bin/bash
# Merge check of the main copy on pc2 (farm name sfx2). Waits until pc2 passes the load check, then
# mirror, build, test, package, scripted run, picture run, fetch. Usage: merge_check.sh [picture script name]
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
LOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs
PICLOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs_pics
PC=pc2
NAME=sfx2

# Priority flag: while it is fresh, status reports the PC as busy to every lane (farm/remote/status.ps1).
flag_on()  { ssh $PC "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"Set-Content -Path C:\\\\UE\\\\Farm\\\\_main_waiting -Value main\"" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
flag_off() { ssh $PC "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"Remove-Item C:\\\\UE\\\\Farm\\\\_main_waiting -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\"" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
trap flag_off EXIT

idle() {
  local s; s=$("$F" status $PC 2>&1)
  local ram cpu busy
  ram=$(echo "$s" | sed -n 's/^free_ram_gb=\([0-9.]*\).*/\1/p')
  cpu=$(echo "$s" | sed -n 's/^cpu_load_pct=\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p')
  busy=$(echo "$s" | sed -n 's/^busy_procs=//p' | sed 's/ *SupercutMainCheckx1//')
  [ -z "$busy" ] && busy=none
  flag_on
  echo "$(date +%H:%M) ram=$ram cpu=$cpu busy=$busy"
  [ -z "$ram" ] && return 1
  case "$busy" in *Supercut*|*UnrealEditor*|*cl*|*link*|*dotnet*) return 1;; esac
  awk -v r="$ram" -v c="$cpu" 'BEGIN{exit !(r>=6 && c<60)}'
}
wait_idle() {
  for i in $(seq 1 90); do idle && return 0; sleep 60; done
  echo "WAIT_TIMEOUT"; return 1
}
step() { flag_on; echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) $*"; "$@"; local rc=$?; echo "=== exit $rc"; return $rc; }

wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" mirror $PC $NAME /d/UE/Projects/Supercut59 || exit 1
step "$F" build $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Jobs 8 || exit 2
wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" test $PC $NAME "$LOGS" || exit 3
grep -a "passed\|failed" "$LOGS/test/console.txt" | tail -3
wait_idle || exit 90
```

#!/bin/bash
# Merge check of the main copy on pc2 (farm name sfx2). Waits until pc2 passes the load check, then
# mirror, build, test, package, scripted run, picture run, fetch. Usage: merge_check.sh [picture script name]
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
LOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs
PICLOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs_pics
PC=[pc-b]
NAME=hallmerge1

# Priority flag: while it is fresh, status reports the PC as busy to every lane (farm/remote/status.ps1).
flag_on()  { ssh $PC "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"Set-Content -Path C:\\\\UE\\\\Farm\\\\_main_waiting -Value main\"" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
flag_off() { ssh $PC "powershell -NoProfile -Command \"Remove-Item C:\\\\UE\\\\Farm\\\\_main_waiting -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\"" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" mirror $PC $NAME /d/UE/Projects/Supercut59 || exit 1
step "$F" build $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Jobs 8 || exit 2
wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" test $PC $NAME "$LOGS" || exit 3
grep -a "passed\|failed" "$LOGS/test/console.txt" | tail -3
wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" package $PC $NAME "$LOGS" || exit 4
wait_idle || exit 90
step "$F" run $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Packaged -Exe '{B}\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe' -Run main8 -Seed 1 -Script '{P}\Script\main8.txt' -FixedFps 240 -Silent -TimeoutSeconds 540
echo "run exit $?"
grep -a "RUN wrapped" "$LOGS/run/run.log"
if [ "$1" = gen ]; then
  wait_idle || exit 90
  step "$F" run $PC $NAME "$PICLOGS" -Packaged -Exe '{B}\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe' -Seed 6 -Script '{P}\Script\gen\s7.txt' -FixedFps 60 -Silent -TimeoutSeconds 540
  grep -a "RUN wrapped\|ROOM built" "$PICLOGS/run/run.log" | tail -4
elif [ -n "$1" ]; then
  wait_idle || exit 90
  step "$F" run $PC $NAME "$PICLOGS" -Packaged -Exe '{B}\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe' -Room fight/01_wind_machine -Dev -ResX 1920 -ResY 1080 -Script "{P}\\Script\\$1" -FixedFps 240 -Silent -TimeoutSeconds 540
  ls "$PICLOGS/run/shots" 2>/dev/null | head -40
fi
step "$F" fetch $PC $NAME builds/Supercut59/Windows "D:/UE/Builds/_from_farm/main"
echo "DONE $(date +%H:%M)"

## A merge during a farm check leaves a stale object that looks fresh (14 Nov 2026, verified)

The farm mirror keeps each file's modified time, so builds on the farm PC are incremental. That has a hole. I merged
lane gen2 into the main copy at 21:22:02 while the check of the previous commit was still packaging on pc2. Thirty-five
seconds later pc2 compiled the game target's `SupercutRoomFile.cpp.obj` from the OLD source. The next mirror sent the
new source with its 21:22:02 time, the build tool saw an object newer than its source and skipped it, and the game
target failed to link (`LNK2019 ... SupercutRoomFile::LoadRun`) while the editor target and all tests passed.
Rule: do not merge into the copy a check mirrors from until that check's package step has ended. Cure after the fact:
delete `Intermediate\Build\Win64\x64\UnrealGame\Development` in the farm copy and package again.

### Sun 15 Nov 09:34:03 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

The c4 trial earned its keep: the first attempt failed to compile here, though the same code builds on both farm PCs.

- **Cause:** c4 groups source files into build units differently from the farm PCs. In c4's grouping, a file-scope table named `Parts` in the enemy gun's file is hidden by local variables of the same name in two test files, and the compiler treats that as an error.
- **Fix:** I renamed the table (`EnemyGunParts`), committed it on main, and started the package again. More collisions of this kind may show up one build unit at a time; I fix each at its source until the package completes.

Nothing in the play folder changes from this. Lane clap2 is still working on [pc-b].

issues i noticed from a quick skim:
1. single taps fire 2 bullets one after another. the revolver is single fire, so no holding down for rapid fire or multi bullet firing.in the reference video, I was spam clicking,not holding down fire.
2. lava should be a pit - recessed deep into the ground, and slightly less thick so its easier to jump without being fully accurate
3. projectile tracers should come from the gun's muzzle, while shots actually cast from the player's camera center.
4. film stage environment: some issues here and there: examples [Image: {273551EE-D720-4D4C-8ACF-15FF37534BA3}.png; ref=image_ebbf6915-8cda-4c5b-b818-0212d1ef1583]  1. fill lamp's light rectangle bigger than its face mesh [Image: image.png; ref=image_24ef1b0d-f7b2-4d4f-bcbe-23e7f4fadefd]  2. scaffolding beams floating without connecting, floating spotlights that arent on a scaffolding beam and so on
5. bullet impact yellow flash - its a circle. dont use simple shapes and use proper vfx or textures, bullet holes in the walls as well. right now they are black circles
6. clapperboard animation looks wrong. i said to mirror my reference video, but the clapperboard's arm hinge is on the right side ingame when if mirrored, it should be on the left edge of the clapperboard, I think the mirror translation had issues
7. reloading shell ejection, while jumping , they hang in the player's view  - shouldnt happen, they should ignore physics and always travel down instead of trying to follow the player's physics
8. level design - I cant tell if this is the procedural variant yet, but if it is, this isnt exactly correct. it still feels very linear and uninteresting, mainly because its a straight line to the finish  always regardless, there are no actual rooms, bends and so on, and all the levels are short. I feel like after the first 2 stages they need to be more winding and have doorways and such to give it some atmosphere and challenge, so the limited clapperboards also feel more like a challenge. right now every stage is so short that clapperboards dont really matter, every level can be outnavigated with the use of 1 or 0 clapperboards, so the fix would be to make later stages longer.
9. the FONT. shortlist me a selection of fonts, nothing too weird looking, one for important text like hero, header,title stuff, and one for description text. for hero text, i am leaning more towards [a shooter the owner likes] and [a game named for its font style] and [other-app]'s styles, and for description/misc text i am ok with the current font, but also show me a selection, and also from the 3 games I mentioned, the closest possible ones to all that are usable (free commercial use)

[a game named for its card layout] augments - so its a card with text and an icon. for the icons, try imagegen and show me.
11. clapperboard counter should be centered bottom on the screen, not next to the health bar. and they should be imagegen icons not  a bunch of squares. healthbar styling too, more like the reference, right now it just looks like a placeholder
12. finish gates should be a proper doorway. fab or cc0 realistic doorway, preferably like a fire exit, and the signal shoudlnt be it turning red to green, but the door swinging open, and be extremely bright white behind it, so its easy to transition to the next room - [Image: image.png; ref=image_2a2ea094-280a-4d20-8d0c-03bf7eec7cf2]  like this.

All the shared rules moved into one file that every brief points at, because I had been\npasting the same forty lines into each brief and they had started to drift apart.\n\nThree things in those briefs are my calls, not his, and are marked for his review: stages 1 and 2 stay short and\nfrom stage 3 on a stage is three to six chambers with at least two right-angle turns and a finish that cannot\nbe seen from the start; the winding-key sound covers the last 1.2 seconds of a freeze; the exit door is worn\ngrey-blue with a lit green sign that has no words.\n\nOne instruction I gave the fire-input lane that is worth recording: the scripted reference runs were recorded\nwith the double-fire fault in them, so fixing it may change their result lines. If it does, the lane writes down\nwhich shots doubled and tells me before anything is re-recorded. A reference that silently changes is no\nreference.\n\nThe effects work would normally go to the stronger model. Its weekly allowance is used up on the helper\naccounts, so that lane runs on the usual one with the studio's effect rules written into its brief (four painted\nlayers, no default particle sprites, no hard-edged ray fans). The owner judges the look either way.\n\nThe feature stop moves from 15:00 to about 19:00. That is the cost of taking all thirteen notes.\n\n**The first-session check finished.** It played the build as a new player would and found one thing I count as a\nreal fault: an upgrade card that names the wrong key and stays on screen for about two minutes. Its smaller\nfinds (a key hint over the health number, the gate's green light flooding the upgrade and wrap screens, a title\nover a slate) went to the interface lane. It also fixed four picture scripts whose clicks had drifted off their\nmenu rows. Those are in the main copy as a scripts-only merge, with no build check run, because no code changed.\n\n**The owner placed the gun himself.** The reference match has been the stubborn part of this game: two lanes\nmeasured the reference and the game still did not look like it. This morning he opened the posing file and moved\nthe gun by hand until it matched his still. Read back from the file: 25.77 cm forward of the eye, 9.89 right,\n7.68 down, turned 4.22 degrees. The turn is the finding. Our study of the reference had said the barrel was\nparallel to the view, and every placement since was built on that. It is turned about four degrees, which is\nwhat shows the back of the gun so well. The wrong line is corrected in the study.\n\nI did not paste his three distances into the code. The game's home constant and the figure the art thread gave\nfor \"today's home\" differ by about 11 cm, so the two files measure from different points on the gun. The lane\ntakes his sight positions on screen as the target (front sight 60.2% across and 55.2% down, rear 65.0% and\n59.1%), solves the home from those, and compares with his distances. If the two disagree by more than 1.5 cm it\nstops and reports. Then it re-checks what hangs off the home: the near plane, the view against a wall, the kick,\nthe reload, the muzzle flash, the clap.\n\n**Not done.** No build has changed since the morning. The current main copy has not been through the test suite\non a farm PC since its last code merge; the next merge check covers that. Sixteen lanes share two farm PCs, so\ntheir builds queue. The credits still show a placeholder where the team's names go.\n"

# font1 handoff (15 Nov 2026)

Font shortlist for SUPERCUT. No game code touched. Results and picks: `FONTS.md`.

## Re-run

From `lanes/font1/`:

- `python -I tools/fetch_fonts.py <folder> ...` downloads families from github.com/google/fonts into `fonts/<folder>/` with `OFL.txt` and `SOURCE.txt`.
- `python -I tools/make_sheets.py` redraws the four PNGs in `out/` and 960-wide JPG slices in `shots/`. It prints "0 layout problems" per sheet when no text box leaves its region, leaves the canvas or overlaps another.
- `python -I tools/write_fonts_md.py` rewrites `FONTS.md` (sizes, URLs and glyph check come from the files).

## Gotchas

- Italic fonts start their ink left of the pen position; `Layout.text` shifts x by the ink's left edge so nothing pokes out of a card.
- Pillow here has no Raqm, so kerning is basic.
- Glyph check compares each character with the font's missing-glyph box; proven by a Chinese character (missing everywhere) and a Thai letter (present only in Kanit).
- Not checked: how UE 5.9 handles variable font files.

#!/bin/bash
# farm.sh: build, test, package and run a SUPERCUT project copy on a farm PC, driven from c4. Details: ../FARM.md.
#
#   farm.sh mirror  <host> <name> <project folder on c4>     copy the project to <root>\Farm\<name> (changed files only)
#   farm.sh build   <host> <name> <log folder> [build.ps1 args, e.g. -Target Supercut -Jobs 8]
#   farm.sh test    <host> <name> <log folder> [run_tests.ps1 args, e.g. -Filter Supercut.Rooms]
#   farm.sh package <host> <name> <log folder>               Tools\package.cmd   -> <root>\Farm\_builds\<name>\Supercut59
#   farm.sh package-shipping <host> <name> <log folder>      Tools\package_shipping.cmd -> ...\_builds\<name>\Supercut59_ship
#   farm.sh run     <host> <name> <log folder> [run_demo.ps1 args]   {P} = the mirror folder there, e.g. -Script {P}\Script\main8.txt
#   farm.sh fetch   <host> <name> <remote path> <local folder>   path in the mirror, or builds/... or out/...
#   farm.sh status  <host>
#
# Each step brings its logs back to <log folder>/<step>/ and exits with the remote step's exit code.
# Logs that come back have the PC's user and computer names replaced by USER and PC.
set -u
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)

root_of() {   # one line per farm PC: ssh alias, root folder there (engine in <root>\UE_5.9, mirrors in <root>\Farm)
  case "$1" in
    [pc-b]) echo 'C:\UE' ;;
    pc2)    echo 'C:\UE' ;;
    [pc-c])   echo 'F:\UE' ;;
    pc4)    echo 'C:\UE' ;;
    *) echo "FARM unknown host '$1' ([pc-b], pc2, [pc-c], pc4)" >&2; exit 64 ;;
  esac
}
fwd() { echo "${1//\\//}"; }   # C:\UE -> C:/UE for scp and tar

# copy remote path $2 (forward slashes) from host $1 into local folder $3, masking user and computer names in text files
pull() {
  local host=$1 src=$2 dst=$3 un cn
  mkdir -p "$dst"
  scp -r -q "$host:$src" "$dst/" || return 1
  un=$(ssh "$host" 'echo %USERNAME%' | tr -d '\r\n'); cn=$(ssh "$host" 'echo %COMPUTERNAME%' | tr -d '\r\n')
  find "$dst" -type f \( -name '*.log' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.ini' -o -name '*.csv' \) -print0 |
    xargs -0 -r sed -i -e "s#$un#USER#Ig" -e "s#$cn#PC#Ig"
}

step() {   # step <name of step> <host> <name> <log folder> [args...]
  local s=$1 host=$2 name=$3 logs=$4; shift 4
  local root; root=$(root_of "$host") || exit $?
  local af=''
  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
    af="$root\\Farm\\_out\\$name.$s.args.txt"
    local tmp; tmp=$(mktemp)
    printf '%s\r\n' "$@" > "$tmp"
    ssh "$host" "if not exist $root\\Farm\\_out mkdir $root\\Farm\\_out" && scp -q "$tmp" "$host

My pc2 step (main8_b) finished and its output is on c4. Nothing of mine is running or waiting on pc2, and I deleted my scheduled task there.

I changed no code or content. The worktree `D:\UE\wt\perf3` is clean at eec7dd4, and every pc2 number was taken at 16 GB, before the memory change.

**1. The 24 errors are harmless, and I left them.**
- **What they are:** I worked this out from the engine source; I didn't get to the check on pc2 that would match each logged hash to a shader name.
  - At start-up the engine pre-builds pipelines for two TSR upscaler shaders in their 16-bit form, on every card.
  - Those are `FTSRDecimateHistoryCS` (16 versions) and `FTSRUpdateHistoryCS` (8 versions), which makes 24.
  - The GTX 1070 has no native 16-bit shader maths, so the driver refuses all 24.
- **Why it's safe:** a failed pipeline the game actually used would crash it (`PipelineStateCache.cpp:722`), and every pc2 run went to the end. On this card TSR uses its 32-bit shaders.
- **Pictures:** I compared 65 shots from the same script on pc2 and on [pc-b].
  - Nothing is missing on pc2: shadows, Lumen light, reflections, sky, the sketch look, effects and upscaling are all there.
  - pc2 is slightly brighter in lit rooms, by 4 to 9 levels out of 255. [taste: owner review]
- **Why I didn't remove them:** it would take an engine change we can't build, or a setting that turns off pre-building for every card and adds stutter on good ones.

**2. Frame rate is under 16.7 ms everywhere, so I changed nothing.** All runs were at default settings (HIGH from the benchmark, 1920x1080), with pc2 to myself.

| Place | Average | Slowest 1% |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hand-made run | 12.5 ms | 21.6 ms |
| Hall | 14.2 ms | 15.1 ms |
| Heaviest generated room (d08), fight | 13.2 ms | 33.7 ms |

- TSR is the biggest GPU cost, at 3.7 ms.
- The first run (13.96 ms) had pc2's [another platform] Studio windows open on the GPU and only 4 GB free RAM, so I marked it and ran it again.
- I discarded one run because another lane's game started during it.

**3. First launch has one hitch.** Within the first minute from the title, the only frame over 50 ms is the first title frame, at 0.24 s. It's the same on a warm start. Room changes cost 22 to 36 ms.
- A pipeline cache shipped with the package is the supported 5.9 way to fix that frame. The steps and source lines are in the handoff.
- I didn't try it because pc2 went down. It would only remove that one frame before play starts, and the warm run suggests it might not remove all of it. My call is that it's not worth doing before submission. [taste: owner review]

- The pipeline cache experiment.

**6. Firewall prompt on a dev build.** The prompt comes from the engine's trace listener, which opens TCP port 1985 in every Development build. I read the 5.9 source: the listener is compiled in whenever tracing is, and I found no command line switch or setting that turns it off at run time. Removing it means compiling the game with tracing off, which is untested on our installed engine and a risk this close to the deadline. Two workable answers:
- Ship a Shipping build. It has no listener, so no prompt. The jam page says "We recommend a development build for all platforms" and also "Shipping builds are also accepted for Windows, macOS, and Android." This is my recommendation and what the submission sheet now says.
- Ship Development and accept the prompt. It is harmless, the game runs whichever button the judge presses, but it is the first thing a judge sees.

52:take_ubt() {   # take_ubt <host> <name> <step>
119:  case "$s" in build|package|package-shipping) take_ubt "$host" "$name" "$s" ;; esac
take_ubt() {   # take_ubt <host> <name> <step>
  local host=$1 name=$2 s=$3 d pid t now waited=0
  mkdir -p "$lockdir"; d="$lockdir/$host.ubt"
  while :; do
    if mkdir "$d" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "$$ $name $s $(date +%s) $(date +%H:%M:%S)" > "$d/owner"
      ubt=$d; trap 'rm -rf "$slot" "$ubt"' EXIT
      [ "$waited" -gt 0 ] && echo "FARM waited ${waited}s for the compiler on $host" >&2
      return 0
    fi
    if [ -f "$d/owner" ]; then
      read -r pid _ _ t _ < "$d/owner"; now=$(date +%s)
      if [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && { [ ! -d "/proc/$pid" ] || [ $((now - ${t:-now})) -gt 3600 ]; }; then rm -rf "$d"; fi
    fi
    [ "$waited" -eq 0 ] && echo "FARM another lane is compiling on $host; this $s waits its turn" >&2
    sleep 15; waited=$((waited + 15))
  done
}
take_slot() {   # take_slot <host> <name> <step>: returns when this process holds a slot on the host

**What I need from you:** two static font files with the OFL name table kept and the family names unchanged.
- `Exo2-BlackItalic.ttf`, made from `Exo2-Italic[wght].ttf` at wght 900.
- `Saira-Regular.ttf`, made from `Saira[wdth,wght].ttf` at wght 400, wdth 100.

Put them in `lanes\font1\fonts\exo2\` and `lanes\font1\fonts\saira\`, or anywhere you tell me.

**Why the variable files won't work**
- UE 5.9 only ever draws a variable font at its default instance. Its sub-face list counts only the faces in the file, never named instances (FontCacheFreeType.cpp:538-563), and the importer makes a single typeface (EditorFactories.cpp:5326).
- The defaults are Exo 2 Italic at weight 400 and Saira Thin, so neither would look like the pick.
- UE's FreeType 2.14.1 does support variable fonts (ftoption.h:738). But the field that would select a named instance, `FFontData::SubFaceIndex`, is a bare `UPROPERTY()` (CompositeFont.h:282). Python and the font editor can't set it. Poking it from C++ at load is too hacky to ship, so I didn't.
- fontTools is not installed in any Python I may use: c4 (its own Pythons plus UE 5.9's and 5.8's), [pc-c], pc2 and pc4. pc3 didn't answer ssh.

I fixed it: the dark flats and blanket stands ahead of the start now read as panels from the start view, and the dark hall is unchanged. pc2 frame time is the one check not done, because pc2 was shut down for a memory upgrade before my build there started. Commit `82204f7` is on branch `light2` and the worktree is clean.

**Cause.** The warm lamp stands behind and to the left of the room's middle. In 216 of the 600 baked rooms the generator puts a flat or blanket stand 2 to 9 m straight ahead of the start, so the player sees its shaded side, at 19 to 34 out of 255. The materials are in a normal range, so I left them alone.

**Change.** The room code now places a soft white light 150 cm behind and 350 cm above the start, aimed 5 m ahead at eye height. It casts no shadow, and its reach ends at the far corner of the set, so the hall stays dark. It comes with four new tuning lines: `StartFillLux` 0.3, `StartFillBack` 150 cm, `StartFillHeight` 350 cm, `StartFillSize` 200 cm. All four values are [taste: owner review].

**Why not ambient alone.** At `AmbientLux` 1.0 the shaded flats only reached 35 to 57, and the hall went from 9 to 29.

**Results** (all on c4, before and after from the same PC):

| What | Target | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shaded flat or blanket stand | 45 to 80 | 19 to 34 | 51 to 82 |
| Brightest wall (99.5% point) | under 245 | | 227 at most |
| Lit to shaded | 2:1 or more | | 2.1:1 at the lowest |
| Hall | stays dark | 9 | 9 |

Two flats land at 81 and 82, one or two over the 45 to 80 band. I kept 0.3 rather than tuning it lower for that.

| --- | --- |

| `missing usage flag` | 0 in every run log |

The first two package tries failed in 0 s because another lane's package was running on c4's second slot and the engine only lets one packager run at a time. The third try passed. This is not the C1001 trap; the fix is to wait a minute and retry.

**Fight, freeze and muzzle flash, before and after**

- **Signal colours** (red frame, yellow line, CUT text): within 3 levels.

**The one 250 ms gap:** last night's video measurement found a single 250 ms gap between shots. It was counted by eye in a stretch with dropped frames and contradicts the 140 a minute figure, so I treated it as a miscount. If you know the gun can fire faster than that, tell me.

- The shot's settle now matches the reference curve directly: about 600 ms, with a 22% dip below rest. It no longer needs squeezing into a 0.18 s cadence.

**Not changed, and what that means:**
- **Damage and enemies are untouched.** The reference's 74 damage only means something against that game's health pools. The exit door is in and every required check passes on the final package (commit `8af66fb` on branch `door1`). The worktree is clean.

**What it does**
- While a stage is locked, the old red disc and frame are replaced by a grey-blue fire door standing in a film-set flat. The door was built by us in Blender, because neither Poly Haven nor the asset sets on disk had a fire door.
- When the gate opens, the door swings 100° toward the player over 0.6 s, easing out with about a 4 % overshoot. Behind it is emissive white that blooms, and a spot light throws a white patch onto the floor.
- The green exit sign is lit all the time. Its doorway-and-arrow picture is drawn in code, with no words.
- The gate's place, size, trigger and timing are unchanged, and nothing of the door has collision.

**What the game shows after the white**
- Before this lane, reaching the gate went straight to the upgrade screen, or the wrap screen on the last room. There is no loading card between rooms.
- Now the screen goes white in 150 ms and the upgrade or wrap screen draws over it, so the white reads as grey behind the cards.
- After a pick, the next room comes up from white over 0.4 s. When every upgrade is already held, it cuts to white and then fades the same way. So yes, it can start from white, and now it does.

**Checks on the final package**
- **Package:** passed on the first try, 0 `Failed to compile Material`.
- **Tests:** 242 passed, 0 failed, including 3 new door tests: the door is shut while locked and open after, the trigger is where it was, and only the sign is in a signal colour.
- **main8, run twice:** both printed `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17`.
- **Generated run (seed 6, s7):** printed `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 144.8 s, shots 54, freezes 16, kills 26`.
- **Usage flags:** 0 `missing usage flag` in all six run logs.

**Tests whose expectations changed**
- The puzzle tests used to check that the gate turned red then green. They now check the door angle, because the gate has no colour any more.
- The soundstage fixture listed 54 pieces and now lists 66: the gate's 4 parts became the door's 16.

**Pictures** (7 sheets in `lanes/door1/shots/`):
- ![shut, 15 m and 3 m](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/door1/shots/door1_shut_15m_3m.jpg>)

**Taste calls** [taste: owner review]
- The white is at strength 4 and the light at 4000 cd. My first values, 12 and 20000, washed the whole end of the room out to white.
- The worn grey-blue paint and the size and look of the sign.

**For the owner to decide**

- The scene/take card and the ammo row draw over the door in the close pictures. That is 2D over 3D, so I'm listing it, not calling it a defect.

From the owner (relayed by another c4 thread at the owner's request, 15 Nov ~14:55): rethink Development vs Shipping for the submitted zip.

Owner's point: Epic recommends Development builds, so judges will see the trace listener's firewall prompt on most UE entries. It is expected engine behaviour and should not count against us. The prompt alone is not a reason to ship Shipping.

Facts measured 14:53 on c4:
- Play folder D:\UE\Builds\Supercut59_play (Development): 1,442 MB raw, ~802 MB as a deflate zip (python zlib level 6 per file, estimate, no zip written). A Dev zip alone fits under 1 GB.
- Dev + Shipping in one zip is ~1.38 GB (802 + your 582 MB Shipping figure): over the 1 GB cap, so not as one zip. Two separate itch uploads: no rule found either way, and it hands judges a choice. Not recommended.

Recommendation (owner said yes to sending this; the call is yours to bring back to them): submit ONE Development zip, as Epic recommends, after two checks on the Development build:
1. Dev-only features a judge could trigger: Tuning.txt being read, the practice keys, the -SupercutRecord path, any on-screen debug text, the ~ console. Confirm a judge can't trigger them by accident, or turn them off in the submitted build.
2. Test/demo rooms and loose WAVs ("Shipping clean" item in GAME.md) are out of the Development package too.
If either check fails and there's no time to fix it, Shipping stays. Upside of Dev: it writes a log if a judge crashes. Update SUBMISSION.md lines 15 and 37-39 to match whichever build is picked, and re-run the ports check only if the pick stays Shipping.

/** The game module. Its one job of its own: "-SupercutWriteTuning" writes Tuning.example.txt and quits before a window opens. */
class FSupercutModule : public FDefaultGameModuleImpl
{
public:
	virtual void StartupModule() override
	{
#if UE_BUILD_SHIPPING
		// -UseFixedTimeStep is read in every build, but -FPS= only outside Shipping (LaunchEngineLoop.cpp). A scripted
		// Shipping run needs the same fixed step as the Development one, so the game reads it here.
		float Fps = 0.f;
		if (FParse::Value(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("-FPS="), Fps) && Fps > 0.f)
		{
			FApp::SetFixedDeltaTime(1.0 / Fps);
		}
#endif
		if (!FParse::Param(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("SupercutWriteTuning")))
		{
			return;
		}
		const FString Path = SupercutTuningFile::TemplatePath();
		const bool bWritten = FFileHelper::SaveStringToFile(SupercutTuningFile::WriteTemplate(FSupercutTuning()), *Path);
		if (bWritten)
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("TUNING template written to %s"), *Path);
		}
		else
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Error, TEXT("TUNING template could not be written to %s"), *Path);
---GM

void ASupercutGameMode::InitGame(const FString& MapName, const FString& Options, FString& ErrorMessage)
{
	Super::InitGame(MapName, Options, ErrorMessage);

Both jobs are fixed. Every check passed: the build, all tests, the package, both reference runs, and the picture strips for the four cases. No farm step of mine is running, and the worktree is clean at `51033ee`.

**Job 1, one click fired two shots. Cause:** `SupercutPlayerController.cpp:248` (ReadKeys) set the fire input from whether the button was held. So `SupercutCharacter.cpp:383` tried to fire on every frame of a press. Once the cooldown fell to the 0.12 s buffer window, the refused try at `SupercutCharacter.cpp:753` buffered a shot from that same press, and Tick (`:434`) fired it at 180 ms. Any click of 60 ms or more fired twice.

**Job 1 fix:** ReadKeys now passes the press itself (`WasActionJustPressed`). As a side effect, a press let go inside one frame now fires; before, it was lost.

**Where the two input paths meet:**
- The real mouse goes through `GameViewportClient.cpp:799` to `APlayerController::InputKey` (`PlayerController.cpp:2415`). The new tests call that same `InputKey`.
- Scripted `fire` lines set the input directly (`SupercutPlayerController.cpp:637`).
- Both meet at `Hero->ApplyInput` in `ASupercutPlayerController::PlayerTick`. That is why the reference runs never double fired, and their lines did not move.

**Job 2, shells hung in view during a jump.** The cause was at `SupercutCharacter.cpp:839`: each shell started with the player's velocity but fell at 700 against the player's 1960. So in a jump the shell climbed up the screen. The fix attaches the shells to the camera, and they fall down the view in the camera's own space. Landing still traces in the world. There is no landing sound, so there was no sound timing to keep.

**Checks (red tests on pc2; the rest on [pc-c] after pc2's disk filled):**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New tests on the old code | 2 of 3 failed. Presses of 100 and 200 ms fired 2 shots; at jump start a shell climbed the screen and stayed visible up to 0.84 s. |
| Build | passes |
| All tests | 242 pass, 0 fail (239 + 3 new), none loosened or changed |
| One press of each length (a single frame, 50, 100, 200, 400 ms, a 2 s hold) at 30/60/144/240 fps | 1 shot each |
| 10 presses at the gun's rate / at twice its rate | 10 shots / one shot per rate interval, never two on one press |
| Shells, all four cases | always below the bottom edge by 0.254 s at worst, never move up |
| Development package | 0 `Failed to compile Material` |
| main8, twice | `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17` both times |
| gen s7 | `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 144.8 s, shots 54, freezes 16, kills 26` |
| Run logs | 0 `missing usage flag`, 0 compute pipeline errors |

**Pictures:** In all four strips the shells only go down, and they leave the screen by +133 to +200 ms.
- My first picture run was mistimed: the eject comes 0.183 s after the reload line, so the jump cases ejected at the wrong moments. I moved those lines (commit `51033ee`, script only) and re-ran it.
- What's wrong in them: at jump start the gun dips with the jump and hides the shells for two frames, so the drop reads less clearly there [taste: owner review]. A crop near the gun shows the shells are there.

**Not checked:**
- There are no "before" picture strips. The failing shell test gives the before numbers instead.
- During a freeze, shells hang in the world as they did before, so a player who jumps inside a freeze sees them move on screen [taste: owner review].
- At 30 fps the gun's real fire rate is one shot per 0.2 s, not 0.18 s. This was already there before my change.

### Sun 15 Nov 15:39:30 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

The check of the merged head failed one test of 252. I fixed it on main and a new check is running on [pc-c].

- **What failed:** the set lane's lamp test (`Supercut.Set.EveryLampGlowsInsideItsHousing`) found two spot lights in each of the eight hand-made rooms where it expects one.

The new check covers the lighting, set, exit door, clap and double-shot changes. The build goes to your play folder when it passes.

raw=open(p,encoding="utf-8",newline="").read(); nl="\r\n" if "\r\n" in raw else "\n"
c=raw.split(nl)

old=c[a:b+1]; assert all(', CC0' in x for x in old), old
print("old",len(old),"removed:",sorted(set(old)-set(cred)),"added:",sorted(set(cred)-set(old)))
c[a:b+1]=cred
open(p,"w",encoding="utf-8",newline="").write(nl.join(c))
# SUBMISSION
p2="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/SUBMISSION.md"
raw=open(p2,encoding="utf-8",newline="").read(); nl="\r\n" if "\r\n" in raw else "\n"
s=raw.split(nl)
idx=[i for i,l in enumerate(s) if "Cut into the game sound" in l and l.startswith("|")]
print("submission sound rows",len(idx),idx[0],idx[-1], idx[-1]-idx[0]+1)
assert idx[-1]-idx[0]+1==len(idx)
oldn=[l.split("|")[1].strip().split('"')[1] for l in s[idx[0]:idx[-1]+1]]
newn=[l.split("|")[1].strip().split('"')[1] for l in rows]
print("rows removed:",sorted(set(oldn)-set(newn)),"added:",sorted(set(newn)-set(oldn)))
s[idx[0]:idx[-1]+1]=rows
open(p2,"w",encoding="utf-8",newline="").write(nl.join(s))
EOF

rem Packages the Windows Development build with UE 5.9 to D:\UE\Builds\Supercut59. The log goes to Saved\Logs\package_run.log.

local host=$1 src=$2 dst=$3 un cn
  mkdir -p "$dst"
  if is_local "$host"; then
    cp -r "$src" "$dst/" || return 1
    un=${USERNAME:-}; cn=${COMPUTERNAME:-}
  else
    scp -r -q "$host:$src" "$dst/" || return 1
    un=$(ssh "$host" 'echo %USERNAME%' | tr -d '\r\n'); cn=$(ssh "$host" 'echo %COMPUTERNAME%' | tr -d '\r\n')
  fi
  [ -n "$un" ] && [ -n "$cn" ] || return 0
  find "$dst" -type f \( -name '*.log' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.ini' -o -name '*.csv' \) -print0 |
    xargs -0 -r sed -i -e "s#$un#USER#Ig" -e "s#$cn#PC#Ig"
}

step() {   # step <name of step> <host> <name> <log folder> [args...]
  local s=$1 host=$2 name=$3 logs=$4; shift 4
  local root; root=$(root_of "$host") || exit $?
  case "$s" in build|package|package-shipping) take_ubt "$host" "$name" "$s" ;; esac
  take_slot "$host" "$name" "$s"
  local af=''
  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
    af="$root\\Farm\\_out\\$name.$s.args.txt"
    local tmp; tmp=$(mktemp)
    printf '%s\r\n' "$@" > "$tmp"
    if is_local "$host"; then
      mkdir -p "$(fwd "$root")/Farm/_out" && cp "$tmp" "$(fwd "$af")" || exit 1
    else
      ssh "$host" "if not exist $root\\Farm\\_out mkdir $root\\Farm\\_out" && scp -q "$tmp" "$host:$(fwd "$af")" || exit 1
    fi
    rm -f "$tmp"
  fi
  local code
  if is_local "$host"; then
    if [ -n "$af" ]; then
      powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$root\\Farm\\_farm\\step.ps1" -Root "$root" -Name "$name" -Step "$s" -ArgsFile "$af"
    else
      powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$root\\Farm\\_farm\\step.ps1" -Root "$root" -Name "$name" -Step "$s"
    fi
    code=$?
  else
    ssh "$host" "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $root\\Farm\\_farm\\step.ps1 -Root $root -Name $name -Step $s ${af:+-ArgsFile $af}"
    code=$?
  fi
  rm -rf "${logs:?}/$s"
  pull "$host" "$(fwd "$root")/Farm/_out/$name/$s" "$logs" || echo "FARM could not fetch the logs of $s" >&2
  exit $code
}

verb=${1:-}; [ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
del.ps1
list.ps1
status.ps1
step.ps1
tree.ps1
vs_install.ps1

slot=''

# UnrealBuildTool runs one at a time per engine copy, and a package that meets another lane's build fails
# (exit 10, 15 Nov 14:04 on [pc-c]). So build, package and package-shipping also hold <lockdir>/<host>.ubt.
take_ubt() {   # take_ubt <host> <name> <step>
  local host=$1 name=$2 s=$3 d pid t now waited=0
  mkdir -p "$lockdir"; d="$lockdir/$host.ubt"
  # The main copy's merge check goes first: while <host>.ubt.first names a live process, other lanes do not try.
  local first="$lockdir/$host.ubt.first" fp
  [ "$name" = maincheck ] && echo "$$" > "$first"
  while :; do
    fp=''; [ -f "$first" ] && read -r fp < "$first"
    if [ -n "$fp" ] && [ ! -d "/proc/$fp" ]; then rm -f "$first"; fp=''; fi
    if [ -n "$fp" ] && [ "$name" != maincheck ]; then
      [ "$waited" -eq 0 ] && echo "FARM the main copy's check compiles next on $host; this $s waits its turn" >&2
      sleep 15; waited=$((waited + 15)); continue
    fi
    if mkdir "$d" 2>/dev/null; then
      [ "$name" = maincheck ] && rm -f "$first"
      echo "$$ $name $s $(date +%s) $(date +%H:%M:%S)" > "$d/owner"
      ubt=$d; trap 'rm -rf "$slot" "$ubt"' EXIT
      [ "$waited" -gt 0 ] && echo "FARM waited ${waited}s for the compiler on $host" >&2
      return 0
    fi
    if [ -f "$d/owner" ]; then
      read -r pid _ _ t _ < "$d/owner"; now=$(date +%s)
      if [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && { [ ! -d "/proc/$pid" ] || [ $((now - ${t:-now})) -gt 3600 ]; }; then rm -rf "$d"; fi
    fi
    [ "$waited" -eq 0 ] && echo "FARM another lane is compiling on $host; this $s waits its turn" >&2
    sleep 15; waited=$((waited + 15))
  done
}
take_slot() {   # take_slot <host> <name> <step>: returns when this process holds a slot on the host
  local host=$1 name=$2 s=$3 n i d pid t now waited=0 order
  n=$(slots_of "$host"); mkdir -p "$lockdir"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Export the transcripts and commit the log. Usage: bash tools/sync.sh "what happened"
# The push is a separate step (see the README) so nothing leaves this PC unread.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
python -I tools/export_transcripts.py
python -I tools/leak_scan.py
git add -A
git commit -q -m "${1:?give a commit message}" && git log --oneline -1

ok
15 Nov 16:02
**Two rules from the owner.** The gameplay video does not start when the features stop. It starts when he
says so. And the dev log is to be checked for anything that breaks a jam rule before anyone outside reads it.
A read-only lane (logaudit1) is doing that now against the official rules: perk codes, private data, other
projects, other games' names, licences, and statements that later entries proved false.

**The firewall prompt.** A Development build asks Windows for network access on its first start. The owner
asked how to stop that. I read the engine source: the prompt comes from the trace system's control listener on
TCP port 1985, which is compiled in whenever tracing is and is polled with no run-time switch that I could
find. The choices are a Shipping build, which has no listener and which the jam page accepts for Windows, or a
compile with tracing off, which nobody here has tried on an installed engine. I recommended Shipping.

**One farm PC is out for the rest of the jam.** The second developer said his PC was laggy and asked whether
our lanes were the cause. Nothing of ours was running on it. The system log showed the cause: the main drive
stalls and Windows resets it. 51 resets since the PC's last start, the worst recorded write took 65 seconds,
and there were 1 to 6 resets a day for ten days before the jam work began. In the hour our eight lanes ran
there it logged 37. So the drive was already failing and our load made it worse. The two restarts this morning
fit a hung drive. I closed that PC to the farm with a marker file the queue script reads, and told the owner
to back the drive up.

**The farm script learned two more things.** A second lock per PC now lets only one compile run at a time,
after a package failed against another lane's build. And a PC can be closed: running steps finish, new ones
wait. The small farm PC is closed too, empty, until the owner has added memory to it.

**Where the lanes are.** Ten lanes are building, testing or packaging on two PCs with five slots between them.
My estimate to the owner: the first batch merged and playable by about 15:30, everything merged by about
17:30, then his play and a round of fixes.

**Not done.** No new build has reached the owner's play folder today. The gun's motions were tuned for the old
rest place and look about twice as big at the new one; they need a pass. The hands have not been shot at the
new rest place.

I rewrote what they assert, to\nthe owner's rule: the named parts may leave the screen, and nothing that leaves it may be seen from the eye.\n\n**The gun's timing.** The owner asked for the fire rate and reload speed of the reference shooter's revolver.\nThe motion lane measured them from his recording and set ours to match: 0.428 s between shots (was 0.18), a\n2.25 s reload (was 1.0), 0.31 s before an empty gun reloads by itself (was 0.2), and a 0.75 s draw. With those\nnumbers both scripted runs die. The scripts fire every 0.25 to 0.3 s, so the gun now refuses half their shots.\nThat is the scripts' problem, but the same arithmetic holds for a player: fewer bullets per second against the\nsame enemies. My call, marked for the owner's review: the Grunt goes from 3 health to 2 and the Rusher from 2\nto 1. The Marksman stays at 2, which keeps the SLOW BURN upgrade worth taking. Enemy damage, player health and\nthe clapperboard are untouched. This is on the motion lane's branch and not merged yet.\n\n**Merged since 14:26.** The home screen, the lighting pass, the set dressing, the exit door, the clapperboard\nfixes, the gun fixes and the owner's three sound picks. The first four reached the owner's play folder at\n15:32 as one build (242 tests, both scripted runs unchanged). The rest are in a build that is being checked\nnow.\n\n- The double shot the owner reported had one cause: the key reader passed \"held\" where the gun expected \"just\n  pressed\", so a click that lasted two frames fired twice. One click now fires one shot.\n- Spent shells are attached to the camera, so they no longer smear when the player turns.\n- The clapperboard's burst of chips vanished during a freeze. The freeze draws the scene as a pencil sketch\n  from the depth buffer, and translucent sprites write no depth. The fix is masked materials, which do. The\n  effects lane is testing its tracer, impact and muzzle effects in a freeze for the same reason.\n\n**A test that counted the wrong thing.** The merged build failed 1 of 252 tests: \"every lamp glows inside its\nhousing\" found two lamp lights in all eight hand-made rooms. The set lane's test counted every spot light in\na room, and the door lane had just given the exit door a spot light of its own. Both lanes passed alone. The\ntest now takes the spot light attached to the room's root, which is the lamp.\n\n**A package that failed said it passed.** The check of that build printed `step=package exit=0 secs=10`. A\npackage takes minutes. The log showed the build tool had crashed on a file another copy of itself held open,\nand returned a negative exit code. Our package script tested the result with `if errorlevel 1`, which is true\nfor 1 and above, so a negative code went through as success. I stopped the check before it ran the game from\nthe previous package, which would have \"proved\" the wrong build. Two fixes. The scripts now treat any code\nexcept 0 as a failure. The farm also reads the log: no `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` line, no package, whatever the script\nreturned. And a compile step now waits while another build tool process is running on that PC. I went back\nthrough every lane's package log of the afternoon; each has the success line. I did not find out what started\nthe second build tool.\n\n**Development or Shipping.** At 14:26 I had recommended a Shipping build because a Development build makes\nWindows show a firewall prompt. The owner's point: the jam page recommends Development builds, so judges see\nthat prompt on most entries, and a Development build writes a log if a judge's copy crashes. So the entry\nbecomes one Development zip if two things hold: a judge who double-clicks the game cannot land in a developer\nfeature by accident, and the zip holds no developer launchers, test rooms or loose source sounds. I checked\nthe first one by reading the code. Practice keys, recording and the raw sound mix all need a command-line\nswitch. The console key does not: in a Development build the tilde key opens the engine console, and eleven\nengine debug key bindings are live. A lane is closing those and writing the script that builds the entry\nfolder. If its checks have not passed by about 20:00 the entry stays Shipping.\n\n**Fonts.** The owner confirmed his pick: Exo 2 Black Italic for headings and numbers, Saira Regular for text.\nBoth are under the SIL Open Font License, and the licence text ships with the game.\n\n**This log was audited, and it moves.** The owner asked for the dev log to be checked against the jam's rules\nbefore anyone outside reads it. A read-only lane went through every file and came back with 19 rows. The\nowner's answer: \"you are right for all 19 calls - fix them. also if these are fixed, can they see the history\nwhere we change them? if so shouldnt we create a clean one?\" He is right on the second point too: a fix in a\nlater commit leaves the earlier text in the history.\n\nWhat the audit found, in counts: the names of two people, used as their PCs' names, about 8,700 times; the\nlocal path of the studio's private notes about 21,000 times; an account name 150 times; the names of real gun\nmakers and models about 280 times; commercial games named as references about 1,200 times; and about 96 lines\nof NVIDIA's DLSS plugin source, which its licence does not allow us to publish. None of it was a password, a\nkey or a perk code. The exporter that writes the transcripts now masks all of these, withholds any tool call\nthat names a private file, and withholds plugin source. The leak check that runs before each commit now uses\nthe exporter's own rules, so the two cannot drift apart. In the test export every one of those counts is 0.\n\nThe log's home from this entry on is a new repo whose first commit is the clean export. The README says so.\n\n**One finding needs the owner.** The audit read how the revolver that ships was made. No photo of a real gun\nwent to the image tool or to the 3D generator, and the prompt banned logos, marks and lettering. But the\nprompt did describe one real revolver's recognisable features in words, and the mesh was scaled from that\nmaker's published sizes. So nothing was copied, and the outline still resembles a real product on purpose.\nThe cheap way out is a change to the barrel in the clean-up file. The owner decides.\n\n**Not done.** The slower gun and the health change are not merged. The level generator has not proved its\nruns at the new numbers. The HUD with the owner's fonts has passed its tests and waits for its scripted runs.\nThe hands stay switched off. One farm PC does all the compiling, so every lane queues behind it.\n"

take_ubt() {   # take_ubt <host> <name> <step>
  local host=$1 name=$2 s=$3 d pid t now waited=0
  mkdir -p "$lockdir"; d="$lockdir/$host.ubt"
  # The main copy's merge check goes first: while <host>.ubt.first names a live process, other lanes do not try.
  local first="$lockdir/$host.ubt.first" fp
  [ "$name" = maincheck ] && echo "$$" > "$first"
  while :; do
    fp=''; [ -f "$first" ] && read -r fp < "$first"
    if [ -n "$fp" ] && [ ! -d "/proc/$fp" ]; then rm -f "$first"; fp=''; fi
    if [ -n "$fp" ] && [ "$name" != maincheck ]; then
      [ "$waited" -eq 0 ] && echo "FARM the main copy's check compiles next on $host; this $s waits its turn" >&2
      sleep 15; waited=$((waited + 15)); continue
    fi
    if mkdir "$d" 2>/dev/null; then
      [ "$name" = maincheck ] && rm -f "$first"
      echo "$$ $name $s $(date +%s) $(date +%H:%M:%S)" > "$d/owner"
      ubt=$d; trap 'rm -rf "$slot" "$ubt"' EXIT
      [ "$waited" -gt 0 ] && echo "FARM waited ${waited}s for the compiler on $host" >&2
      return 0
    fi
    if [ -f "$d/owner" ]; then

GLASSBOX-MEGAJAM-2026 lane=icons1

Make a set of interface icons by image generation for SUPERCUT, a first-person shooter set on a film set. The
player has a revolver and a film clapperboard; clapping the board freezes the scene for a few seconds, and the
frozen scene turns into a pencil sketch. Bullets fired during a freeze hang in the air and fly when the freeze
ends. Do the work yourself; start no subagents. Images only: change no code.

## What to make

Eleven subjects, each in TWO styles, so 22 pictures, plus two contact sheets.

Subjects (file name, then the idea; the upgrade's rule is given so the picture can say it without words):

1. `longtake`: LONG TAKE. Freezes last longer. Idea: a film reel with a long strip of film running out of it.
2. `extrareel`: EXTRA REEL. One more freeze charge. Idea: two film reels, one behind the other, or a reel with a
   small plus-shaped spark beside it (a shape, not a typed character).

The splinters and dust now show in the freeze. The fix is commit `80d5f4c` on `clap2`, a change to `Tools/make_vfx.py` and the burst's assets only, no game code. No test expectation changed.

**What looks wrong first, in the new break strip:**
- [taste: owner review] The dust shows from +17 to +150 ms, but the sketch draws it as blank paper with a cyan outline and no hatching. It reads more like cut-out paper than dust.
- [taste: owner review] The splinters and chips show only as small cyan-ringed specks, a few pixels across at 1080p. In the 960-wide strip they are hard to see. Their sizes are the same as in job 2.

![break strip](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/clap2/shots/after_break_60fps.jpg>)

**Cause.** The freeze's pencil sketch (`Art/sketchfx/SketchFreeze.hlsl`, lines 71-75 and 108-110) builds each pixel from depth, normals, stencil and the picture's brightness. The burst used see-through materials, which write no depth, normal or stencil. All a sprite left was a small brightness change, which disappears in the hatching.

**How the other causes are ruled out:**
- **Time step:** the freeze does not slow world time. It sets time dilation to 0 only on actors that join the scene, and the burst never joins. In the engine, a Niagara component that is not solo takes the world's delta; only a solo one multiplies in its own dilation (`NiagaraComponent.cpp:1011` and `:4777`). An earlier probe also showed the particle counts falling on time.
- **Culling, held-depth scaling, first-person flag, missing usage flag:** I made one probe build and ran the same break twice. The only difference was the sketch held off in the freeze. With it off, the dust and dark chips show from +16 to +183 ms. With it on, nothing shows. Both run logs have 0 "missing usage flag".

**Fix.** `make_material` takes a new `masked=True` option, and NS_BoardBurst now uses three masked copies (M_Vfx_BoardSplinter, M_Vfx_BoardChip, M_Vfx_BoardPuff). Masked sprites write depth, so the sketch draws them the way it draws the break pieces. The dust's particle alpha goes from 0.5 to 1, because under a mask alpha only wears the cloud away at its edge. The six shared materials and the other four effects are unchanged. I added no second effect and no fallback.

**For lane vfx2,** who owns the shared effects helper, the changes in `Tools/make_vfx.py` are:
- `make_material`: the new `masked` argument, the blend-mode line and the opacity-pin line;
- the three material references in `make_board_burst`, and the dust colour's alpha;
- the material loop at the end of the file.

NS_ImpactDust and the other see-through effects vanish in the freeze the same way. I left them alone.

### Sun 15 Nov 16:18:37 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

Three lanes are out for your animation and gun request, and here is my answer on the hanging bullet.

**Hanging enemy bullets: I would not damage the player for touching one.** That is also what the game does today. A frozen enemy shot does nothing if you walk into it, and when time runs again it flies on and hits whoever stands in its path. Three reasons to keep it:

- The freeze is the player's planning time. If frozen bullets hurt, walking through a frozen room becomes fiddly instead of clever.
- REVERSE SHOT works by touching a frozen enemy bullet to turn it round. Damage on touch would contradict that card.
- The danger is already there and reads better: do not be standing in the bullet's line when the freeze ends.

Say so if you want them to hurt and I will have it changed.

**Animations and guns:**

- **Mixamo download:** a lane is driving your Firefox in the background, in a new window of its own, the same way the Megascans download was done. It fetches rifle aiming idle, firing rifle, rifle idle, rifle walk, run and strafes both ways, a hit, a death, the unarmed strafes for the Rusher, then every other strafe variant up to 30 more. If Mixamo is signed out in Firefox it stops without touching the sign-in, and I will ask you to sign in.
- **Guns:** a lane is shortlisting a scoped bolt-action sniper rifle and a rifle, then preparing the best of each. I allowed CC0 first and CC BY 4.0 with a credit line second. No model with a maker's name, logo or lettering on it gets in.
- **Wiring:** a third lane retargets the clips onto the enemies' skeleton and makes each enemy pick its moving clip from the direction it travels against the way it faces. The Grunt already sidesteps in code with forward clips only, which is the slide you saw. This lane changes how enemies look, not what they do.

The risk is the retarget. Mixamo's skeleton is not the one our figures use, so the first report I asked for is one converted clip with pictures before the rest are done.

The check of main `418f51a` has a real package now (263 s) and is waiting for [pc-c]'s one run slot. The dev log re-export finished its export pass and is in its scans.

Both conditions hold at commit `dcb2434`. I checked them in a packaged Development build on c4:

- **Without `-SupercutDev`:** no console key, no engine debug keys, no gameplay debugger, no engine on-screen messages. The start log says `DEV features off: console keys 0, debug bindings 0, gameplay debugger off, on-screen messages off`. With the switch it says `DEV features on (-SupercutDev): console keys 1, debug bindings 11, gameplay debugger on, on-screen messages on`.
- **The SUPERCUT folder plays the same runs as the full package:**
  - Hand-made main8, both builds: `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17`.
  - Generated run, both builds: `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 144.8 s, shots 54, freezes 16, kills 26`.
  - All four logs have 0 `missing usage flag`.

**Open points:**
1. **The brief contradicts itself on main8.** It says unreachable runs go, but also says the hand-made run must play from the folder. A plain start never plays main8, so I kept it and its 8 rooms (a few KB) so that check could run. To leave it out instead, take `main8` out of `KEPT_RUNS` in the script.
2. **Shipping was not tried.** No Shipping package was at hand. The fix is compiled out of Shipping builds.
3. **Everything was built on [pc-c], not c4.** Every c4 build crashed the compiler (C1001, a bad shared precompiled header). Lane motion1 hit the same crash. c4 needs that cleared before the judges' build.
4. **Two big files stay unless you say otherwise:** `Supercut.pdb` (397 MB, 112 MB zipped, gives function names in crash logs) and the Vulkan layer files (39 MB, not proven unneeded).
5. **The window title still ends in "(64-bit Development ...)".** Changing it means a new setting, which the brief rules out. [taste: owner review]

**One bug I found and fixed:** in my first package, engine on-screen messages were still on without the switch. The engine turns them back on after the game module starts (`LaunchEngineLoop.cpp:4464`). The gate now runs after engine init, before the first map loads. The headless tests could not catch this because they call the gate directly. The start log line caught it, since it reads the live state.

**What the script leaves out:** 52 entries, 0.5 MB in all:
- the 3 manifests
- `Play_dev.bat`
- `Tuning.example.txt`
- `Saved/`
- 42 room files that no shipped run names
- 4 runs: demo3, door1_cross, fight5, main

The folder is 778 files, 1374.5 MB. The test zip came to 805,049,745 bytes, which is 268,692,079 bytes (256 MiB) under the 1 GB limit. I deleted the zip after.

In Git Bash, `tar.exe` is GNU tar, and it writes an uncompressed 1.44 GB file named `.zip`. Use `C:\Windows\System32\tar.exe` instead.

**Tests:** two added. Both go red when the fix is removed and green with it. The full run is 249 pass, 1 fail. The failure is `Supercut.Set.EveryLampGlowsInsideItsHousing`, which already fails at the base commit and is fixed on main by `da66b41`. No test was deleted or loosened.

To run the script: `python -I Tools\entry_folder.py <package folder> <output folder>`.

Commits on branch `devsafe1`:
- `de1fad2`: the gate and its tests
- `68862d8`: `Tools/entry_folder.py`
- `dcb2434`: the screen-message fix

`Tools/farm_run_demo.ps1` is untracked in the worktree and not committed. It is a copy of `run_demo.ps1` that none of these commits need.

"""Where a scan word hits in the unpushed dev log lines. Masks digits after an IP-like prefix."""
import re, subprocess, sys
repo = "D:/UE/megajam-2026-devlog"
d = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "diff", "origin/main", "HEAD", "--", "transcripts", "DEVLOG.md"], capture_output=True).stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")
cur = None
for line in d.splitlines():
    if line.startswith("+++ "):
        cur = line[6:]
        continue
    if not line.startswith("+"):
        continue
    for w in sys.argv[1:]:
        for m in re.finditer(w, line, re.I):
            a, b = max(0, m.start() - 70), min(len(line), m.end() + 50)
            ctx = line[a:m.start()] + "<<" + m.group(0) + ">>" + re.sub(r"\d", "#", line[m.end():b])
            print(cur, "|", ctx)
EOF

FVector ASupercutCharacter::GetMuzzleLocation() const
{
	// Fixed to the camera: no view motion (bob, kick, reload, draw) moves where a shot starts. Since lane home1 it is the
	// muzzle at the old home (CharacterShotStart), not the drawn muzzle, which sits nearer the eye.
	return Camera->GetComponentTransform().TransformPosition(CharacterShotStart);
}

FVector ASupercutCharacter::GetDrawnMuzzleLocation() const
{
	// The renderer draws a held part at FirstPersonScale of its distance from the eye, along its own sight line (the
	// first-person field of view is off, so no other correction: SceneView.cpp, WorldToFirstPerson).
	const FVector Eye = Camera->GetComponentLocation();
	const FVector Muzzle = GunKick->GetComponentTransform().TransformPosition(MuzzleOffset);
	return Eye + (Muzzle - Eye) * Camera->FirstPersonScale;
}

FVector ASupercutCharacter::GetEyeLocation() const
{
	return Camera->GetComponentLocation();
}

float ASupercutCharacter::GetViewAngle() const
{
	return Camera->FieldOfView;
}

FVector ASupercutCharacter::GetAimDirection() const
{
	// The control rotation, not the camera's view: a camera kick must not move the aim.
	return GetViewRotation().Vector();
