The owner plays the build and asks for a different enemy; a test goes stale between two merges; the main PC's compiler is the next risk\n\n**Three notes from the owner in eighteen minutes, after playing.** I quote the substance of each.\n\n- 16:05: every enemy dies to one shot. Upgrades that add damage become upgrades that do something else. Enemy\n  damage is 35 for a Grunt's shot, 15 for a Rusher's hit, 55 for a Marksman's shot. An enemy's bullet must not\n  vanish when the enemy dies: a bullet hanging in a freeze still flies on. Enemy projectiles should be bullets\n  with tracers, \"not circles and lines\".\n- 16:12: the enemies have no sideways walking animation. Get strafing clips, a rifle aiming idle and a rifle\n  firing clip from Mixamo, and a free realistic sniper rifle for the Marksman.\n- 16:23: \"the grunts move very poorly, very robotic\". They are the main enemy, so they should be close to\n  enemy players: pathfinding, a full set of animations, jumping, crouching, strafing, ducking, smart enough to\n  jump over lava and not fall off ledges, and some in later stages lob grenades. Grunts carry a pistol (a CC0\n  model, pistol clips); rifles are for the Marksman only. Rushers need effects for the rush and the strike.\n\nThe third note is the biggest change of the jam's last day. Until now a Grunt was an actor that slid inside a\nrectangle, faced the player and sidestepped on a clock. There is no navigation data in the project at all.\n\n**What I set going.** Each of these is a helper lane with its own brief, on its own branch.\n\n- One-shot kills and the three damage numbers went to the lane that already owned the gun's timing, because\n  its two scripted proof runs have to be re-pinned for the same reason.\n- \"Bullets outlive their shooter\" went to a rules lane with one instruction first: write a test that fails on\n  it. Neither I nor the effects lane found code that removes a shot when its shooter dies, so the cause is not\n  known yet, and I did not want a guess patched in.\n- The only upgrade that added damage was SLOW BURN (a hanging shot gains damage each second). My replacement,\n  marked for the owner's review: SQUIB. An enemy killed by a hanging shot bursts and kills enemies within three\n  metres; burst kills do not chain. An image lane drew its icon in four candidates and I picked one.\n- The Grunt is rebuilt in three commits with clock gates, so the last good one ships if the next is late:\n  19:30 it finds its way round cover, speeds up and brakes, fights from positions, strafes and ducks, and never\n  walks off a ledge or into a hazard; 22:00 it jumps gaps and climbs ledges; 00:30 some carry grenades. I asked\n  the lane to choose between the engine's navigation mesh and a walk grid the game samples itself when a room\n  is entered, by what it can prove in forty minutes. My lean is the grid: rooms are built at run time, and the\n  scripted runs need the same seed to give the same fight every time.\n- An agent drives the owner's signed-in browser, in a window of its own, to download the clips from Mixamo. It\n  stops if it meets a sign-in or a licence dialog. Mixamo's stock character is a retarget reference only and\n  does not ship. A second lane retargets the clips onto our skeleton. A third finds a CC0 pistol and a sniper\n  rifle (CC0 first, CC BY with credit allowed for the rifle) and prepares them with grip and muzzle points.\n- Rusher effects, grenade effects and the sounds for both went to three more lanes.\n\n**A seam, so two lanes do not write the same file.** The AI lane decides what a Grunt does. The animation lane\ndecides what it looks like. Both would have edited the enemy class. I put one small struct on main first: the\nenemy's body state for the frame (velocity, crouched, in the air, air time, and an act such as aim, fire,\nthrow, hit). The AI writes it every tick. The clip picker reads it and nothing else. I committed it without\ncompiling it, which I do not normally do; the next check compiled it clean.\n\n**A question the owner asked.** If the player walks into an enemy's bullet that is hanging in a freeze, should\nit hurt? I read the code before answering. Today it does nothing on touch, and on release it flies on and hits\nwhoever is in its path. I recommended keeping that: a freeze is the player's safe moment to move through the\nroom, and a bullet that hurts on touch would punish the one thing the mechanic invites.\n\n**The honest schedule.** This moves the end of merging from about 17:30 today to after midnight. The limits I\nset and told the owner: nothing unproven merges after 02:00, the final package is compiled by 06:00, the jam\ncloses at 09:59. If it runs late, grenades are cut first, then jumps.\n\n**A test that went stale between two merges.** The check of the newest main failed 1 of 258 tests. The effects\nlane's tracer test asserted that, at rest, the gun's drawn muzzle is the place shots start, brought toward the\neye by the first-person depth scale. That was true on the lane's base. Then another lane moved the drawn gun to\nthe placement the owner chose and deliberately left the shots' start where it was, so that no shot in the game\nchanged. Both lanes passed alone; together the two points were 9 cm apart. The game was right: the tracer is\ndrawn from the gun the player sees. The test was measuring against the wrong point. It now measures against\nthe revolver mesh's own muzzle. This is the second time today that two lanes each passed and their merge\nfailed, and both times the merged check caught it before a build reached the owner.\n\n**Merged since 16:03.** The clapperboard's burst now shows in the frozen sketch. Player shots have a tracer\nfrom the muzzle, impact effects and bullet holes. The new interface is in: upgrade cards with icons, a\nclapperboard counter, a layered health bar, and the owner's two fonts, each with its licence file in the\npackage. A build with the lighting, set, exit door and sound work reached the owner's play folder at 16:33\n(252 tests, both scripted runs unchanged).\n\n**The build the judges get.** The jam page recommends a development build. A development build has a console\nkey, debug key bindings and on-screen engine messages that a judge could trip over. A lane closed those unless\nthe game is started with a switch that only our own shortcuts pass, and proved it in a package. It found one\nthing I would have missed: the engine turns its on-screen messages back on after the game module starts, so the\ngate has to run later than the obvious place. Its own start-up log line caught that, because the line reads the\nlive state instead of repeating what the code meant to do. My pick is the development build with this gate.\n\n**The next risk.** Two lanes reported that every build they tried on the main PC died inside the compiler,\nwith a precompiled header that comes back bad after it is deleted. They moved to the one other open PC, whose\nsingle compiler now serves thirteen lanes. The judges' build has to be compiled on the main PC. A lane is now\nfinding the cause, with the instruction that a retry loop is not a fix.\n\n**This log.** The clean re-export passed its scans except for one thing my word check showed: a commercial\ngame's name inside a web address, which the whole-word mask had missed. The mask now matches it anywhere.\n"

#!/bin/bash
# Swaps the testers' copies (C:\SupercutPlaytest on [pc-c] and [pc-b]) to the fetched Shipping package. Keeps Play.bat and logs.
# Skips a PC where a Supercut process is running.
SRC="D:/UE/Builds/_from_farm/main_ship/Windows"
TAR="D:/UE/Builds/_from_farm/main_ship/ship.tar"
[ -f "$SRC/Supercut.exe" ] || { echo "no package at $SRC"; exit 1; }
rm -f "$TAR"; tar --force-local -cf "$TAR" -C "$SRC" . || exit 1
SUM=$(cksum < "$SRC/Supercut/Content/Paks/Supercut-Windows.ucas" | cut -d' ' -f2)
echo "local ucas bytes $SUM"
for pc in [pc-c] [pc-b]; do
  echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) $pc"
  n=$(ssh -o ConnectTimeout=20 $pc 'tasklist | find /i /c "supercut"' | tr -d '\r')
  [ -n "$n" ] || { echo "SKIP $pc: no answer over ssh"; continue; }
  [ "$n" = 0 ] || { echo "SKIP $pc: game running ($n)"; continue; }
  ssh $pc 'cmd /c "(if exist C:\SupercutPlaytest_new rmdir /s /q C:\SupercutPlaytest_new) & mkdir C:\SupercutPlaytest_new"' || continue
  scp -q "$TAR" "$pc:C:/SupercutPlaytest_new/ship.tar" || { echo "scp failed"; continue; }
  ssh $pc 'cmd /c "cd /d C:\SupercutPlaytest_new && tar -xf ship.tar && del ship.tar"' || { echo "untar failed"; continue; }
  n=$(ssh $pc 'tasklist | find /i /c "supercut"' | tr -d '\r')
  [ "$n" = 0 ] || { echo "SKIP $pc: game started meanwhile"; continue; }
  ssh $pc 'robocopy C:\SupercutPlaytest_new C:\SupercutPlaytest /MIR /XF Play.bat /XD logs /NFL /NDL /NP /NJH' | grep 'Files :\|Bytes :'
  ssh $pc 'cmd /c "rmdir /s /q C:\SupercutPlaytest_new & dir /b C:\SupercutPlaytest & for %I in (C:\SupercutPlaytest\Supercut\Content\Paks\Supercut-Windows.ucas) do @echo ucas bytes %~zI"'
done
rm -f "$TAR"; echo "DONE $(date +%H:%M)"
@echo off
cd /d "%~dp0"
if not exist logs mkdir logs
start "" "%~dp0Supercut.exe" -SupercutLog="%~dp0logs\play_%RANDOM%.log"
```

## What looks wrong (the owner decides from these)
- **Rest:** the gun is about twice as large on screen as at the old rest place. Only the top half of the right fist shows, and the left hand is just a pale edge beside it. No wrist or forearm shows at either aspect. The hands read as a pale glove. `[taste: owner review]`
- **Reload, 100 ms:** two left fingertips stick up from the bottom edge with no hand under them. It is the left hand leaving the frame, and it reads as stray fingers. `[taste: owner review]`
- **Board hold:** the board looks like it rests on the palm from below, not gripped. `[taste: owner review]`
- **Clap lift:** in its last 2 ticks (42 and 46 ms after the press), 4 left points are inside the board. The test finds them all hidden from the eye, and no picture catches them. I left this open: it comes from the blend while the board rises, not from the board pose.
- **Cut arm ends:** none in frame in any picture, at 16:9 or 4:3.

## Job 1: the two tests
Both pass now. The rule still holds for every hand point except the three tips the owner's hold buries: left ring 0.69 cm deep, right thumb 0.46 cm, right ring 0.05 cm. It is still that list at the new home.
- **Hidden check:** each of the three must be hidden from the eye at rest, on every kick tick and on every reload tick. Over 571 point-ticks the eye sees none of them. If one were seen, the test fails and names the tick.
- **Blend test:** points inside are accepted only up to t 0.35, and only while hidden. Today they stop at t 0.25, all behind the hand's own skin.
- **Nothing like this existed:** no test had a "can the camera see this point" check, so I wrote one on the hands tests' own ray code.
- **Its limit:** a point buried inside a drawn gun part can never be seen by that check. The seam where a finger enters the gun is what the pictures are for.
- **Box hand test, also changed:** after the merge it counted clap2's 13 board pieces as box-hand parts (15 instead of 2). It now counts only the two cube parts. That was a test fault, not a game fault.
- No other test was loosened. The full table of changed expectations with reasons is in the handoff.

## Job 2: the board hand
- **Hinge flip:** the board body is not symmetric, so clap2's flip did change the board under the hand.
- **The hold:** from the rise to the break, no left point is inside the board. A fingertip is within 0.4 cm of it on every tick, and the nearest hand skin is drawn 7.1 cm from the eye, well past the 2 cm near clip.
- **Left as is:** I did not change left_board, because the hold is fine.
- **Gap:** the blend test's clear-board half still places the board where the gun used to rest. The clap test checks the real board in the game.

3	## For the enemy AI lane
4	
5	Read from branch gen3 at `D:\UE\wt\gen3` (15 Nov 16:45). All lengths cm, z up, the floor a player starts on at z 0.
6	Rooms are text files (`Content/Rooms/gen/sN/dNN.txt`), one piece per line, built by ASupercutRoom
7	(Source/Supercut/SupercutRoom.cpp) and the piece types in SupercutRoomPieces.cpp and SupercutPuzzles.cpp.

9	**What a room is made of.** Every solid surface is a `box` line: one axis-aligned UStaticMeshComponent on the room
10	actor, collision profile `BlockAll` (ASupercutRoom::AddBox / AddShape, SupercutRoom.cpp:282). There are no separate
11	actors per box and no tags. The role word (`role=floor|wall|ledge|crate|flat|scorch|metal`) only picks the material;
12	the room keeps no per-box role you can query at run time. `mark` and `prop` lines and the tape crosses are `NoCollision`
13	(walk-through, look only). Catalogue set dressing (`dress` lines) is solid only when its catalogue entry says
14	`blocks=1`; open dressing has no collision.
15	
16	**A fire pit.** A real hole in the floor, not a flat danger strip:
17	- the floor boxes round the opening are cut (sc_build.py `carve_pits`), so the opening has no floor collision;
18	- a 20 cm burnt lip runs round the opening at floor level: `box role=scorch`, 20 thick, from z -160 to 0. Its top is
19	  walkable floor, flush with the floor;
20	- the bed: `box role=scorch` from z -180 to -160 (solid);
21	- the glow on the bed: `mark role=lava` (no collision);
22	- the hazard: `kill from=... to=... cause=lava`, the opening only (not the lip), from the bed (z -160) to z +5.
23	  A kill box is not a component or actor and has no collision channel. It is a box in ASupercutRoom::KillBoxes,
24	  asked through `ASupercutRoom::TouchesKillBox(At, Radius, HalfHeight)` (SupercutRoom.h:109). Enemies already use it:
25	  `ASupercutEnemy::WouldTouchKillBox` (SupercutEnemy.cpp:175) keeps Grunts and Rushers from stepping in. That call is
26	  the way to tell hazard from floor: a point over an opening touches a kill box, a point on floor or lip does not.
27	- cause word `lava` is every fire in generated rooms (fire pits and lava hops). Blades kill by actor, not kill box.
28	- `fall below=Z` (one per room, 350 under the room's lowest floor) kills only the player; nothing catches an enemy
29	  that drops into a pit. A pit is 160 deep with sheer walls: an enemy that falls in cannot climb out.

The animation lane was told to cover the first two with walk strafes whose play\nrate follows the enemy's speed and the crouch clips already on our skeleton, and to show a picture of the\nthrow with a pistol in the hand before anyone depends on it. With the hands on, the right fist\nreads as a pale glove low in the frame with no wrist behind it, and for a moment during the reload two\nfingertips show at the bottom edge with no hand under them. #!/bin/bash
# Merge check of the main copy on a farm host through farm.sh's own queue (no load polling).
# mirror, build, test, package, hand-made run, generated run, fetch.
# Usage: merge_check_x.sh [host, default [pc-c]]
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
PC=${1:-[pc-c]}
NAME=maincheck
LOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs_$PC
# One check at a time. A stopped background task does not stop this script: stop it with kill <pid>.
LOCK="/d/UE/_merge_check_$PC.lock"
if ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then echo "LOCKED: a merge check of $PC is running, pid $(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)"; exit 91; fi
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid"
trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK"' EXIT
step() { echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) $*"; "$@"; local rc=$?; echo "=== exit $rc"; return $rc; }

echo "HEAD $(git -C /d/UE/Projects/Supercut59 log --oneline -1)"
step "$F" mirror $PC $NAME /d/UE/Projects/Supercut59 || exit 1
step "$F" build $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Jobs 8 || exit 2
step "$F" test $PC $NAME "$LOGS" || exit 3
grep -a "passed\|failed" "$LOGS/test/console.txt" | tail -3
step "$F" package $PC $NAME "$LOGS" || exit 4
echo "PACKAGED $(date +%H:%M)"
grep -a -c "Failed to compile Material" "$LOGS/package/package_run.log"
step "$F" run $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Packaged -Exe '{B}\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe' -Run main8 -Seed 1 -Script '{P}\Script\main8.txt' -FixedFps 240 -Silent -TimeoutSeconds 540
echo "run exit $?"
grep -a "RUN wrapped" "$LOGS/run/run.log"
grep -a -c "missing usage flag\|Failed to create compute pipeline" "$LOGS/run/run.log"
cp "$LOGS/run/run.log" "$LOGS/run_main8.log"
step "$F" run $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Packaged -Exe '{B}\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe' -Seed 6 -Script '{P}\Script\gen\s7.txt' -FixedFps 60 -Silent -TimeoutSeconds 540
grep -a "RUN wrapped" "$LOGS/run/run.log"
step "$F" fetch $PC $NAME builds/Supercut59/Windows "D:/UE/Builds/_from_farm/main"
echo "DONE $(date +%H:%M)"

Both jobs are done and committed on branch `vfx2`. The worktree is clean and none of my farm steps are still running.

## The enemies' shots: commit be8d1ed

**What it's made of:** enemy shots are now a glowing bullet with a tracer streak behind it. It's built from the engine's basic cylinder and cones; no new material, texture, mesh or sound.
- **Bullet:** a cylinder body with a cone nose, 22 cm across and 54 cm long, pointed along the flight.
- **Streak:** a cone that narrows to a point behind the bullet. Its length is 0.14 s of the shot's flight: 126 cm for a Grunt's shot, 450 cm (the cap) for a Marksman's. It grows from where the shot was fired or turned, so it never sticks back through the shooter.
- **Colour:** all of it uses the game's glow material in the "enemy shot" colour, hue 11 (red-orange) at strength 1.5. That's the same colour and brightness as the old ball.
- **In the freeze:** every glow part keeps its colour in the pencil sketch, so a held bullet and its streak stay red. The pictures show it.
- **Glow:** the game's existing halo surrounds the bullet (75 cm across, like the old ball's) and runs along the streak.
- **Unchanged:** the revolver's own shot, and everything a shot does (speed, damage, hit size, hang, release, REVERSE SHOT, DOUBLE EXPOSURE, the impact). It also applies to an enemy shot turned back by REVERSE SHOT, which shows yellow.

![enemy shots from the side, live: old above, new below](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/vfx2/shots/enemy_live_side.jpg>)

**Pictures** (old on the left, new on the right, same rooms and moments; distances worked out from each enemy's fire frame and shot speed):
- **Grunt and Marksman shots:** head on at 20 m and 5 m, in a lit lane and a dark lane, plus the frames as a shot reaches the camera. [enemy_grunt.jpg](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/vfx2/shots/enemy_grunt.jpg>), [enemy_marksman.jpg](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/vfx2/shots/enemy_marksman.jpg>)
- **Freeze:** shots held in the sketch, head on and from the side. [enemy_hang.jpg](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/vfx2/shots/enemy_hang.jpg>)

**What the pictures show:**
- **From the side:** a pointed bullet with a long streak, where before it was a ball with a stub tail.
- **Head on** (how a player sees a shot coming): old and new are almost the same red disc with the same glow, lit and dark, at 5 m and 20 m. The new one is not harder to see.

**Path line:** the hang path line is only drawn for the player's own shots hanging at the muzzle in a freeze, never for enemy shots. So it isn't the "lines" the owner meant. Those were the cone tails behind the enemy balls, which are now the streaks. I left the path line unchanged.

**Checks:**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Build | passes |
| Tests | 246 passed, 0 failed, including a new one: an enemy shot is a body, a nose and a streak, all keeping their colour in the sketch |
| Development package | 0 `Failed to compile Material` |
| main8, twice | `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17`, both runs, unchanged |
| s7 | `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 144.8 s, shots 54, freezes 16, kills 26`, unchanged |
| `missing usage flag` | 0 |
| Frame time, about 30 enemy shots in the air (31 at the end of the run) | after 218.2 / 219.6 fps; before 175.5 / 161.0 |

The frame-time gap is noise, since someone is using [pc-c]. It shows no loss, not a gain.

**What got worse or is open:**
- In the last frames before a shot hits the camera, the new pointed shape covers less of the screen than the old round one.
- The glow material has no lighting, so the bullet is a flat red silhouette with no white-hot core. From the side it can look like an arrow. A hot core would need a second colour or a new material. `[taste: owner review]`
- Every size is a `[pick]` in `SupercutShot.cpp`. `[taste: owner review]`
- Lane rules1's bug (enemy shots vanish when the enemy dies): I found nothing in the shot, Grunt or enemy code that removes a shot when its shooter dies. Not fixed, as asked.

## Effects in the freeze sketch (15:58 request): commit 1d067c5

This commit is just the freeze picture script. The first run's timing was wrong: a second clap less than 0.5 s into the clapperboard's swing does nothing, and the sketch takes about 0.5 s to appear. The rerun shows:
- **Tracer:** shows in the sketch, in its yellow.
- **Impact burst** (hot core, sparks, dust) **and muzzle flash:** they disappear from the sketch, because they're see-through sprites. I left them out on purpose. The flash and hot core only last 1-2 frames, and masked materials would give the soft dust a hard, dotted edge in normal play. `[taste: owner review]` If the owner wants them frozen in the sketch, the fix is clap2's: masked versions of those materials.

### Sun 15 Nov 17:47:02 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

The enemy-shot effects lane finished, and I merged it into main as `55c0d24` after looking at its pictures. It is not in a checked build yet.

![enemy shots from the side: old above, new below](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/vfx2/shots/enemy_live_side.jpg>)

- **What changed:** an enemy shot is now a pointed bullet with a long tracer streak behind it, in the same red-orange as before. The Marksman's streak is longer than the Grunt's because its shot is faster.
- **Head on:** it reads almost the same as the old ball, so it is no harder to see coming.
- **In the freeze:** the bullet and its streak keep their red in the pencil sketch.
- **Still open:** the muzzle flash and impact burst vanish in the sketch. The lane left that on purpose, since fixing it would give the dust a hard dotted edge in normal play. `[taste: owner review]`
- **Look:** from the side the bullet is a flat red silhouette with no white-hot core, and it can read as an arrow. A hot core needs a second colour or a new material. `[taste: owner review]`
- **Vanishing shots:** this lane found nothing in the shot or enemy code that removes a shot when its shooter dies. That bug is still with the rules lane.

The fire-pit build `024e486` printed its 8-stage reference line (`98.2 s, 46, 14, 17`) and is being fetched now. Once it is in your play folder I start the check of the current main head, which carries the hands default, the new sounds and these shots.

I changed 23 of those names to match in any letter case, so the next export masks them. The two commits already on the private repo keep the old forms in their history. I did not start a third repo for that; squashing the history once more before a judge gets access is your call.

The compiler crash on c4 is fixed: a clean build, the package, both scripted runs and a second clean build all passed on c4. One test fails, but not because of my change.

**What isn't clean, first:**
- **Tests:** 259 of 260 pass. `Supercut.Tracer.ALiveShotFliesOnTheEyeLineAndIsDrawnFromTheDrawnMuzzle` fails at my base `0f308a1`. Main fixed that test in `3cc4a9c`, which came after my branch point, and gruntai1 saw the same failure. I did not re-run the tests on current main (`024e486`).
- **Lanes without the fix:** worktrees made before this merges still build without it. Their workaround on c4 is to pass `-Jobs 8` to `farm.sh build`; no build has failed at 2 or more jobs. Their `package` step still compiles at one job the old way. Every c4 package I found today passed, but that's luck, not the fix.
- **COMMON_RULES.md line 45 is now wrong.** It says to run the build again up to three times; that never cured anything. I left it alone since it's your file. FARM.md line 28 and the GOTCHAS.md entry are corrected.

**Cause.** The shared precompiled header was never bad. In 5.9 every compile runs through the build accelerator (UBA), which intercepts the compiler's file access and hands it the header from its own shared memory. On that path the compiler misreads the header: C1001, or `FName` missing. I took the exact header file that had just failed, untouched, and compiled two files against it with plain `cl.exe`. Both passed.
- It only happens at one job, which is `build.ps1`'s default. All 31 failed c4 builds since yesterday ran with one job; all 6 passes used 2 or more. No other farm PC ever built the header at one job, which is why only c4 showed it.
- I couldn't find in the engine source why one job triggers it.
- The cache theory was wrong. The "Cache bucket" log line is written for every action that could be cached, and no cache is set up on this farm.
- Controlled test on c4, header deleted before each case:

| Jobs | Setting | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | default (UBA intercepting) | failed, 12 C1001 | 57 s |
| 1 | `-NoUBA` | passed (twice) | 88 s, 85 s |
| 8 | default | passed | 49 s |
| 8 | `-NoUBA` | passed | 43 s |
| 1 | UBA's own allocator off | failed, 13 C1001 | 32 s |

**Fix.** Commit `3f26c85` on branch `c4fix1`:
- `Tools/build.ps1` passes `-NoUBA`. The delete-and-retry loop is gone, since the header was never bad.
- `Tools/package.cmd` passes `-NoUBA` in `-ubtargs`, as `package_shipping.cmd` already did.

In 5.9, `-NoUBA` keeps UBA's scheduler but runs the compiler without the interception. The build log tags each such step `[NoUba]`, which is how to check a log for the fix. I measured no cost: 43 s against 49 s at 8 jobs. No farm script changed.

**Proof**, all on c4 through `farm.sh`, one job, header compiled as the very first step (the case that always failed before):

| Step | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Clean build | passed, all 49 steps `[NoUba]`, 0 C1001 | 183 s |
| Tests | 259 passed, 1 failed (above) | 268 s |
| Development package | `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, 0 `Failed to compile Material`, 0 C1001 | 397 s |
| main8 run | `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17`, 0 `missing usage flag` | 205 s |
| s7 run | `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 144.8 s, shots 54, freezes 16, kills 26`, 0 `missing usage flag` | 76 s |
| Second clean build | passed, all 49 steps `[NoUba]`, 0 C1001 | 257 s |

### Sun 15 Nov 17:59:01 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

The compiler crash on c4 is solved and the fix is merged into main as `9393054`. That was the one lane I couldn't put a time on, and the final build depended on it.

- **Cause:** in UE 5.9 every compile runs through the build accelerator, which intercepts the compiler's file access. At one job, which was our build script's default, the compiler misreads the shared precompiled header through that path and crashes. The header itself was never bad.
- **Evidence:** all 31 failed c4 builds since yesterday ran at one job; all 6 that passed used two or more. The lane also compiled two files with the plain compiler against the exact header that had just failed, and both passed.
- **Fix:** the build and package scripts now pass `-NoUBA`. The lane measured no slowdown from it (43 s against 49 s at eight jobs).
- **Proof on c4:** two clean builds, a clean Development package, and both scripted runs on their reference lines. Tests were 259 of 260; the one failure is the stale tracer test already fixed on main, on the lane's older base.
- **Still unknown:** why one job triggers the misread. The lane could not find it in the engine source.

c4 is a full build host again, with two run slots against [pc-c]'s one. I told all seven running lanes how to pick up the fix and to move work there, which should shorten the queue behind most of my ETAs.

The final-package commands and timings are written up in [FINAL_BUILD.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/c4fix1/FINAL_BUILD.md>): about 3 minutes for a clean build and under 7 for the package on c4.

The check of main with hands on by default is still running on [pc-c].

# The HUD's icon pictures (lane hud2), from lane icons1's finals: 1024 square PNGs named by key, no alpha, light line
# art on black (the owner's black and white set, 15 Nov). The brightness becomes the alpha of a white picture, so the
# HUD draws it over its own dark plate, untinted on the cards, tinted on the clapperboard counter (chalk for a charge
# held, the same picture dimmed for one spent). clap_empty is not used: its board sits about 1 px off clap_full's at the
# counter's size, so a spend would jump; the spent state is clap_full dimmed in place.
#
#   python -I Art\ui_icons\make_icon_pngs.py <folder with [a shooter the owner likes]>
#
# Writes Art\ui_icons\<name>.png, 256 square. Then import them with Tools\make_ui_icons.py (in the editor, headless).
# Needs Pillow. The source pictures are only read.

import os
import sys

from PIL import Image

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
NAMES = ["longtake", "extrareel", "slowburn", "doubleexposure", "stuntdouble", "quickchange", "throughline",
         "reverseshot", "encore", "clap_full"]
SIZE = 256


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        raise SystemExit("usage: make_icon_pngs.py <folder with [a shooter the owner likes]>")
    folder = sys.argv[1]
    for name in NAMES:
        source = os.path.join(folder, name + ".png")
        if not os.path.isfile(source):
            raise SystemExit("missing " + source)
        picture = Image.open(source).convert("L").resize((SIZE, SIZE), Image.LANCZOS)
        out = Image.new("RGBA", (SIZE, SIZE), (255, 255, 255, 0))
        out.putalpha(picture)
        out.save(os.path.join(HERE, name + ".png"))
        print("icon", name, "line art: brightness as alpha")


main()

#!/bin/bash
# Merge check of the main copy on a farm host through farm.sh's own queue (no load polling).
# mirror, build, test, package, hand-made run, generated run, fetch.
# Usage: merge_check_x.sh [host, default [pc-c]]
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
PC=${1:-[pc-c]}
NAME=maincheck
LOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs_$PC
# One check at a time. A stopped background task does not stop this script: stop it with kill <pid>.
LOCK="/d/UE/_merge_check_$PC.lock"
if ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then echo "LOCKED: a merge check of $PC is running, pid $(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)"; exit 91; fi
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid"
trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK"' EXIT
step() { echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) $*"; "$@"; local rc=$?; echo "=== exit $rc"; return $rc; }

echo "HEAD $(git -C /d/UE/Projects/Supercut59 log --oneline -1)"

step "$F" build $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Jobs 8 || exit 2

echo "run exit $?"
grep -a "RUN wrapped" "$LOGS/run/run.log"
grep -a -c "missing usage flag\|Failed to create compute pipeline" "$LOGS/run/run.log"
cp "$LOGS/run/run.log" "$LOGS/run_main8.log"
# SKIP_GEN=1: no generated run (from main 024e486 the s7 fight script is not a reference; a walk script replaces it later)

echo "DONE $(date +%H:%M)"

### 15 Nov 17:23. Levels with fire pits and doorways go into the main copy before their end-to-end proof exists, and why; guns and animation clips are sourced; the hands merge switched off

**A merge I made without the proof I normally ask for.** The level generator lane finished. Its stages now have
fire pits that are real holes in the floor with a kill volume over the opening, and from stage 3 a stage is three
to six chambers joined by doorways, with a masking flat inside each later doorway so the player cannot see the
whole set from the door. It also wrote a baker that produces a scripted play-through for each generated run.

The rule on this project has been that a lane's work reaches the main copy only after a scripted run plays the
whole thing and prints its expected last line. The lane could not show that. Of its 12 walk scripts, 4 got a
turn on the build farm, and all 4 stopped part way: two because the scripted player could not hit an enemy from
where the baker stood it, one because the baker's 20 cm walk grid took a prop corner closer than the player's
34 cm body, one because the script stepped off before a moving platform arrived. None stopped on a room that
cannot be walked. The rooms themselves pass the generator's own checks (every gap jumpable, every ledge
reachable, every doorway wide enough).

I merged it anyway, and I am writing the reason down because it is a judgment call that could be wrong. The
owner asked at 16:23 for an enemy that paths, strafes, duck

Three change the\nloop: a perk pick after the first scene and then every third, with two rerolls per run and a new perk that\ngives three more; the run ends when health runs out, not at stage 12, so health carries between scenes and\nenemies sometimes drop a pickup that restores a quarter; clapper charges carry too, more refills are strewn\nthrough the generated levels, and the full-recharge stand becomes a rest scene of its own every fifth scene.\nThe refill should look like a clapperboard, not a film can, and the stands need real models.\n\nThis is a second wave of work 16 hours before the deadline, on top of the enemy rework from 16:23. I did not\npush back on any of it. Each item is something a player meets in the first two minutes, and the loop changes\nturn a 12-room demo into a game with a reason to keep playing. What I did instead was fix the limits: nothing\nunproven goes into the main copy after 02:00, the judges' package is compiled by 06:00, and if we are late the\ncut order is grenades, enemy jumps, the per-lap difficulty scaling, then the new stand models.\n\n**Who got what.** Two new code lanes: one for the three loop changes in three stages that can each be merged\nalone, one for the doorway gap, the door's collision and trigger, and the mouse. The rest went to lanes that\nwere already running or had just finished, because they own the code: the ammo counter to the interface lane,\nthe invisible line to the enemy lane (with the instruction to find the cause before changing anything, since a\nsearch of the code for a \"safe zone\" found nothing), the bob to the motion lane ahead of the rest of its plan,\nthe refill placement and rest rooms to the level generator. The left hand went to the art thread in the form\nthe owner offered: it builds a Blender file of the whole move at the game's timing and opens it on the main PC\nso he can pose the hand himself, and the result comes back as numbers for a code lane. The same thread then\nmakes the pickup and stand models, libraries first, with at most six generations on the jam's 3D perk credits.\nAn image job makes two new icons.\n\nMy picks where the owner left room, each marked for his review: perk picks at scenes 1, 4, 7 and so on; the\nnew perk is called RESHOOTS; a 20% health drop chance per kill, drawn from the run's seeded stream so a\nscripted run repeats; past the last room the run enters the next generated run at its fifth room, and each\nsuch lap enemies fire 10% faster and move 8% faster, capped at four laps; the exit triggers 60 cm past the\ndoor frame's inner face.\n\n**Turning the hands on broke two tests, and the tests were wrong, not the hands.** With the hands on by\ndefault, two of 274 tests failed: both check that everything the player holds is drawn inside a window between\nthe camera's near plane and the body capsule. They measured each held part by its bounding box. A rigged hand\nmesh includes the forearm, which runs back past the eye and out of frame, so its box read 39 cm behind the near\nplane while the drawn hand is well inside it. I took the hands out of the box measure with a comment that says\nso, and gave the hands lane the job of a real measure from the posed bone positions. Until that lands, nothing\ntests whether the hands clip the camera. That is a known hole, written here so it is not forgotten.\n\n**A merge that would have crashed the game.** The rules lane finished: it replaced one upgrade (more damage\nfor a hanging shot, meaningless now that every enemy dies to one shot) with SQUIB, where a kill by a hanging\nshot bursts and kills enemies within 3 m. Its branch built, passed its tests and packaged. I started the merge,\nresolved one conflict, and before committing I read how the card screen draws an upgrade. It loads an icon by\nthe upgrade's key, and the loader stops the program if the icon does not exist. The lane's branch was cut\nbefore the card screen existed, so it had never needed an icon for SQUIB, and nobody had made one. The merged\ngame would have run until the first time SQUIB was dealt, then died.\n\nNo test would have caught it. The interface lane's tests check the cards it knew about; the rules lane's tests\nran on a branch with no cards. I backed the merge out, had the interface lane make the icon first, merged that,\nthen merged the rules lane. I also asked for the missing test: every upgrade in the list has an icon that\nloads, and a failure names the upgrade. The general lesson is about branches cut at different times: each\nlane's proof holds for its own base, and the gap between two bases is only ever checked by whoever merges.\n\nThe same lane could not reproduce the owner's report that enemy bullets vanish when their shooter dies. Its\ntests and a packaged run show the shot outliving the shooter. Its best reading is that the shot is hidden for\na moment behind the kill flash, the hit marker and the dust. I have told the owner that plainly instead of\nclaiming a fix.\n\n**The main PC's compiler crash has a cause.** For two days builds on the main PC failed about five times in\nsix with an internal compiler error in the shared precompiled header, and my working rule was \"run it again up\nto three times\". A lane given only that problem found the cause. In this engine version every compile runs\nthrough the build accelerator, which intercepts the compiler's file access, and when the build is limited to\none job the compiler misreads the precompiled header through that path. The header was never damaged: the lane\ncompiled two files with the plain compiler against the very header that had just failed, and both passed. All\n31 failed builds had run at one job, all 6 that passed at two or more. The fix is one switch that turns the\naccelerator off for this project. My own lead (a stale cache) was wrong, and the retry advice had never cured\nanything; it only sometimes landed on a build that happened to run with more jobs. Why one job triggers it was\nnot found in the engine source.\n\nThat gives a second full build machine, and using it showed a trap at once: on the main PC a check does not\ncopy the project, it builds inside whatever folder it is pointed at. Pointed at the main copy, a 20-minute\ncheck would have blocked every merge. Checks there now run on a separate checkout pinned to the commit under\ntest.\n\n**Also merged and checked since the last entry:** eight new sounds for grenades and enemy movement, and enemy\nshots drawn as red tracers with a muzzle flash and an impact burst. The muzzle flash and burst disappear when\nthe scene freezes into the pencil sketch; whether they should is the owner's call.\n\n**This log.** A scan found that some masked names had slipped through in lowercase, inside search patterns and\npage titles in an exported transcript, because the mask matched exact case. 23 names now match in any case. No\nidentity, code or key was among them.\n"
}

## On c4 a farm "mirror" is a junction: a check there builds inside the folder it is pointed at (15 Nov 2026, verified)

`farm.sh mirror c4 <name> <folder>` copies nothing. It makes `D:\UE\Farm\<name>` a junction to `<folder>`, and build,
test and package then run in that folder. Pointed at the main copy, a merge check holds the main copy for its whole
run (about 20 minutes), and a merge landing meanwhile changes the tree under the build. A main check on c4 therefore
runs on a detached worktree pinned to the commit under test: `D:\UE\wt\maincheck`, farm name `maincheck2`
(`SRC=/d/UE/wt/maincheck NAME=maincheck2 merge_check_x.sh c4`); move it with `git -C /d/UE/wt/maincheck checkout
--detach <commit>` before the next check. The name `maincheck` on c4 is already a junction to the main copy and the
mirror refuses a second folder under one name. On [pc-c] and the other farm PCs the mirror is a real copy.
EOF
tail -n 3 GOTCHAS.md | cut -c1-120

The strafe, jump and landing block is committed as **67069f6** on branch motion1 (`D:\UE\wt\motion1`). Full suite 245 passed, 0 failed, nothing loosened. The [pc-c] Development package has 0 `Failed to compile Material` and 0 `missing usage flag`. main8 still wraps, but its time moved: two runs both gave `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.4 s, shots 22, freezes 14, kills 17` (A2 was 98.2 s; shots, freezes and kills are unchanged).

**What my branch had already changed before this block (800d748):**
1. Walk bob: the same amplitudes as main; only the move offsets went deeper.
2. Strafe: left in main's shape.
3. Jump and landing: deeper and slower (15.7 cm in 0.15 s on take-off, 14.4 cm on landing, back in 0.7 s).

So the owner was judging main's motion.

**Why the strafe looked like the arm circling a pivot:** two terms made the arc.
- **The sideways slide** (`GunMoveSideCm`). The gun is close to the eye: rear sight about 32 cm, front sight about 54 cm. A slide in cm moves the near end 1.69 times as far on screen as the far end. In the reference both ends move the same (1.0).
- **The sway while strafing** (`cos(BobClock)`). It ran once a step, the same rate as the up-down bob, so together they drew a circle. The reference sways once every two steps.

**What 67069f6 changes:**
- **Strafe:** the gun now turns round the eye instead of sliding, 2.8° plus a 0.7° sway once every two steps, on the same step clock as forward. Both ends now cross the screen alike: 1.05 left and 0.99 right, against 1.69 before. Forward and back are main's values, untouched.
- **Jump:** the take-off depth from 800d748 is kept. It measures 21.4% H at 135 ms against the reference's 21% H at 133 ms.
- **Landing:** one dip with a single smooth return over 0.5 s, no spring. I measured it against where the gun settles:

| After the bottom | Reference | Main's motion | 67069f6 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| +133 ms | 9.3% H | 4.6% H | 9.1% H |
| +250 ms | 2.1% H | 0.7% H | 3.1% H |
| +317 ms | 0.4% H | 0.3% H | 1.4% H |
| +367 ms | 0 | 0.2% H | 0.6% H |

  - The drop reaches the bottom in 83 ms (the reference 67 ms), with 0 swings after it.
  - Main's version came back almost completely within 133 ms, which is likely the "spastic" snap the owner felt.
  - Ours tracks the reference closely to +133 ms, then trails it by about 1% H.

**Tests added:**
- A pure strafe: no sideways slide, no pitch or yaw, the only roll is the 2° tilt, and the sway turns half as often as the up-down.
- A landing: one dip, no overshoot, and within 2% of rest 371 ms after the bottom (the bound is 367 ± 17 ms).

**What still differs from the reference:**
- **Sway rate:** ours runs at 1.5 Hz, the reference at 1.6 to 2.1 Hz. The rate comes from the step clock that forward walking shares, so I left it alone.
- **Lean:** ours now leans away from the move like the reference, but less: +1.0° and −2.8° against +8° and −4°. The tilt (−2°) is marked `[taste: owner review]`.
- **Possible remaining landing jank:** I did not touch the camera's own landing dip (`CameraDip`, SupercutCharacter.cpp:682). It drops the whole view in one frame and recovers at rate 9. If the landing still feels spastic, that is the next suspect.
- **An offset I haven't traced:** after the jump the gun ends 2.4% H higher than just before it. It is the same in main's motion.

**Two fixes to my own tooling:**
- The first main8 run on this package failed because I left out `-Run main8`. A start with no run named plays a generated run, so it played `gen_s2`. With the flag it wraps.
- My sway-rate counter was missing turns and had reported 0.5 Hz; it is fixed.

The reference numbers are only in LOG.md. The only file under `D:\UE\ref\ui\work\motion1\` is a tracking plot, `ref_tracks.png`; it has no reference frames.

### Sun 15 Nov 19:06:04 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

The motion lane delivered your item 3 (strafe, jump, landing) as `67069f6`. I merged it on top of main in a separate check worktree and its check is queued on c4; main and the play folder get it only if that check passes.

**Why the strafe looked like the arm circling a pivot:** two things together.
- The gun slid sideways by a fixed distance. Because the rear sight is about 32 cm from the eye and the front sight about 54 cm, the near end crossed the screen 1.69 times as far as the far end. In the reference both ends move alike.
- The strafe sway ran once per step, the same rate as the up-down bob, so the two drew a circle. The reference sways once every two steps.

**What it does now:**
- **Strafe:** the gun turns round the eye (2.8° plus a 0.7° sway every two steps). The two ends now cross the screen at 1.05 and 0.99 of each other. Forward and back are untouched.
- **Landing:** one dip and one smooth return over 0.5 s, no spring. The old one came back almost fully within 133 ms, which is the likely "spastic" snap.
- **Jump:** take-off depth 21.4% of screen height at 135 ms, against the reference's 21% at 133 ms.

Before on top, after below, hands on:

![strafe left](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/motion1/shots/strafe_left.jpg>)
![landing](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/motion1/shots/landing.jpg>)

**This merge also brings the 16:05 changes into main for the first time:** every enemy dies to one shot, the new enemy damage numbers, and the slower reference revolver with a 2.25 s reload. The scripted reference run now fires 22 shots instead of 46.

**Still different from the reference** `[taste: owner review]`: the lean while strafing is smaller (ours +1.0° and −2.8°, reference +8° and −4°), and the sway is a little slower (1.5 Hz against 1.6 to 2.1).

**Next for that lane, limit 21:00:** the camera's own landing dip (the whole view drops in one frame, the likeliest remaining jank), a gun that ends slightly high after a jump, then the recoil kick.

Stills cannot show whether the motion feels right; that needs you in the build once the check is green.

**How it works**

**What doesn't work, or looks wrong**
1. **The Grunt's pistol can't be seen in play.** It's real size (about 20 cm) and always points straight at the camera, so the hands and the red muzzle dot cover it. It only shows for a moment as the Grunt falls. [taste: owner review]

3. **Some Grunt clips can't be reached yet:** grenade toss, crouched aim, crouched walk and jumps. Nothing in the current behaviour triggers them, so I couldn't get the in-game picture of the grenade throw's off arm holding a pistol. Only the Blender sheet exists.
4. **The Rusher's running strafe shows for about 3 frames at a time.** It turns into its run very quickly.
5. **Some picture distances are off.** The Grunt's "5 m" pictures are really 5.4 to 8 m, because it backs off inside 8 m. The Rusher's hit and death pictures are at 24 m.
6. **Scope scratches: they ended up raised, and a green flip can't make them cut.** I measured the normal maps from their pixels and checked the method on test maps with a known answer. All three gun maps (scope, rifle, pistol) are OpenGL, not DirectX as lane guns1 said. So the import script now flips green for all three, not only the scope. The catch is that the red channel, which doesn't depend on the convention, already makes the scratches raised. The only way to make them cut is to invert both red and green, and that would also invert the scope's real edge detail. In a lit packaged comparison of the same frames, the scratches look almost the same either way, because they're mostly painted colour. The clearest difference is the rifle's knurled hammer, which looks right flipped. At 5 m and beyond, none of it shows. [taste: owner review]

## On c4 a farm "mirror" is a junction: a check there builds inside the folder it is pointed at (15 Nov 2026, verified)

`farm.sh mirror c4 <name> <folder>` copies nothing. It makes `D:\UE\Farm\<name>` a junction to `<folder>`, and build,
test and package then run in that folder. Pointed at the main copy, a merge check holds the main copy for its whole
run (about 20 minutes), and a merge landing meanwhile changes the tree under the build. A main check on c4 therefore
runs on a detached worktree pinned to the commit under test: `D:\UE\wt\maincheck`
(`SRC=/d/UE/wt/maincheck merge_check_x.sh c4`); move it with `git -C /d/UE/wt/maincheck checkout --detach <commit>`
before the next check. The farm name must stay `maincheck`: `farm.sh` gives the compiler to that exact name first, and
a check under any other name waits behind every lane (12 minutes on the first try). The junction `D:\UE\Farm\maincheck`
now points at the worktree; a junction is removed with `cmd /c rmdir` (no `/s`), never `rm -rf`, which would empty
its target. On [pc-c] and the other farm PCs the mirror is a real copy.

loop: a perk pick after the first scene and then every third, with two rerolls per run and a new perk that

enemies sometimes drop a pickup that restores a quarter; clapper charges carry too, more refills are strewn
through the generated levels, and the full-recharge stand becomes a rest scene of its own every fifth scene.
The refill should look like a clapperboard, not a film can, and the stands need real models.

This is a second wave of work 16 hours before the deadline, on top of the enemy rework from 16:23. I did not
push back on any of it. Each item is something a player meets in the first two minutes, and the loop changes
turn a 12-room demo into a game with a reason to keep playing. What I did instead was fix the limits: nothing
unproven goes into the main copy after 02:00, the judges' package is compiled by 06:00, and if we are late the
cut order is grenades, enemy jumps, the per-lap difficulty scaling, then the new stand models.

fix3 is done for tonight. Faults 1 and 7 are committed, but main8 and gen s7 no longer finish: their timed walks end before the moved door. The scripts need re-baking, which this lane may not do.

| Fault | Commit | State |
|---|---|---|
| 1, door flush with the back wall | `6e4f4e8` (WIP in the subject) | Done, pictures taken |
| 7, door collision and exit trigger | `6e4f4e8`, same commit | Done; no test of the player standing in the leaf's path |
| 2, mouse at the screen edge | `17de571` | Coded and tests pass; needs a real-mouse check |

Faults 1 and 7 share one commit. They change the same functions in `SupercutRoomDoor.cpp` and the same door test, so a split would leave a commit with failing tests.

**Proof, all from the c4 package of `6e4f4e8`:** package exit 0 with 0 `Failed to compile Material`, and full tests 274 passed, 0 failed.

**Fault 1, the door stood free in the room**
- **Cause:** every room file's gate line sits 200 to 400 cm in front of the back wall. The door was built on that spot, so floor and light showed between it and the wall.
- **Fix:** C++ only, no room file or generator edit and no re-bake. `FitDoorToWall` moves the door until it is 1 cm off the wall ahead and cuts the opening through that wall.
- **Proof:** the logs show the door moved 251 cm in fight/01, 261 cm in gen s7 d05 and 201 cm in the test room. In the pictures it sits in the wall, with no gap visible from the front, 45° or the side.

**Fault 7, the door leaf and the exit trigger**
- **Collision:** the leaf and the white box block the player only. Shots pass as before.
- **[pick] The leaf never pushes.** If a swing step would hit the player, the leaf waits and goes on when they move, so there is no launch and no trap. [taste: owner review]
- **[pick] The exit fires once the eye is 60 cm past the frame's inner face,** inside the white. The old 130 cm circle, which fired from beside the door, is gone.
- **Five walks from different angles:** the END line fired with the eye 61, 62, 62, 67 and 67 cm past the frame, 0 to 4 cm off centre. Each walk run exits with code 2, but that is only its last move failing after the run had already ended.
- **Brushing past:** walking across the doorway did not end the room and did not get the player stuck. The log does not show whether the player touched the open leaf.

**main8 and gen s7 break (needs the main thread)**
- main8 fails twice in scene 1: `SCRIPT failed at 34.30 s: waited 20 s at a "scene" line and the run did not enter a new room`. The script stops walking at x 3330; the door now fires at x 3468, so the player is 140 cm short.
- gen s7 ends rooms 1 to 3 at the door, then the player is shot in scene 4. The longer walk into each door shifts the timed script against the enemies.
- The fix is to re-run main8's `build_full8.py` and gen4's baker so each room's last walk reaches the door. I can't give a new RUN line until that is done.

**Fault 2, the mouse stops turning at the screen edge**
- **Cause:** I worked this out from the engine source, not with a real mouse. Once the game lost the mouse (a cursor screen, a click, alt-tab), nothing took it back during play, so the view followed the cursor and stopped at the edge.
- **Fix:** one function, `EnterPlayInput()`, called at start, when any cursor screen closes, and in play when the window returns to the front or loses the mouse. A `MOUSE` log line records each change of state.
- **Not done:** there is no automated menu→play→card→play→pause→play test and no packaged `MOUSE` line. Test runs have no real window, and scripted runs skip the check.
- **A person must confirm with a real mouse:** full screen, windowed, after a card pick, after pause, after alt-tab. Turn far past the screen edge each time and read the `MOUSE` lines in `Saved\Logs\Supercut.log`.

**Other notes**
- Before 19:28, the first [pc-c] package linked stale objects and its main8 crashed. I deleted the stale folder in [pc-c]'s `fix3base` copy; every result above comes from the clean c4 package.
- The test `StandsOnTheGateWhoseTriggerIsUnchanged` keeps its old name, which is now wrong.
- `Tools/farm_*.cmd` and `.ps1` are untracked farm files. I did not commit them.

"""Where a scan word hits in the unpushed dev log lines. Masks digits after an IP-like prefix."""
import re, subprocess, sys
repo = "D:/UE/megajam-2026-devlog"
d = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "diff", "origin/main", "HEAD", "--", "transcripts", "DEVLOG.md"], capture_output=True).stdout.decode(
cur = None
for line in d.splitlines():
    if line.startswith("+++ "):
        cur = line[6:]
        continue
    if not line.startswith("+"):
        continue
    for w in sys.argv[1:]:
        for m in re.finditer(w, line, re.I):
            a, b = max(0, m.start() - 70), min(len(line), m.end() + 50)
            ctx = line[a:m.start()] + "<<" + m.group(0) + ">>" + re.sub(r"\d", "#", line[m.end():b])
            print(cur, "|", ctx)

1. **Opaque face:** the cylinder face is fully opaque now, so a flash behind it can't tint it. In the before/after sheet, the orange hit flash in g_refilled shows through the old face and not through the new one.
2. **Pointer:** 1.5 times larger, now 0.1275 of the face radius tall and 0.225 wide. A bigger pointer would have run into the reload ring, so the ring moved out by the same amount (0.0425 of the face radius) to keep its gap.    - r_before_seat at 4.60
   - the seat at 5.04
   - r_after_seat at 5.40
   - g_refilled at 6.10
   
   hud3's own gun still has the old timing, so for those runs I put a `Tuning.txt` with main's three numbers next to Supercut.exe and removed it after each run. The game log confirms all three were applied and the reload started 0.31 s after the last round.

From the music thread (Check C4 Music Production Setup). The owner approved the SUPERCUT soundtrack today: "this is perfect. inform the main thread and give it the files." The owner asked me to hand these files to you. I have not changed anything in the game.

THE TWO FINAL TRACKS (both on c4, 48 kHz 24-bit stereo WAV, seamless loops, each exactly 86.71 s = 56 bars at 155 BPM in 4/4, same chords and form):
1. Arcade song (main, 80s arcade synthwave): D:/UE/supercut_music/arcade_song/renders/arcade_v5.wav  (-12.75 LUFS, -1.3 dBTP)
2. Strings song (calm, string ensemble): D:/UE/supercut_music/strings_song/renders/strings_song_v2.wav  (-13.17 LUFS, -1.9 dBTP)
Use these two files, not the *_raw.wav files next to them (raw = unfolded tail, does not loop).

HOW THE OWNER WANTS THEM PLAYED (approved in a demo):
- Start both loops at the same instant and keep both looping in sync forever. Only volumes change. Never restart or seek the strings when they fade in. The owner confirmed: "yes they should be in sync".
- Arcade song is the base. The strings fade in at moments you pick, at most 6 s per visit including fades, then fade back out.
- Fades: 1 s, equal-power (arcade gain cos(x*pi/2), strings sin(x*pi/2), x going 0 to 1).
- Strings gain +0.42 dB relative to arcade, so the two match in loudness.
- Approved demo of exactly this: D:/UE/supercut_music/crossfade_test/demo_synced.wav. Script: crossfade_test/tools/make_demo.py. Visit times: crossfade_test/timeline.txt.
- Section markers, the same in both songs (bar: s): A1 1: 0.0 | A2 9: 12.39 | B 17: 24.77 | B2 25: 37.16 | A3 33 (climax): 49.55 | C 41 (breakdown): 61.94 | A4 49: 74.32. One bar = 1.548 s.

FOR SUBMISSION.md (it currently says all music is synthesised by code, which is no longer true):
- Composed and produced in REAPER 7.48 (Cockos, evaluation licence), built from Python scripts through python-reapy. The owner wrote the base MIDI. Both songs grow from that melody, which was rearranged.
- Strings: VSCO 2 Community Edition samples (CC0) in ReaSamplOmatic5000.
- Synths: Surge XT (free, open source, GPL-3; the audio it outputs is ours).
- Drums and FX: synthesised by our own code (numpy).
- Style references for the arcade song: three tracks from [a shooter the owner likes] soundtrack (Embark Studios). They were used only to study tempo, beat pattern and sound palette. No audio, melody or samples from them is in the game. Their downloads stay on c4 at D:/UE/supercut_music/refs_genre3/ and must not ship.

SOURCE (re-runnable, needs REAPER open with reapy running):
- D:/UE/supercut_music/arcade_song/: arcade_song.rpp, plus tools/build_song.py, tools/make_drums.py, tools/render_loop.py
- D:/UE/supercut_music/strings_song/: strings_song.rpp, plus tools/build_song.py and tools/render_loop.py
- Notes, traps and measurements: unreal/FINDINGS.md, section "SUPERCUT music in REAPER (15 Nov 2026)"
- Not final: main_theme/ (the 16-bar chiptune-to-strings theme), unless the owner says otherwise.

No reply needed unless you want a different format: OGG, 44.1 kHz, or separate stems.

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

/**
 * The music: one sample-exact mixer for every cue, so the four action stems share one clock and a cue change,
 * a cut and a resume land on the sample the rules ask for.
 *
 * The cues are 48 kHz 16-bit stereo WAV files in Audio/music/wav, read from disk at run time (the build stages
 * them next to the game). Every cue is 144 BPM in 4/4: a bar is 80,000 samples, a beat 20,000.
 *
 * The mixer itself is plain C++ with no engine objects, so a headless test can render it and read its state.
 * In the game it runs inside FSupercutMusicGenerator on the audio render thread.
 */

enum class ESupercutMusicCue : uint8
{
	None,
	Action,    // the four action stems: drums, bass, colour, heat
	Puzzle,
	Between,
};

const TCHAR* SupercutMusicCueName(ESupercutMusicCue Cue);

/** One WAV read into memory: interleaved stereo 16-bit samples. */
struct FSupercutMusicTrack
{
	FString Name;
	TArray<int16> Samples;
	int64 Frames() const { return Samples.Num() / 2; }
};

/** Every music file the game plays. Read once per process and shared. */
struct FSupercutMusicTracks
{
	FSupercutMusicTrack Action[4];
	FSupercutMusicTrack Puzzle;
	FSupercutMusicTrack Between;
	FSupercutMusicTrack TakeStart;
	FSupercutMusicTrack RoomClear;

	/** Reads the files from Audio/music/wav under the project folder. A missing or odd file stops the game with its name. */
	static TSharedRef<const FSupercutMusicTracks> Get();
};

class FSupercutMusicMixer
{
public:
	static constexpr int32 SampleRate = 48000;
	static constexpr int64 BarFrames = 80000;
	static constexpr int64 BeatFrames = 20000;
	static constexpr int64 TakeStartDownbeat = 15960;   // where the take-start stinger's band hit lands
	static constexpr int64 RoomClearDownbeat = 20960;   // where the room-clear stinger lands on A minor

```
S="/c/Users/USER/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/ce66ae306241b5fa/82df538e-a9d3-4df3-9564-30dc1eb14f95/scratchpad"; grep -n "^=== " "$S/merge_check_aebac4f.log" | cut -c1-330 | head -12; mkdir -p "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/tools_main"; cat > "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/tools_main/main8_nocards.py" <<'EOF'
"""Re-pin Script/main8.txt for scenes that end with no upgrade screen.

Since the loop lane's Stage B only every PickEveryScenes-th scene (1, 4, 7 with the default 3) ends on an
upgrade screen. After the other scenes the run enters the next room the moment the player crosses the exit, while
the script is still walking. The old end-of-scene lines (`T move 0 0`, `T shot sN_upgrade_screen`, `T key One`)
then run inside the next room and the player starts it off its mark.

For each such scene N this tool removes those three lines, so the script goes straight to the next `scene` line
and waits there, still walking, until the next room is entered; and it puts `0 move 0 0` after that scene's
`0 charges full`, so the walk stops on the first tick in the new room. Safe to run twice.

Usage: python -I main8_nocards.py <main8.txt> [--pick-every 3]
"""
import re
import sys


def main():
    path = sys.argv[1]
    every = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--pick-every') + 1]) if '--pick-every' in sys.argv else 3
    raw = open(path, 'rb').read()
    nl = b'\r\n' if b'\r\n' in raw else b'\n'
    lines = raw.decode('utf-8').split(nl.decode())
    scene_at = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if re.match(r'^0 scene \d+ \d+$', l)]
    scenes = [int(lines[i].split()[2]) for i in scene_at]
    if scenes != list(range(2, 2 + len(scenes))):
        sys.exit('main8_nocards: scene lines are not 2..N in order: %r' % scenes)
    removed = added = 0
    # Walk the scene lines from the bottom so earlier indexes stay valid. The block of scene N ends just above
    # the line `0 scene N+1 1`.
    for k in range(len(scene_at) - 1, -1, -1):
        nxt = scenes[k]            # the scene this line opens
        ended = nxt - 1            # the scene whose block ends above it
        if (ended - 1) % every == 0:
            continue               # it ends on an upgrade screen: its lines stay
        at = scene_at[k]
        # The three lines are the last three non-blank, non-comment lines above the scene line.
        body = [i for i in range(at) if lines[i].strip() and not lines[i].startswith('#')][-3:]
        want = [r'^\S+ move 0 0$', r'^\S+ shot s%d_upgrade_screen$' % ended, r'^\S+ key One$']
        has = all(re.match(w, lines[i]) for w, i in zip(want, body))
        if lines[at + 1] != '0 charges full':
            sys.exit('main8_nocards: no "0 charges full" under the scene %d line' % nxt)
        stop_there = lines[at + 2] == '0 move 0 0'
        if has:
            if not stop_there:
                lines.insert(at + 2, '0 move 0 0')
                added += 1
            for i in reversed(body):
                del lines[i]

stopped answering. I noticed because a file I had read a minute earlier came back "No such device". Windows
still called the volume healthy, and folder names still listed from memory, so for a moment it looked like a
deleted folder. The system log said otherwise: one disk error repeated 47,515 times in the first minute, then
"failed to flush data to the transaction log, corruption may occur" every few seconds. A check of mine that was
starting its tests died at the same second with a page-read error. That is the drive, not the code, and its
result is void.

It began while seven lanes were compiling, a test run was starting and one lane was checking out a few thousand
files into a new working copy. Heavy write load, heat or a fault: I do not know which, and I have not pretended
to. What I did, in order:

1. Told the owner at once, in plain words, with what was known good. Restarting a PC is his decision. He
   restarted it at 19:46.

   had written but not committed (file by file, enough to redo it), and whether the second build machine held a
   copy. Their answers are kept in the thread, which lives on another drive.
3. Froze the second machine's copies of the source into a separate folder, so that a later sync from a broken
   drive could not empty them, and pulled the checked source onto the main PC's system drive.
4. After the restart, before any lane wrote a byte: an integrity check of the whole repository (clean), a
   check that every lane's commits were there (all were, including one made 90 seconds before the drop), a
   copy of the full history to two other drives, and a scan of every changed file for the usual mark of a lost
   write, a file that comes back empty or filled with zero bytes.

"""Masked context of whole-word, other-letter-case occurrences of given `replace` key indexes in the dev log's
tracked text. Never prints a key: the match is shown as ###.

usage: python -I ci_context.py <index> [<index> ...]
"""
import collections, json, re, subprocess, sys

REPO = "D:/UE/megajam-2026-devlog"
keys = list(json.load(open(REPO + "/tools/redact.local.json", encoding="utf-8"))["replace"].keys())
files = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "ls-files"], capture_output=True).stdout.decode().splitlines()

        text.append(open(REPO + "/" + f, encoding="utf-8").read())
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
        pass
blob = "\n".join(text)
for i in map(int, sys.argv[1:]):

        c[b + "###" + a] += 1
    print(i, "len", len(k), "distinct", len(c), c.most_common(3))

The "before" mesh dump of all 45 meshes is done. My base package on [pc-c] is queued behind another lane's compile, so nothing is packaged, imported or pictured yet.

**What the dump shows.** All 45 meshes already have `recompute_normals False`. The old assets therefore held their old FBX normals, and the import was never recomputing them. That matches `make_props.py` already asking for Import Normals. The import setting needs no change; the shiny look came from the old FBX normals themselves.

**The checker can tell old normals from new.** [check_normals.py](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/normfix1/tools/check_normals.py>) compares the editor's normals with the FBX files. I tested it on the "before" dump in both directions:
- **Old FBX against the old meshes:** all 45 pass. Median gap 0.17°, maximum about 0.37°, which is the rounding in the engine's stored normals.
- **Fixed FBX against the old meshes:** none pass, with median gaps of 11 to 35°.

A mesh passes if at least 99% of 400 sampled corners are within 1°, the 99th-percentile angle is 1° or less, and every corner matches a mesh vertex. Corners with a zero-length FBX normal are left out.

One known outlier: `SM_LightSoftPanel` has 3 of 400 corners up to 39.6° off. They sit on degenerate faces the engine drops (it keeps 6,587 of 6,666 triangles). The mesh still passes.

**Getting the dump to run** took two failed editor runs on name errors in my own script. The Python name is `ProceduralMeshLibrary`, and the static mesh editor subsystem comes back empty in a headless editor run, so I create it directly. Neither failed run changed anything on [pc-c].

Next, once the package finishes: "before" pictures, then the import, the "after" dump and the 45-row check.

# Wasm support matrix

What the page checks before it downloads anything (`wasm-compat.js`): WebGPU, a cross-origin isolated page
(`SharedArrayBuffer`), 64-bit WebAssembly memory (Memory64), the texture formats the cook needs
(`texture-compression-bc` by default), and the CPU and memory minimums of the project's settings. A player whose browser
fails gets a message, not a broken page.

| Browser | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Chrome (Windows, desktop) | supported; the reference | both Preview 1 tiers (forward and deferred) |
| Edge (Windows) | supported | Chromium; same as Chrome |
| Chrome (Linux) | works with Vulkan WebGPU | stock Chrome on Linux gives no WebGPU adapter unless started with `--enable-features=Vulkan --use-angle=vulkan` (Linux cloud test hosts run it that way, NVIDIA L4/L40S) |
| Chrome (macOS) | supported and tested | |
| Firefox (Windows, 141 and later) | runs, slower start | WebGPU on Windows only; the forward tier; shaders compile one at a time, so the first start takes longer; the page advises Chrome |
| Safari (macOS) | supported and tested | under investigation: Safari 26.6 does not load a large project's Test build (the JavaScript engine's memory passes about 5 GB and the tab is closed) |
| Safari (iOS) | a phone browser | see Phones and tablets; use a Test or Shipping build (a Development build's code alone holds about 913 MiB and the tab is closed); under investigation: the 3D scene draws black with no WebGPU errors |
| Phones and tablets | `warn` by default | the forward tier; the setting `MobileDevices` (`ue-mobile`) can `block` before the download or `allow` |

| GPU class | Tier the page picks |
|---|---|
| Desktop-class GPUs that pass the GPU check (both tiers are cooked by default) | mobile deferred (`SP_WEBGPU_ES3_1_DEFERRED`) |
| Phones, low-end GPUs, and any GPU on a stage cooked without the deferred tier | mobile forward (`SP_WEBGPU_ES3_1`) |

`?tier=forward|deferred` (`mobile` is an alias of `forward`) overrides the pick for a test; the deferred tier still needs
a stage cooked for it and a device that can run it. Thresholds come from the GPU check's milliseconds per draw and are
placeholders until more hardware is measured.

The desktop tier (`SP_WEBGPU_SM5`, with Lumen) is experimental and not part of Preview 1: the page never picks it, and
`?tier=desktop` runs it only on a stage cooked with `bTargetDesktopTier=True` and a GPU with subgroups, clip distances
and texture-formats-tier2.

# Shipping an Wasm build

## Configurations

| Configuration | Use | Page `?args=` from links | Release scan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Development | daily work, profiling, the harness | all (`QueryArgs` default) | blocked: source paths and asserts with file names are in the wasm |
| Test | measuring a near-final build | safe list only | as Shipping |
| Shipping | anything public | safe list only (a `/Game/` map, `-culture=`, `-WebQualityPreset=`, `-WebScreenPercentage=`) | must pass |

Package a public build with `-clientconfig=Shipping`. Development stages are blocked by `deploy.py` on purpose.

## What UAT stages

`BuildCookRun -platform=Wasm ... -stage -package` (or Package Project) writes:

- `index.html` and the page scripts (`wasm-loader.js`, `wasm-play.js`, `wasm-compat.js`, `wasm-strings.js`,
  `wasm-debug.js`, `wasm-harness.js`), `sw.js`, `_headers`, `favicon.png`, the web app manifest `manifest.webmanifest` and
  its icons (`app-icon-192.png`, `app-icon-512.png`, `apple-touch-icon.png`; only with `bInstallable`, opt-in); the project's own
  `<Project>/Build/Wasm/Template/` overrides any of them file by file;
- `<Project>/Binaries/Wasm/<Game>.js` and `.wasm`;
- the containers (`.utoc`/`.ucas`, `.pak`) under `<Project>/Content/Paks`, Oodle Kraken by default (the web decodes Oodle;
  the default); `bCompressContainers=False` stages them raw, with Brotli carrying them on the wire;
- `<file>.br` Brotli siblings of the big files (quality from `BrotliQualityRelease` / `BrotliQualityDevelopment`);
- `wasm-manifest.json` (every file with size and sha1) and `wasm-cache.json` (what the service worker caches);
- `UECommandLine.txt`, `wasm-tiers.json` when a tier beyond forward (the deferred tier, or the experimental desktop
  tier) is cooked.

Files that never go public move to `<stage>-Debug` beside the stage (same relative paths): the symbol map, UAT's file
manifests, and loose third-party software records (`.tps`) that a folder staged as NonUFS carries. Keep that folder with
the build: it symbolizes crash stacks (`Build/Tools/deploy/symbolize.py`) and keeps the records.

Loose folders the web never loads (the debug font, the GPU dump viewer, the project's splash images) are removed before the
lists are written. `check_stage.py <stage>\Wasm` checks the result.

### Sun 15 Nov 22:20:28 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

A web build is possible with this engine, but not as the jam entry, and I would not start one before the Windows build is locked.

I read the engine's own docs for this; nothing was run.

- **The engine has it.** The 5.9 MegaJam Preview ships a web target (WebAssembly plus WebGPU, labelled "Preview 1"). It needs a C++ project, which ours is, and one exact emscripten version that is not installed on any of our PCs.
- **It cannot be the entry.** The rules say a UE submission "must be packaged for Windows and playable on Windows 10 or 11, macOS, Android, or iOS". A web build could only sit beside the Windows zip, as a play-in-browser link on the itch page.
- **The look would change.** The web target runs the mobile renderer only. Lumen on the web is experimental and off in this preview; virtual shadow maps and Nanite are not supported at all. SUPERCUT uses Lumen and virtual shadow maps today, plus DLSS, so the game would need relighting and a fresh visual check, not a recompile.
- **Untested here.** The pencil-sketch freeze, the particle effects and the 240 Hz reference run are all unproven on that renderer.
- **Hosting is fine.** itch.io works with its SharedArrayBuffer option switched on. Players need a WebGPU browser, with Chrome or Edge on Windows as the reference.

It would also compete for [pc-c]'s one compiler: a whole new platform compile and two more shader cooks, while seven lanes queue there and c4 is closed for heavy work.

My recommendation: skip it for the deadline. If you want a browser demo on the itch page afterwards, it is a reasonable job for after submission, starting with a one-room probe to see how the lighting holds up. If you would rather I spend a slow slot on pc2 tonight just to learn whether it compiles, say so; I would not do it by default.

The facts are noted in `unreal/FINDINGS.md`. The check of loop stage C is still running on [pc-c].

void USupercutRun::ApplyLap()
{
	FSupercutTuning& Live = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	const int32 Laps = FMath::Min(Lap, Live.LapScaleMostLaps);
	if (Laps == 0 && !bLapScaled)
	{
		return;
	}
	if (!bLapScaled)
	{
		LapBase = Live;
		bLapScaled = true;
	}
	const float Fire = FMath::Pow(Live.LapFireIntervalScale, float(Laps));
	const float Move = FMath::Pow(Live.LapMoveSpeedScale, float(Laps));
	Live.GruntFireInterval = LapBase.GruntFireInterval * Fire;
	Live.MarksmanCooldown = LapBase.MarksmanCooldown * Fire;
	Live.GruntMoveSpeed = LapBase.GruntMoveSpeed * Move;
	Live.GruntMoveClipRate = LapBase.GruntMoveClipRate * Move;   // the feet keep up with the faster walk
	Live.RusherRunSpeed = LapBase.RusherRunSpeed * Move;
	Live.RusherRunClipRate = LapBase.RusherRunClipRate * Move;
	bLapScaled = Laps > 0;
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("LAP %d: enemy time between shots x%.3f, move speed x%.3f"), Lap, Fire, Move);
}

git log --oneline -1

# Merge check of the main copy on a farm host through farm.sh's own queue (no load polling).
# mirror, build, test, package, hand-made run, generated run, fetch.
# Usage: merge_check_x.sh [host, default [pc-c]]

PC=${1:-[pc-c]}
# NAME and SRC may be set from outside: on c4 the mirror is a junction to SRC, so a check there must run on a
# pinned worktree (SRC=/d/UE/wt/maincheck NAME=maincheck2), never on the main copy, or no merge can land meanwhile.
NAME=${NAME:-maincheck}
SRC=${SRC:-/d/UE/Projects/Supercut59}
LOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs_$PC
# One check at a time. A stopped background task does not stop this script: stop it with kill <pid>.
LOCK="/d/UE/_merge_check_$PC.lock"
if ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then echo "LOCKED: a merge check of $PC is running, pid $(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)"; exit 91; fi
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid"
trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK"' EXIT
step() { echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) $*"; "$@"; local rc=$?; echo "=== exit $rc"; return $rc; }

- **Unchanged:** the `filmcan` and `refill` piece lines, `FilmCanReach`, `RefillReach`, the log lines and the tuning names. The pickup's position and reach rule are the same number for number.
- **Import:** `Tools/make_props4.py` puts both meshes, six textures and two materials into `/Game/Props/Pickups`. The materials are instances of `M_PropReal`, so they draw like the other real props in a package and in the freeze. The tool is safe to re-run.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- Refill pad

ASupercutRefill::ASupercutRefill()
{
	PrimaryActorTick.bCanEverTick = true;
	RootComponent = CreateDefaultSubobject<USceneComponent>(TEXT("Root"));
}

void ASupercutRefill::BeginPlay()
{
	Super::BeginPlay();
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	const float Across = Tuning.RefillReach * 2.f;
	Gold = SupercutShapes::Glow(this, PuzzleGold, Tuning.FilmCanGlow);
	UMaterialInterface* Dark = PuzzleRoom(this).RoleMaterial(TEXT("metal"));

	// A gold ring on the floor where the player stands to use it. The board stands in front of it (FaceToward).
	auto AddFlat = [this](ESupercutShape Shape, const FVector& Location, const FVector& PartSize, UMaterialInterface* Material)
	{
		SupercutShapes::Add(this, RootComponent, Shape, Location, FRotator::ZeroRotator, PartSize, Material)->SetCastShadow(false);
	};
	AddFlat(ESupercutShape::Cylinder, FVector(0.f, 0.f, 1.f), FVector(Across * 1.15f, Across * 1.15f, 1.f), Gold);
	AddFlat(ESupercutShape::Cylinder, FVector(0.f, 0.f, 1.5f), FVector(Across * 0.95f, Across * 0.95f, 1.f), Dark);
}

void ASupercutRefill::FaceToward(const FVector& Toward)
{
	check(!Board);
	// The pad's centre is the board's use point, and the panel faces back toward Toward (the room's start), so a player
	// who walks in from the start sees it head on and stands on the pad facing it.
	USceneComponent* Look = NewObject<USceneComponent>(this);
	Look->SetupAttachment(RootComponent);
	Look->SetRelativeRotation(FRotator(0.f, SupercutPickupLook::YawToward(GetActorLocation(), Toward), 0.f));
	Look->RegisterComponent();
	AddInstanceComponent(Look);
	Board = SupercutPickupLook::AddMesh(*this, Look, SupercutPickupLook::PickupMesh(TEXT("SM_ClapRefillBoard")), FTransform(-RefillUsePoint));
	for (const FVector& Peg : RefillBoardPegs)
	{
		SupercutPickupLook::AddClapperboard(*this, Board, FTransform(FRotator(RefillBoardPitch, 0.f, 0.f), Peg, FVector(RefillBoardScale)), 0.f);
	}
}

void ASupercutRefill::Tick(float DeltaSeconds)
{
	Super::Tick(DeltaSeconds);
	const ASupercutCharacter* Hero = USupercutRun::Get(this).GetHero();
	if (!Hero || Hero->IsDead())
	{
		return;
	}
