Two things: there is a newer build in your play folder, and your three points are with lanes.

## New build (00:02)
Main is `97c0024`. It adds the Grunt's paths, strafes, ducks and jumps, and your posed clap move with the flat-normal board. The check passed: 332 tests, clean package, scripted run on its reference line.

## Your three points

**1. Collision on the stand and board.** The stand and board lane is on it, due 01:20. One risk I found by reading the level generator: refill pads sit on the walking line between room sections, and the board stands 75 cm past the pad. A solid board there can close a passage. The lane has to prove that no room with a pad or pickup is closed off, and move the board's position rule until none are. If rooms still fail at 01:00, the stand gets collision tonight and the board does not.

**2. The stick's textures and the normal fixes.** My reading, tell me if it is wrong: the pictures I showed you were taken before the clap lane merged, so the clapperboards on the stand and board had the old stripes and the old smoothed normals.
- The pickups use the game's own clapperboard meshes, so in the 00:02 build they should already have the mirrored stripes you asked the art thread for, and the flat normals. The lane is re-taking the pictures to prove it.
- The stand and board themselves are built from boxes and tubes by script, not generated, so the generated-model fault should not apply. The lane measures that too.
- One fault is real either way: the break pieces were cut from the old stick, so the stripes flip direction at the break. I asked the art thread for re-exported pieces.

If "wrong" means you want the old stripe direction back on the stick, say so and the arm goes back instead.

**3. One-time claim at the board.** In work, same lane. Taking the charges removes the six clapperboards and the board stays.

`[pick, your call]` I added one exception. The level generator proves no room can strand the player by counting on the pad as a refill at any time. A strict one-time claim breaks that proof in the generated rooms: waste your charges and you are stuck. So the board restocks when your charges reach 0 in that room, and the pad still resets the room's puzzle pieces on every step-on. Say "strict" if you want no restock.

# props4: collision of the film can's stand and the refill board (16 Nov 2026, 00:15)

Room-file coordinates, cm. `start` is the room's `start at=` point, `at` the piece's `at=` point. Both pieces turn the
same way: let `u = unit(at.xy - start.xy)` along the floor (u = (1, 0) when at.xy equals start.xy), and
`yaw = atan2(u.y, u.x)` in degrees. Each box is a box turned by `yaw` about Z: its own X runs along u, its own Y along
(-u.y, u.x). Nothing else of either prop collides.

| Piece | Box size X x Y x Z | Box centre | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filmcan at=` (the stand) | 56.6 x 65.1 x 104.1 | `at + (0, 0, 52.05)` | the stand mesh's bounds; the clapperboard on its tray does not collide |
| `refill at=` (the board) | 74.0 x 142.0 x 160.0 | `at + 75 * u + (0, 0, 80)` | the board mesh's bounds; its pivot is 75 cm past the pad's centre, away from the start; the six clapperboards do not collide |

- Half extents: stand (28.3, 32.55, 52.05), board (37, 71, 80).
- What they stop: the player and shots (and anything else that traces WorldStatic/Visibility), like a solid catalogued
  prop (`BlockAll`). Enemies are let through them (`IgnoreComponentWhenMoving`, the way the room lets enemies through
  film gear) `[pick]`: a Rusher that lunges into a stand would stop dead on it, and enemy movement code is not touched.
- For a walk checker, grow each box by the player's capsule radius, 34 cm.
- The pickup still works on contact: the stand's half diagonal is 43.1 cm, so a player touching it from any side has
  their middle at most 43.1 + 34 = 77.1 cm from `at`, inside `FilmCanReach` 80. The board's front face is 38 cm past
  the pad's centre, so the player (radius 34) can stand on the pad's centre, inside `RefillReach` 90.

If a number changes it is changed here and named in props4's report.

# Final Development package on c4 from the main copy

Lane c4fix1, 15 Nov 2026. The times are what each step took on c4 for this lane's worktree today (branch
`c4fix1`, 3f26c85 on main 0f308a1), through `farm.sh`, with other lanes using c4 at the same time. A step's own time
is `secs` in its `farm_step.txt`; the wait for the compiler lock comes on top and depends on the queue (up to 19
minutes today).

## 0. Before: the fix must be in the main copy

The main copy builds with its own `Tools\build.ps1` and `Tools\package.cmd`. Both need `-NoUBA` (commit 3f26c85 on
branch `c4fix1`), or the first build on c4 at one job dies with `C1001 ... msc1.cpp, line 1589`. After the merge,
from Git Bash on c4:

```bash
cd /d/UE/Projects/Supercut59
grep -c -- "-NoUBA" Tools/build.ps1 Tools/package.cmd Tools/package_shipping.cmd   # each must print at least 1
git log --oneline -1                                                                # note the commit being built
```

## 1. Steps

Run from Git Bash on c4. `final` is a farm name for the main copy; the mirror on c4 is a junction, so the build
writes `Intermediate` and `Binaries` inside `D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59` and the package lands in
`D:\UE\Farm\_builds\final\Supercut59\Windows`. Nothing goes to `D:\UE\Builds`.

```bash
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
LOGS=/d/UE/wt/final_farmlogs

"$F" mirror c4 final /d/UE/Projects/Supercut59                       # under 1 s (junction, nothing copied)
"$F" build  c4 final "$LOGS/build"                                    # 183 s clean at 1 job (49 actions); see note a
"$F" test   c4 final "$LOGS/test"                                     # 268 s, 260 tests
"$F" package c4 final "$LOGS/package"                                 # 397 s (game target compile 304 s at 1 job, cook, stage, pak)
"$F" run c4 final "$LOGS/run_main8" -Packaged -Exe '{B}\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe' \
     -Run main8 -Seed 1 -Script '{P}\Script\main8.txt' -FixedFps 240 -Silent -TimeoutSeconds 540     # 205 s
"$F" run c4 final "$LOGS/run_s7" -Packaged -Exe '{B}\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe' \
     -Seed 6 -Script '{P}\Script\gen\s7.txt' -FixedFps 60 -Silent -TimeoutSeconds 540                # 76 s
```

Total step time about 19 minutes, plus queue waits.

# farm.sh: build, test, package and run a SUPERCUT project copy on a farm PC, driven from c4. Details: ../FARM.md.
#
#   farm.sh mirror  <host> <name> <project folder on c4>     copy the project to <root>\Farm\<name> (changed files only)
#   farm.sh build   <host> <name> <log folder> [build.ps1 args, e.g. -Target Supercut -Jobs 8]
#   farm.sh test    <host> <name> <log folder> [run_tests.ps1 args, e.g. -Filter Supercut.Rooms]
#   farm.sh package <host> <name> <log folder>               Tools\package.cmd   -> <root>\Farm\_builds\<name>\Supercut59
#   farm.sh package-shipping <host> <name> <log folder>      Tools\package_shipping.cmd -> ...\_builds\<name>\Supercut59_ship
#   farm.sh run     <host> <name> <log folder> [run_demo.ps1 args]   {P} = the mirror folder there, e.g. -Script {P}\Script\main8.txt
#   farm.sh fetch   <host> <name> <remote path> <local folder>   path in the mirror, or builds/... or out/...
#   farm.sh status  <host>
#   farm.sh slots                                             who holds or waits for which PC right now
#
# Each step brings its logs back to <log folder>/<step>/ and exits with the remote step's exit code.
# Logs that come back have the PC's user and computer names replaced by USER and PC.
#
# Hosts: [pc-b], pc2, [pc-c], pc4 over ssh, and c4 itself (15 Nov: the owner freed c4 for lanes). On c4 nothing is
# copied: "mirror" makes D:\UE\Farm\<name> a junction to the project folder, so the steps build in that folder.
#
# Slots (15 Nov): build, test, package, package-shipping and run take one of the host's slots and wait for one
# when all are taken, so the lanes no longer pile onto one PC. A slot whose farm.sh has died is taken over.
set -u
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)

root_of() {   # one line per farm PC: ssh alias, root folder there (engine in <root>\UE_5.9, mirrors in <root>\Farm)
  case "$1" in
    [pc-b]) echo 'C:\UE' ;;
    pc2)    echo 'C:\UE' ;;
    [pc-c])   echo 'F:\UE' ;;
    pc4)    echo 'C:\UE' ;;

Straight answers.

Solid, it can close a passage, and that would be a dead end in a generated room. So the lane checks all 570 rooms that have a pad or pickup, which is a 9-minute run. The stand is small and is not the worry.

### Mon 16 Nov 00:23:35 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

Not by hand, and it would not help much tonight, because compiling is no longer the slow part.

**What a check on [pc-c] actually costs** (from tonight's logs):

| Step | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Compile | 47 to 72 s, and 2 s when only art changed |
| 332 tests | about 2 minutes |
| Package (cook, stage, pak) | 1 to 6 minutes |
| Scripted run | 2.5 minutes, plus the wait for the one run slot |
| Copy the build back | 2 to 3 minutes |

The compile is about one minute out of twelve to fifteen. The long waits tonight were queueing: each lane holds the machine for its whole chain, one after another. The worst was 17 minutes waiting for the run slot.

**Splitting one compile across PCs** is something Unreal can do with its build accelerator, which farms compile jobs out to agent machines. I turned that accelerator off on Friday because it crashed the compiler on the main PC with this preview engine. Setting up a coordinator and agents across three PCs now would be new, unproven plumbing nine hours before the deadline, to save about a minute per check. Object files from separate machines cannot be merged manually.

**What does help is whole lanes on separate machines**, since each lane's chain is independent. That is what pc2 is doing now with the Shipping trial. The Grunt lane also ran its proof there earlier.

My recommendation is to leave it as it is. Three lanes are in proof and all are due by 01:20. Adding [pc-b] would take roughly 30 to 40 minutes of copying and a first full build before it could run anything, so it would arrive about when the freeze does.

### Mon 16 Nov 00:28:10 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

Short answer: not by much, and freeing resources on [pc-c] would help only a little.

**Why there is a queue.** It comes from two locks, not from [pc-c] being short of CPU or memory:

- **One compile or package at a time.** A package that met another lane's build failed outright on 15 Nov 14:04, so those steps now go one after another.
- **One game run at a time.** Two runs started together on [pc-b] and one crashed at start. That was two runs from the same package folder. Two runs from separate folders were never tried, so the rule may be stricter than it needs to be.

Tests and cooks take neither lock and already run side by side. As of 00:27, [pc-c] has 2 of its 3 slots in use (a level-lane run and the clap lane's package) and nothing is waiting.

**What freeing resources on [pc-c] would do.** Each step would finish a bit faster. The steps would still go one after another, so the queue stays.

**What does speed it up, and is already in place:**

- My merge check jumps the compiler queue ahead of the lanes.
- Ready lanes are stacked into one check instead of one check each.
- The Shipping trial is on pc2, so it takes nothing from [pc-c]. Its package started at 00:27.

**The one thing I could still try** is allowing two game runs at once on [pc-c] from separate folders. I am not doing that tonight. The remaining runs add up to about 25 minutes one after another, which fits before 01:20, and a crashed run at this hour costs more than the wait it would save.

The queue is not what sets the 01:20 time. The lanes' own work is: the collision lane's failing walk test and its nine-minute every-room check.

## Shipping builds and user settings (5.9, lane shell1)

- **A Shipping build writes no log, and `-log` / `-abslog=` change nothing** (14 Nov 2026, verified). Shipping has
  `NO_LOGGING`, so `UE_LOG` compiles away. `bUseLoggingInShipping` would turn it back on, but it needs a unique build
  environment, which an installed engine refuses (RulesAssembly.cs). A Shipping run with `-log -abslog=<file>`
  left no file. SUPERCUT's fix: under `NO_LOGGING`, `Supercut.h` redefines `UE_LOG` to write to the file named by
  `-SupercutLog=<file>` (Fatal still stops the game).
- **Shipping ignores `-FPS=`** (14 Nov 2026, verified). LaunchEngineLoop.cpp reads it inside
  `#if !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING`, so `-UseFixedTimeStep` alone steps at the default 1/30 s. The game module reads `-FPS=`
  itself in Shipping and calls `FApp::SetFixedDeltaTime`. `-UseFixedTimeStep` and `-DeterministicAudio` work in
  every build.
- **A Shipping shared PCH built through UBA crashes cl.exe 14.44** (14 Nov 2026, verified). Every project file that
  used `SharedPCH.Engine.Project.ValApi.ValExpApi.Cpp20` stopped with `C1001: Internal compiler error`, plus odd
  errors such as "'delete': is not a member of the global namespace". A fresh build with UBA failed again, the
  same build with `-NoUBA` was clean, and the Development target with UBA was clean. `-NoUBA` in the `-ubtargs` fixes
  it (`Tools\package_shipping.cmd`). A build with `-NoUBA` that reuses the bad PCH still fails: delete
  `Intermediate\Build\Win64\x64\Supercut\Shipping` first.
- **A packaged Shipping game saves its settings in the user's folder** (14 Nov 2026, verified):
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<Project>\Saved\Config\Windows\GameUserSettings.ini`, plus CrashReportClient folders and a
  pipeline cache in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<Project>\Saved`. A Development package saves beside the game, in
  `<build>\<Project>\Saved`. Delete the user folder after Shipping tests, or the next test starts from old settings.

step() {   # step <name of step> <host> <name> <log folder> [args...]
  local s=$1 host=$2 name=$3 logs=$4; shift 4
  local root; root=$(root_of "$host") || exit $?
  case "$s" in build|package|package-shipping) take_ubt "$host" "$name" "$s" ;; esac
  take_slot "$host" "$name" "$s"
  local af=''
  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
    af="$root\\Farm\\_out\\$name.$s.args.txt"
    local tmp; tmp=$(mktemp)
    printf '%s\r\n' "$@" > "$tmp"
    if is_local "$host"; then
      mkdir -p "$(fwd "$root")/Farm/_out" && cp "$tmp" "$(fwd "$af")" || exit 1
    else
      ssh "$host" "if not exist $root\\Farm\\_out mkdir $root\\Farm\\_out" && scp -q "$tmp" "$host:$(fwd "$af")" || exit 1
    fi
    rm -f "$tmp"
  fi
  local code
  if is_local "$host"; then
    if [ -n "$af" ]; then
      powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$root\\Farm\\_farm\\step.ps1" -Root "$root" -Name "$name" -Step "$s" -ArgsFile "$af"
    else
      powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$root\\Farm\\_farm\\step.ps1" -Root "$root" -Name "$name" -Step "$s"
    fi
    code=$?
  else
    ssh "$host" "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $root\\Farm\\_farm\\step.ps1 -Root $root -Name $name -Step $s ${af:+-ArgsFile $af}"
    code=$?
  fi
  rm -rf "${logs:?}/$s"
  pull "$host" "$(fwd "$root")/Farm/_out/$name/$s" "$logs" || echo "FARM could not fetch the logs of $s" >&2
  exit $code
}

I have not checked whether any perk changes enemy health; do not write \"always\" in a way a perk could contradict, \"one shot\" as the base rule is safe.\n\n(2) Yes, a scripted capture can do it, with these facts:\n- Resolution: the run wrapper takes -ResX 1920 -ResY 1080, and its picture output (-Shots) is real rendered frames. Frames come from a fixed-step run, so a GIF cut from them plays at the true speed whatever the capture PC's frame rate.\n- Staging: rooms are plain text files, so a staged room (a Grunt, a Rusher and a Marksman placed staggered in front of the start) needs no compile. Three such picture rooms exist already from the effects lanes (tests/vfx2_hang for hanging bullets, tests/vfx2_grunts, tests/vfx2_marksmen), so this is known ground.\n- \"Held still until the clap\": I know of no hold switch. The simple way that needs none: the script claps in the first tenth of a second, so the three are frozen in their opening pose before they act, then fires one shot at each (the bullets hang), then the freeze ends and all three fall. If the owner wants them visibly standing for a beat before the clap, that needs a look at the room file's enemy options, which the capture lane does first.\n- \"From the final build\": the staged room file is not in the entry folder (the entry keeps only rooms a real run uses), so the capture plays a copy of the same final package with the one room file added. Same exe, same content, one extra text file. Say on the page nothing that implies the staged room is a level in the game.\n- The stills (freeze beginning, bullets hanging, a figure falling) and the cover pair (one camera spot, normal and frozen, clapperboard raised) come from the same run as chosen frames. For the cover pair the script has to hold the camera still across the clap; that is a script line, not a code change.\n- Where and when: on the second machine, after the final build is zipped, by a picture lane I start. One run slot there, so plan one run with all shots in it. Send the shot list with frame times relative to the clap (for example \"0.10 s after the clap\") and I will brief the lane from it.\n- Honest limits: no sound in the GIF source, UI is in the frames unless the list says to hide it (a hide-UI option exists for picture runs in Development builds only, and this capture can use the Development package of the same commit if the HUD must be off; say which you want)."
}
```

**What I checked in the frames**
- **S1, S2, S3:** S2 at C1 + 3.5 shows all three enemies frozen, each with its bullet hanging in front of it, well inside the frame. In S3 all three fall when the freeze ends.
- **Clean frames:** no black or half-drawn frame, no debug text, no enemy cut by the edge in S2. I saw no floating or sunk props.
- **Camera still before C2:** I compared frames from C2 - 1.5 to C2 - 0.017 pixel by pixel. The picture moves less than 0.005 px. The pixels that differ are object edges (anti-aliasing noise) and the gun's idle sway, which moves the gun only.

**How this differs from the shot list**
1. **No beat before the clap.** The room file has no option that holds an enemy still. Grunt and Rusher take only position, facing and home area; the Marksman only position and facing. So the clap is pressed at 0.10 s, and tight homes keep the Grunt and Rusher in place. No game code changed.
2. **The GIF and S1 start at the run's start**, because C1 is only 0.1 s in. GIF frames begin at C1 - 0.067 and S1 at C1 - 0.05.
3. **No cover frame before C2 shows the clapperboard.** The freeze starts on the press frame, and the board first appears on that same frame. The frames with the board up while the scene still has normal colours are C2 + 0.00 to + 0.15. The sketch is complete by about C2 + 0.4. [taste: owner review]
4. **The view nods 1.5° for 0.18 s at C2.** This is the game's clap kick. By eye on the cover sheet, frames from C2 + 0.2 on line up with the frames before C2. The sketch frames defeat a pixel measure, so this is not measured.
5. **Turns between shots are smooth.** The script has no smooth-turn command, so each turn is one eased look line per frame. Shots land at C1 + 0.5, + 1.4 and + 2.3 s.
6. **Other things in the frames:** the Marksman's red aim line is in every Phase A frame, and the dead enemies break into blocks. The cover view is a corner of gear to the right of the start. [taste: owner review]

**Times (run seconds = script clock, fixed 60 fps)**

- C2 = 9.600 s (frame 576): `FREEZE begin #2` is on frame 576.

#!/bin/bash
# Sends the build in the owner's play folder to [pc-b]'s C:\SupercutPlaytest (keeps Play.bat and logs there) and opens it
# on [pc-b]'s desktop. Skips the swap if a Supercut process is running there.
SRC="D:/UE/Builds/Supercut59_play"
TAR="D:/UE/Builds/_[pc-b]_play.tar"
pc=[pc-b]
[ -f "$SRC/Supercut.exe" ] || { echo "no package at $SRC"; exit 1; }
rm -f "$TAR"; tar --force-local --exclude=./Saved -cf "$TAR" -C "$SRC" . || exit 1
SUM=$(cksum < "$SRC/Supercut/Content/Paks/Supercut-Windows.ucas" | cut -d' ' -f2)
echo "local ucas bytes $SUM"
echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) $pc"
n=$(ssh -o ConnectTimeout=20 $pc 'tasklist | find /i /c "supercut"' 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')
[ -n "$n" ] || { echo "STOP: no answer over ssh"; exit 1; }
[ "$n" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: game running ($n)"; exit 1; }
ssh $pc 'cmd /c "(if exist C:\SupercutPlaytest_new rmdir /s /q C:\SupercutPlaytest_new) & mkdir C:\SupercutPlaytest_new"' 2>/dev/null || exit 1
scp -q "$TAR" "$pc:C:/SupercutPlaytest_new/play.tar" 2>/dev/null || { echo "scp failed"; exit 1; }
ssh $pc 'cmd /c "cd /d C:\SupercutPlaytest_new && tar -xf play.tar && del play.tar"' 2>/dev/null || { echo "untar failed"; exit 1; }
n=$(ssh $pc 'tasklist | find /i /c "supercut"' 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')
[ "$n" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: game started meanwhile"; exit 1; }
ssh $pc 'robocopy C:\SupercutPlaytest_new C:\SupercutPlaytest /MIR /XF Play.bat /XD logs /NFL /NDL /NP /NJH' 2>/dev/null | grep 'Files :\|Bytes :'
ssh $pc 'cmd /c "rmdir /s /q C:\SupercutPlaytest_new & dir /b C:\SupercutPlaytest & for %I in (C:\SupercutPlaytest\Supercut\Content\Paks\Supercut-Windows.ucas) do @echo ucas bytes %~zI"' 2>/dev/null
rm -f "$TAR"
echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) open"
ssh $pc 'cmd /c "schtasks /create /tn SupercutPlayOnce /tr C:\SupercutPlaytest\Play.bat /sc once /st 23:59 /it /f && schtasks /run /tn SupercutPlayOnce"' 2>/dev/null
echo "DONE $(date +%H:%M)"
---
Engine
logs
Manifest_DebugFiles_Win64.txt
Manifest_NonUFSFiles_Win64.txt
Manifest_UFSFiles_Win64.txt
NOTICES.txt
Play.bat
Play_dev.bat
Play_dev_windowed.bat
Play_windowed.bat
Supercut
Supercut.exe
Tuning.example.txt
2
```

void USupercutRun::WrapForScript()
{
	if (Phase == ESupercutRunPhase::Playing || Phase == ESupercutRunPhase::Picking)
	{
		Offer.Reset();
		SetPhase(ESupercutRunPhase::Wrapped);
		SetPaused(true);
		USupercutAudio::Get(this).PlayWrap();
	}
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("RUN wrapped: takes %d, time %.1f s, shots %d, freezes %d, kills %d, scenes %d"), Take, Stats.Seconds, Stats.Shots, Stats.Freezes, Stats.Kills, ScenesCleared);
}

void USupercutRun::ReachGate()
{
	++ScenesCleared;
	Hero->Heal(FSupercutTuning::Get().GateHeal);
	USupercutAudio& Audio = USupercutAudio::Get(this);
	Audio.PlayFlat(TEXT("gate_reached"));

	if (!IsPickScene(GetScene()))
	{
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PICK none after scene %d"), GetScene());
		GoOn();
		return;
	}
	DealOffer({});
	if (Offer.Num() == 0)
	{
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PICK skipped: every upgrade is held"));
		GoOn();
		return;
	}

	TArray<FString> Names;
	for (const FName Key : Offer)
	{
		Names.Add(Key.ToString());
	}
	SetPhase(ESupercutRunPhase::Picking);
	SetPaused(true);
	Audio.PlayFlat(TEXT("ui_open"));
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PICK offered: %s"), *FString::Join(Names, TEXT(", ")));
}

bool USupercutRun::IsRestScene(int32 Scene)
{
	return Scene % FSupercutTuning::Get().RestEveryScenes == 0;
}

bool USupercutRun::IsPickScene(int32 Scene)
{
	return (Scene - 1) % FSupercutTuning::Get().PickEveryScenes == 0;
}

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "SupercutUiStyle.h"

/**
 * The loading card (UI_SPEC section 9) at run start and restart: a Chalk band across the top third with SCENE n and
 * TAKE n, a row of film holes along its bottom edge, and the first room below it, still, in the sketch look, inside
 * four corner brackets. It cuts in from black, holds, cuts to black, then the room starts. USupercutMenu times it.
 */
namespace SupercutLoadingCard
{
	/** The card is up this long [pick], then the screen is black this long [ref 9: 17 frames]. */
	constexpr float HoldSeconds = 1.5f;
	constexpr float BlackSeconds = 0.283f;
	constexpr float Seconds() { return HoldSeconds + BlackSeconds; }

	FBox2D Band(float W, float H);
	/** Where the scene title's left edge and centre line are, and its cap height. */
	FVector2D SceneAt(float W, float H);
	float SceneCap(float H);
	/** Where the take label's right edge and centre line are, and its cap height. */
	FVector2D TakeAt(float W, float H);
	float TakeCap(float H);
	/** The film holes along the band's bottom edge, left to right. */
	int32 HoleCount();
	FBox2D Hole(int32 Index, float W, float H);
	/** Corner bracket Corner (0 top left, 1 top right, 2 bottom right, 3 bottom left): its two arms. */
	FBox2D BracketAcross(int32 Corner, float W, float H);
	FBox2D BracketDown(int32 Corner, float W, float H);

	/** The card Since seconds after it cut in: the card up to HoldSeconds, black after. */

### Mon 16 Nov 02:40:30 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

Motion blur is already off by default, so nothing needs changing, and off is the right default.

**What I checked in the code of the current build**
- The setting starts as off, and "reset to defaults" also sets it to off.
- The engine's own default is switched off in the project config too.
- With the setting off, the camera's blur amount is 0.
- It stays available as a switch: MOTION BLUR under VIDEO, and again under ACCESSIBILITY.
- Your own saved settings on this PC also have it off. A judge starts with no saved settings, so they get the default.

**Why off is right for judges**
- In a first-person shooter, blur smears the picture on every fast turn, and most players turn it off first thing.
- This game's freeze look is drawn in fine pencil lines, which blur would soften more than a normal picture.
- It is one click away for anyone who wants it.

I have not looked at a frame taken during a fast turn, so "no blur on screen" rests on the code, not on a picture. If you saw blur while playing, tell me where and I will look at that moment.

#!/bin/bash
# Merge check of the main copy on a farm host through farm.sh's own queue (no load polling).
# mirror, build, test, package, hand-made run, generated run, fetch.
# Usage: merge_check_x.sh [host, default [pc-c]]
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
PC=${1:-[pc-c]}
# NAME and SRC may be set from outside: on c4 the mirror is a junction to SRC, so a check there must run on a
# pinned worktree (SRC=/d/UE/wt/maincheck NAME=maincheck2), never on the main copy, or no merge can land meanwhile.
NAME=${NAME:-maincheck}
SRC=${SRC:-/d/UE/Projects/Supercut59}
LOGS=/d/UE/main_farmlogs_$PC
# One check at a time. A stopped background task does not stop this script: stop it with kill <pid>.
LOCK="/d/UE/_merge_check_$PC.lock"
if ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then echo "LOCKED: a merge check of $PC is running, pid $(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)"; exit 91; fi
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid"
trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK"' EXIT
step() { echo "=== $(date +%H:%M) $*"; "$@"; local rc=$?; echo "=== exit $rc"; return $rc; }

echo "HEAD $(git -C "$SRC" log --oneline -1)"
step "$F" mirror $PC $NAME "$SRC" || exit 1
step "$F" build $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Jobs 8 || exit 2
step "$F" test $PC $NAME "$LOGS" || exit 3
grep -a "passed\|failed" "$LOGS/test/console.txt" | tail -3
step "$F" package $PC $NAME "$LOGS" || exit 4
echo "PACKAGED $(date +%H:%M)"
grep -a -c "Failed to compile Material" "$LOGS/package/package_run.log"
step "$F" run $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Packaged -Exe '{B}\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe' -Run main8 -Seed 1 -Script '{P}\Script\main8.txt' -FixedFps 240 -Silent -TimeoutSeconds 540
echo "run exit $?"
grep -a "RUN wrapped" "$LOGS/run/run.log"
grep -a -c "missing usage flag\|Failed to create compute pipeline" "$LOGS/run/run.log"
cp "$LOGS/run/run.log" "$LOGS/run_main8.log"
# SKIP_GEN=1: no generated run (from main 024e486 the s7 fight script is not a reference; a walk script replaces it later)
if [ -z "$SKIP_GEN" ]; then
step "$F" run $PC $NAME "$LOGS" -Packaged -Exe '{B}\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe' -Seed 6 -Script '{P}\Script\gen\s7.txt' -FixedFps 60 -Silent -TimeoutSeconds 540
grep -a "RUN wrapped" "$LOGS/run/run.log"
fi
step "$F" fetch $PC $NAME builds/Supercut59/Windows "D:/UE/Builds/_from_farm/main"
echo "DONE $(date +%H:%M)"

#!/bin/bash
# The judges' build on the main PC: editor build, Shipping package, entry folder, scripted run from the entry folder, zip.
# usage: c4_ship.sh <tag>      (tag names the log and output folders; the project is D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59 as it stands)
# The main PC is closed to farm steps by D:\UE\Farm\_locks\c4.closed. This script moves that file aside while it runs
# and puts it back when it ends, whatever the result.
TAG=$1
[ -n "$TAG" ] || { echo "usage: c4_ship.sh <tag>"; exit 64; }
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
P=/d/UE/Projects/Supercut59
LOGS=/d/UE/final_farmlogs_$TAG
OUT=/d/UE/Builds/entry_$TAG
PKG=/d/UE/Farm/_builds/final/Supercut59_ship/Windows
LOCK=/d/UE/Farm/_locks/c4.closed
HELD=/d/UE/Farm/_locks/c4.closed_held_by_final
LAD="$LOCALAPPDATA/Supercut"
t() { date "+%H:%M:%S"; }
restore() {
  [ -f "$HELD" ] && mv "$HELD" "$LOCK"
  if [ -d "$LAD.held_$TAG" ]; then rm -rf "$LAD"; mv "$LAD.held_$TAG" "$LAD"; echo "settings folder put back"; fi
}
trap restore EXIT
[ -e "$OUT" ] && { echo "$OUT exists already"; exit 1; }
echo "START $(t) tag $TAG commit $(git -C $P rev-parse --short HEAD) dirty $(git -C $P status --short -uno | wc -l)"
[ -f "$LOCK" ] && mv "$LOCK" "$HELD"
mkdir -p "$LOGS"

"$F" mirror c4 final $P || { echo "mirror FAILED"; exit 1; }
echo "BUILD $(t)"
"$F" build c4 final "$LOGS/build" -Jobs 8; c=$?; echo "build exit $c $(t)"; [ $c -eq 0 ] || exit 2
echo "PACKAGE $(t)"
"$F" package-shipping c4 final "$LOGS/package"; c=$?; echo "package-shipping exit $c $(t)"; [ $c -eq 0 ] || exit 3
L="$LOGS/package/package-shipping/package_ship_run.log"
echo "BUILD SUCCESSFUL $(grep -c 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL' "$L"); material faults $(grep -c -E 'missing usage flag|Failed to compile Material' "$L"); $(grep -a 'Packages Cooked:' "$L" | tail -n 1 | cut -c1-1
[ -f "$PKG/Supercut.exe" ] || { echo "no $PKG/Supercut.exe"; exit 3; }

void ASupercutCharacter::ShowTitleLook()
{
	bTitleLook = true;
	if (!HasActorBegunPlay())
	{
		return;   // BeginPlay calls this again once the sketch exists
	}
	// The title screen pauses the game, so Tick does not run there: the look is set here in full.
	SketchBlend = 1.f;
	Sketch->SetScalarParameterValue(TEXT("Blend"), 1.f);
	SketchValues->SetScalarParameterValue(TEXT("Blend"), 1.f);
	Sketch->SetScalarParameterValue(TEXT("SweepFront"), FSupercutClapMotion::FullSweepFront);
	SketchValues->SetScalarParameterValue(TEXT("SweepFront"), FSupercutClapMotion::FullSweepFront);
	StillFrame->bStill = true;
	Camera->AddOrUpdateBlendable(Sketch, 1.f);
	GunRoot->SetVisibility(false, true);
	ClapRoot->SetVisibility(false, true);
}

#!/bin/bash
# farm.sh: build, test, package and run a SUPERCUT project copy on a farm PC, driven from c4. Details: ../FARM.md.
#
#   farm.sh mirror  <host> <name> <project folder on c4>     copy the project to <root>\Farm\<name> (changed files only)
#   farm.sh build   <host> <name> <log folder> [build.ps1 args, e.g. -Target Supercut -Jobs 8]
#   farm.sh test    <host> <name> <log folder> [run_tests.ps1 args, e.g. -Filter Supercut.Rooms]
#   farm.sh package <host> <name> <log folder>               Tools\package.cmd   -> <root>\Farm\_builds\<name>\Supercut59
#   farm.sh package-shipping <host> <name> <log folder>      Tools\package_shipping.cmd -> ...\_builds\<name>\Supercut59_ship
#   farm.sh run     <host> <name> <log folder> [run_demo.ps1 args]   {P} = the mirror folder there, e.g. -Script {P}\Script\main8.txt
#   farm.sh fetch   <host> <name> <remote path> <local folder>   path in the mirror, or builds/... or out/...
#   farm.sh status  <host>
#   farm.sh slots                                             who holds or waits for which PC right now
#
# Each step brings its logs back to <log folder>/<step>/ and exits with the remote step's exit code.
# Logs that come back have the PC's user and computer names replaced by USER and PC.
#
# Hosts: [pc-b], pc2, [pc-c], pc4 over ssh, and c4 itself (15 Nov: the owner freed c4 for lanes). On c4 nothing is
# copied: "mirror" makes D:\UE\Farm\<name> a junction to the project folder, so the steps build in that folder.

## Game description `[taste: owner review]`

SUPERCUT is a first-person shooter set on a film set that fights back. You are the director. Snap your
clapperboard and the scene freezes: enemies, their shots and the machines stop where they are. Walk through the
frozen set, line up your shots (each one leaves the gun and hangs in the air), then let the scene roll and every
shot flies at once. Three snaps per room, four seconds each.

A run is one shooting day: a string of scenes, fights against wooden stand-in figures mixed with small puzzles
that need frozen time, like a wind machine you stop to slip past or marks that only show while the scene is
frozen. Between scenes you pick one of three upgrades. Die and it is "CUT!": the next take starts again from scene
one.

## How the theme is used (DIRECTOR'S CUT) `[taste: owner review]`

- Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5): all game code (C++), room files, tests,

# The HUD's icon pictures (lane hud2), from lane icons1's finals: 1024 square PNGs named by key, no alpha, light line
# art on black (the owner's black and white set, 15 Nov). The brightness becomes the alpha of a white picture, so the
# HUD draws it over its own dark plate, untinted on the cards, tinted on the clapperboard counter (chalk for a charge
# held, the same picture dimmed for one spent). clap_empty is not used: its board sits about 1 px off clap_full's at the
# counter's size, so a spend would jump; the spent state is clap_full dimmed in place.
#
#   python -I Art\ui_icons\make_icon_pngs.py <folder with [a shooter the owner likes]> [name ...]
#
# Writes Art\ui_icons\<name>.png, 256 square, for every name in NAMES, or only the names given (one new icon leaves the
# others untouched). Then import them with Tools\make_ui_icons.py (in the editor, headless).
# Needs Pillow. The source pictures are only read.

import os
import sys

from PIL import Image

NAMES = ["longtake", "extrareel", "doubleexposure", "stuntdouble", "quickchange", "throughline",

SIZE = 256

clap_full.png

make_icon_pngs.py

**Design.** The loop is a third looping source in `FSupercutMusicMixer`. The mixer already plays through pauses, follows the master and music volumes, stays silent with no device and under `-Silent`, and the tests can read and render it with no device. A plain sound asset would have needed its own pause handling and couldn't prove the seam frame by frame.

**One pointer in the brief was wrong.** The songs aren't imported into `.uasset` files. The game reads them as 16-bit WAVs from `Audio/music/wav`, and `Supercut.Build.cs` copies them into the package. The menu loop goes the same way, so there is no import step. A missing file stops the game with a Fatal error, like the songs.

**What changed**
- **`Audio/music/wav/mx_menu.wav`** (new): the loop converted to 16 bits with seeded dither, no gain change, every frame kept.
- **`convert_music.py`**: the menu loop has its own dither seed, and `convert_music.py menu` converts it alone, reading only `menu_loop_v1.wav`.
- **`SupercutMusic.h/.cpp`**: the menu track, its two constants, `MenuPlay`, `MenuFadeOut`, `IsMenuPlaying`, `GetMenuPosition`. The loop is mixed in `Render`, and `FSupercutMusicTracks::Get` reads the new file.
- **`SupercutAudio.h/.cpp`**: two new calls, `MusicMenuPlay` and `MusicMenuFadeOut`.
- **`Supercut.Build.cs`**: `mx_menu` added to the list of music files copied into the package.
- **`SupercutAudioTests.cpp`**: three tests and two includes.
- **`Script/menumusic1_title.txt`** (new): the title run script.
- **`SupercutMenu.cpp`**: three added lines, nothing in `Tick`, the drawing or the loading card:
  - last line of `USupercutMenu::ShowTitle`: `USupercutAudio::Get(this).MusicMenuPlay();`
  - in `Choose`, `case ERow::Start`, after `LeavingAt = RealNow();`: `USupercutAudio::Get(this).MusicMenuFadeOut();`
  - in `Choose`, `case ERow::QuitToTitle`, after `Open(ESupercutScreen::Title, 0, true);`: `USupercutAudio::Get(this).MusicMenuPlay();`

### Mon 16 Nov 04:18:32 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

Yes. The main menu backdrop is the first stage of the run you're about to play: a real 3D build of that run's scene 1, paused, drawn in the pencil-sketch look with the gun and clapperboard hidden.

- **Which room:** at launch the game picks one of the twelve generated runs by seed and builds that run's first room behind the menu (`SupercutRun.cpp:142`, the log line `TITLE backdrop: scene 1`).
- **What START does:** it unpauses and begins the same run with the same seed (`SupercutRun.cpp:149-155`), so you start in the room you were just looking at.
- **It varies:** a different launch can pick a different run, so the backdrop isn't always the same room.

That's also why the parallax is cheap: the backdrop is a real room, so its camera can move.

- **Hook:** `ASupercutPlayerController::PlayerTick`. It already runs every frame on the paused title.
- **Why it moves the character, not the camera:** the title pauses the world in its first frame, so the world clock stays at 0. At 0, `GetPlayerViewPoint` (PlayerController.cpp:1013-1026) skips the camera and draws from the title character's own position and turn. A camera offset changed nothing on screen (0 px), so the fix moves the title character instead. At zero offset it goes back to the stored still pose exactly.
- **Files and functions:**
  - `SupercutCharacter.h/.cpp`: namespace `SupercutTitleParallax` (the caps as constants, plus `CursorOffset`, `Ease`, `CameraOffset`, `Target`), `FollowTitleCursor`, `GetTitleParallax`.

  - `Script/parallax1_title.txt` and `Script/parallax1_still.txt`: the picture scripts.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

/**
 * Generated runs: runs of rooms made by the room generator in Tools/gen, baked into Content/Rooms/gen/s<seed> and
 * Content/Runs/gen_s<seed>.txt (Tools/gen/README.md). The game reads them as it reads any run list and room file.
 *
 * A start with no -SupercutRun and no -SupercutRoom plays one of them, picked by the run seed, while the tuning line
 * GeneratedRuns is above 0. GeneratedRuns is how many are baked: seeds 1 to GeneratedRuns, with no gap.
 */
namespace SupercutGeneratedRuns
{
	/** True when a start with this command line plays a generated run: GeneratedRuns above 0, and no run or room named. */
	bool PlaysGeneratedRun(const TCHAR* CommandLine, int32 GeneratedRuns);

	/** The generated run a seed plays: gen_s<1 + Seed % GeneratedRuns>, the seed read as unsigned. GeneratedRuns must be above 0. */
	FString RunName(int32 Seed, int32 GeneratedRuns);

	/** FNV-1a 32 of a catalogue file's bytes with each CR LF read as LF, as Tools/gen/sc_build.py hashes it. */
	uint32 CatalogueHash(const TArray<uint8>& FileBytes);

	/**
	 * The hash of the prop catalogue the game loaded: CatalogueHash of Content/Props/catalogue.txt, the file
	 * SupercutProps::Catalogue reads. Read once, after the loader has read the file.
	 */
	TOptional<uint32> LoadedCatalogueHash();

	/**
	 * A room made with props carries the line "# catalogue=<8 hex digits>": the hash of the catalogue it was made and
	 * checked with. With that line, Loaded must be the same hash. A room without it is not checked.
	 * A mismatch, a hash that does not read, or no catalogue loaded is a problem naming both: added to OutErrors as
	 * "<file>:<line>: catalogue: ..." in a Development build, logged as a warning in Shipping.
	 */
	void CheckCatalogueLine(const FString& File, const TArray<FString>& Lines, TOptional<uint32> Loaded, TArray<FString>& OutErrors);
}

{

	Offer.Reset();
	if (bFreshOffers)

		Random.Initialize(RunSeed);
		DropRandom.Initialize(RunSeed);
		RestRandom.Initialize(RunSeed);
	}

	Stats = FSupercutRunStats();
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("%s"), Why);
	StartTake();

### Mon 16 Nov 04:35:00 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

I answered the itch thread's fact check from the code. The short version, since it affects what the page can honestly say:

- **Not generated at play time.** The rooms are made ahead of time by our Python room generator, checked there, and baked into room files the game reads. What is random while playing is which baked run you get, the perk cards offered, the health drops and the rest rooms.
- **12 runs ship**, each of 12 rooms. The repo has 50 baked; the entry keeps 12.
- **The run is picked when the game is launched**, from the clock. It is not re-picked inside one launch: QUIT TO TITLE then START plays the same run again.
- **After a death** you replay the same rooms from scene 1. RESTART RUN replays the same run with the same card offers.
- **After a run's 12th room** the game rolls on into the next baked run, entered at its room 5, with enemies scaled up.

So I suggested the page say "levels built by our procedural generator: 12 runs of 12 rooms, one picked each time you launch", not "procedurally generated as you play".

One thing you may not expect: a player who never closes the game sees the same 12 rooms on every attempt. Re-picking the run on each return to the title would be a small change, but it also changes the menu backdrop room each time. Say if you want it; I haven't started it.

Waiting on my parallax check and the sign removal lane.

### Mon 16 Nov 04:37:25 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

**Re-picking the run inside one launch** is about an hour to a new zip, with one caveat.

- **The work:** on a death, on RESTART RUN and on QUIT TO TITLE, the game draws a new seed and loads that run's room list instead of reusing the one picked at launch. That is one place in the run code plus tests. Scripted starts keep their fixed run, so the reference runs don't change.
- **The time:** about 30 to 40 minutes for a lane, with the second machine's queue, then my check (11 minutes) and the Shipping zip (6 minutes).
- **The caveat:** scene 1 is the blade-tunnel lesson room in every run, so a player who dies still restarts in a blade tunnel. What changes is rooms 2 to 12 and the card offers. The menu backdrop after QUIT TO TITLE becomes the new run's scene 1, which is the same kind of room.

**Why only 12 of the 50 ship:** only those 12 are proven walkable end to end. Size isn't the reason; all 50 runs together are 6 MB.

- All 50 pass the generator's own checks (600 rooms, 0 problems).
- Runs 1 to 12 also each have a walk script: a bot walks the run from the start to the last gate in the real game, and all 12 completed. The pool was cut to "the 12 runs the play scripts prove" on 15 Nov for that reason.
- Runs 13 to 50 have never been walked by anything. If one has a room that can't be crossed, a judge who draws it is stuck.

**Shipping all 50** is a one-number change, but proving them means baking 38 more walk scripts and running each on the second machine. That is roughly 45 to 60 minutes of that machine's time, longer if some bots stall and need a look. The game needs seeds with no gap, so if run 20 failed we'd ship 1 to 19.

My recommendation: do the re-pick, since it's what makes a second attempt feel different, and it fits in the fourth zip with the sign removal. For the 50, I'd start the 38 walks in the background now and ship as many consecutive runs as pass by about 05:30, with 12 as the fallback. Both leave time for the trailer.

Say go on either or both and I'll start them at once.

# Lane video1: gameplay video pipeline for SUPERCUT

## The command

From c4, in Git Bash, in this folder (`unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/video1`):

```
bash tools/make_video.sh
```

It writes `out/draft1.mp4` and `out/draft1_sheet.jpg` and takes about 6 min. The first run after a new build takes
longer because it copies the package to pc2 (725 MB, 350 files, about 15 s). Options:

- `--build <folder>`: the package to record. Default `/d/UE/Builds/Supercut59/Windows`, the Development package of
  commit cf7dae4. It must be a Development (or Debug) package: see "Requirement not met" below.
- `--tag <name>`: the take's name under `logs/` and pc2's `out\`. Default `final`.
- `--name <name>`: the output file name. Default `draft1`.
- `--keep-raw`: keep the raw capture on pc2 (it is deleted at the end otherwise).

It stops at the first failure and says which step failed. Exit 0 means every check in `tools/check.py` passed.

## How it works

1. Checks c4 has python, ffmpeg, ffprobe, ssh, scp and tar, and that the game exe contains the `-SupercutRecord`
   switch (stored as UTF-16 text in the exe).
2. Copies the package to pc2 `C:\UE\SupercutVideo1\build`, without pdb files, when its file list (names, sizes,
   times) differs from the stamp left there by the last copy.
3. Copies `ffmpeg71.exe` (ffmpeg 7.1 from c4's imageio-ffmpeg package), `ffprobe.exe`, `take.ps1` and the settings
   file to pc2 `C:\UE\SupercutVideo1\tools`.
4. `scripts/build_take.py` writes the take script `scripts/take.txt`.

float ASupercutRoom::ExitDoorFrameBack()
{
	return RoomDoorWhiteBox.Min.X;

bool ASupercutRoom::IsInsideExitDoor(const FVector& EyeInDoorAxes)
{

		&& FMath::Abs(EyeInDoorAxes.Y) < RoomDoorWhiteBox.Max.Y
		&& EyeInDoorAxes.Z > 0.f;

This UE 5.9 MegaJam Preview is the first Unreal Engine release built primarily with agentic workflows. A handful of people directed fleets of agents to port the AI tooling from our UE6 development branch and implement Web as a target platform. Agents wrote the web platform code, starting from UE4’s retired HTML5 platform, with engineers directing, reviewing, and testing the work.

We’re using this release to learn how to build the engine with multiple people directing swarms of agents working in parallel… and we still have lots to learn. Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview Release Notes
=======================================

Overview of new and updated features in Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview.

On this page

_Last updated 11/9/26_

What's New
----------

Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview comes with significant improvements to Python scripting and the Unreal MCP, as well as improvements to AI-assisted workflows and machine learning.

This release introduces a new experimental feature called Unreal Canvas that provides a way to combine your development and iterative processes with agentic workflows and tools.

UE 5.9 also includes improvements in animation, rendering, world building, gameplay and much more.

Unreal Canvas
-------------

UE 5.9 introduces **Unreal Canvas**, a shared workspace where people and agents create and refine content using Unreal Engine and the other connected tools.

Its canvases include text, images, videos, and mesh generators that you drive with a prompt and a chosen generation service. Several companion plugins arrive with it:

*   **Unreal Canvas Bridge** exposes Movie Render Graph rendering to Canvas as MCP tools. This plugin requires the Model Context Protocol plugin.
    
*   **Unreal Canvas Spatial Annotations** places annotations in the 3D scene and captures the scene for use in Canvas.
    

You can learn more about these new features by reading our [documentation](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/unreal-canvas-overview-in-unreal-engine).

Python & MCP updates
--------------------

Python scripting receives several improvements, such as the ability to manage extra Python search paths. The old Python Foundation Packages plugin was removed. 

Scripting the editor also gets improvements with new Blueprint and Python libraries that let you edit Blueprints, chooser tables, StateTrees and Dataflow graphs from scripts.

Using Python with AI Agents
===========================

Learn how to use Python with AI agents in Unreal Editor through Unreal MCP, including running scripts and writing toolsets and agent skills.

![Using Python with AI Agents](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/45769dab-bd9d-446a-9279-a31d4ac0f875?resizing_type=fill&width=1920&height=335)

On this page

You can use Python to work with AI agents in the Unreal Editor in two ways. AI agents can run editor Python scripts to inspect and change your project, and you can write toolsets and agent skills in Python that extend what AI agents can do in the editor.

This page is for technical artists, pipeline engineers, and tools programmers who already script the editor in Python and want to make their scripts, tools, and workflows available to AI agents.

Prerequisites
-------------

Before you start, do the following:

*   Set up Unreal MCP and connect an AI agent to the editor. For more information, see [Unreal MCP](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/unreal-mcp-in-unreal-editor).
    
*   Enable the **Python Editor Script Plugin** for your project. For more information, see [Scripting the Unreal Editor Using Python](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/scripting-the-unreal-editor-using-python).
    

Running Python Through AI Agents
--------------------------------

With the `PythonScriptingTools` toolset in `EditorToolset`, an AI agent can run editor Python through the `execute_python` tool, which uses the Execute access mode. The `search_symbols`, `get_symbol`, and `grep_stubs` tools look up the Python API. The toolset's `read_me` tool is intended to be called once per conversation.

Scripts that run through `execute_python` work as follows:

*   All imports must be at the top level of the script, and star imports (`from module import *`) aren't allowed. `execute_python` checks the script before it runs and rejects it if it breaks either rule. The error names the line.

Unreal MCP
==========

Overview of using MCP-compatible workflows to drive editor functionality.

Learn to use this **Experimental** feature, but use caution when shipping with it.

On this page

Unreal MCP is **Experimental**. Many features are still under development and APIs and data formats may change at any time. Use caution when shipping a project with it.

**Unreal MCP** embeds a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server inside the Unreal Editor process so any MCP-compatible AI agent, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Visual Studio Code with GitHub Copilot, or the MCP Inspector, can control the editor over a local HTTP connection. The plugin exposes engine functionality as tools that an AI agent can call, such as spawning and editing actors, building Blueprints and Widget Blueprints, authoring materials, MetaSounds, PCG, Niagara, and Sequencer content, inspecting Slate widgets, profiling, and running automation tests. You can also add your own tools.

What Is the Model Context Protocol?
-----------------------------------

The **Model Context Protocol** (MCP) is an open specification published at [modelcontextprotocol.io](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). It defines how an AI client talks to an MCP server using a small set of JSON-RPC message types: initialize, tools/list, tools/call, and similar. An MCP server can offer three kinds of primitives:

*   **Tools** are named functions the client can call, with typed parameters and return values.
    
*   **Resources** are read-only data the client can fetch by a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI).
    
*   **Prompts** are reusable prompt templates.
    

**Unreal MCP** is an MCP server. It offers tools from toolsets registered with the Toolset Registry, supports Resources, and accepts connections from any MCP client. It doesn’t support Prompts.

### Fri 13 Nov 06:38:28 · Agent (claude-fable-5-2)

**Scope:** the forum post and release notes list 5.9 additions but never state a 5.8 baseline, so "new versus 5.8" is mostly not stated. The two doc pages are 5.9 docs and do not mark what is new.

**1. Python**
- Post: "expanded Python APIs covering audio, MetaSounds, modeling, physics, Niagara, materials, PCG, networking, and UI", and these "also extend to AI agents".
- Release notes: you can now manage extra Python search paths, and the Python Foundation Packages plugin is removed.
- Release notes: new Blueprint and Python libraries edit Blueprints (graphs, nodes, variables), chooser tables, StateTrees and Dataflow graphs.
- Docs: agents run Python via `execute_python` in the `PythonScriptingTools` toolset (in `EditorToolset`); lookup tools are `search_symbols`, `get_symbol`, `grep_stubs`.
- Docs: a script can call other tools with `await call_tool(name, **arguments)`.
- Docs: toolsets can be written in Python with `unreal.ToolsetDefinition`, `@toolset_registry.tool_call(mode=...)` and `Registration([...]).register()` from `init_unreal.py`.
- New module names: not stated.

**2. MCP, toolsets, Assistant, Lore, Fab**
- Post: Unreal MCP "launches automatically with the editor, delivers more reliable connections", with toolsets expanded to "rendering, source control, profiling, debugging, gameplay testing, geometry, audio, UI, and level creation".
- Lore: integrations let agents "manage project changes and automate source control workflows".
- Fab: "the new Fab toolset lets agents search the catalog, browse your library, and install free or purchased assets".
- Release notes: new Editor Preferences for port, allowed origins and highest protocol version, plus a project-level settings page, Semantic Search settings and a Knowledge Base.
- Release notes toolset areas: "Blueprints, editor actions, MVVM, Slate inspection, performance, files, scene capture, console, Texture Graph, widget animation".
- Release notes: "A Toolset Registry controls which toolsets agents may use", and an MCP Client toolset manages external MCP servers.
- Toolset and plugin names that appear: AllToolsets, EditorToolset, BlueprintToolsets, ConsoleToolset, LiveCodingToolset, GeometryToolset, GASToolsets (experimental, off by default). None is labelled new.
- Unreal Assistant: the panel runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode or custom ACP agents; it gains notification preferences and a tool-access setting (Ask, Read, Edit, Auto, Full).

**3. Known issues and warnings**
- About a week of development and "a shorter QA pass than usual"; previews are "not fully quality-tested"; Epic says to test on a copy of your project.
- Opening projects back in 5.8: not stated.
- UE-412135: in new projects the MCP server is on but the Toolset plugins are off, so `list_toolsets` offers no actor, level, asset, Blueprint or Python tools. Fix: enable All Toolsets in Edit > Plugins, restart, reconnect.
- UE-411502: Python Blueprint root swaps can crash the editor.
- UE-410941: undo after scripted Deformer Graph additions can crash.
- Packaging issues are all for the web (Wasm) target: UE-411774 (Launcher builds fail with trim profiles), UE-411525 (`-NoCleanStage` can ship stale content), and Mac/Linux Launcher builds lack some Wasm files.
- MCP doc limits: HTTP/SSE only (no stdio), loopback, no authentication, tool calls run one at a time.

**4. Install**
- Epic Games Launcher, GitHub (tag `5.9.0-preview-1`) or a Linux download. Size: not stated by Epic.
- Web target "currently requires a source build and C++ project".
- A user (not Epic) cites 200 GB to compile from source, and another says the Launcher lists it under "Other builds".

**5. Staff replies**
- The only Epic-looking reply is RaghibK's known-issues list (post 3); the page shows no staff badges.
- A user's report that Model Context Protocol is missing from Editor Preferences in 5.9 is unanswered.
